christianity_1_kings_8_22.context: Solomon, the son of King David, stands before the altar in the temple, representing the gathering of Israelites.

christianity_1_kings_8_23.meaning: The importance of acknowledging God's greatness, expressing gratitude for His promises, and committing to serve Him with all of our heart.
christianity_1_kings_8_23.context: Solomon addresses God, acknowledging His uniqueness, faithfulness to His covenant with David, and His care for their hearts.

christianity_1_kings_8_24.meaning: This verse encourages trust in God's promises and emphasizes the importance of gratitude for His blessings.
christianity_1_kings_8_24.context: Solomon is reminding God of His past faithfulness to His covenant with David, emphasizing the fulfillment of God's word.

christianity_1_kings_8_13.meaning: God acknowledges Solomon's dedication and hard work in building the temple. This promises hope and assurance to the people that their worship place will be a symbol of God's presence and protection. The verse emphasizes the importance of faithfulness and obedience in fulfilling God's will.
christianity_1_kings_8_13.context: This verse is from the Christian Old Testament, specifically in 1 Kings 8:13. It is spoken by God to King Solomon after Solomon has completed building the Temple in Jerusalem. In this context, God promises to make Solomon's temple a place where He will dwell among His people forever.

christianity_1_kings_8_14.meaning: The verse highlights Solomon's humility and gratitude towards God after completing the temple. It teaches us the importance of acknowledging God's blessings and showing appreciation to Him and others around us.
christianity_1_kings_8_14.context: This verse is from the Christian Old Testament, in the book of 1 Kings 8:14. It describes the scene where King Solomon, after dedicating the temple, turns around and blesses the gathered Israelites. This shows Solomon's humility and gratitude towards God.

christianity_1_kings_8_15.meaning: God reveals His choice of David as the king and emphasizes that the temple is built for His presence among His people. The verse teaches us the importance of trusting in God's decisions and recognizing His guidance in our lives.
christianity_1_kings_8_15.context: This verse is from the Christian Old Testament, in the book of 1 Kings 8:15. It is spoken by King Solomon, quoting God's words to him regarding the selection of David as the king and the purpose of the temple.

christianity_1_kings_8_16.meaning: King Solomon expresses gratitude towards God for His guidance and blessings in building the temple. The verse encourages us to be thankful for God's blessings and seek His guidance in our endeavors.
christianity_1_kings_8_16.context: This verse is from the Christian Old Testament, in the book of 1 Kings 8:16. It is spoken by King Solomon, reflecting on the dedication of the temple.

christianity_1_kings_8_17.meaning: David had good intentions to serve God, but God chose his son Solomon to fulfill the task, showing that God decides such matters.
christianity_1_kings_8_17.context: King David of Israel wanted to build a temple to honor God's name, but God told him that it was His will to do so.

christianity_1_kings_8_18.meaning: God appreciates when we have good intentions and desires to serve Him, but ultimately decides who will carry out His plans.
christianity_1_kings_8_18.context: God confirmed David's desire to build a temple for His name and appreciated his dedication.

christianity_1_kings_8_19.meaning: God chooses who will serve and fulfill His purposes, not humans trying to control everything.
christianity_1_kings_8_19.context: God tells David that his son Solomon will build the temple, not him, showing divine choice over human efforts.

christianity_1_kings_8_20.meaning: God has ultimate control and decides who will serve Him and accomplish His will.
christianity_1_kings_8_20.context: King Solomon builds the temple after being appointed by God, showing His sovereignty.

christianity_1_kings_8_33.meaning: When people face hardships, like losing battles, it reminds them of their mistakes. They turn to God, ask for forgiveness, and show their faithfulness. God responds by hearing their prayers and guiding them.
christianity_1_kings_8_33.context: This verse is from the Christian Bible, specifically in the book of 1 Kings, during the time of King Solomon. It talks about a situation where Israel, the people of God, are defeated by their enemies because of their sins. They repent, pray, and seek God's forgiveness in the temple (this house).

christianity_1_kings_8_34.meaning: When we pray and ask for forgiveness, God listens and helps us. It's essential to teach others the right path and seek rain for crops, showing God's blessings on our land.
christianity_1_kings_8_34.context: King Solomon continues to pray. He asks God to hear the prayers of Israel and forgive their sins, bringing them back to the land promised to their ancestors.

christianity_1_kings_8_35.meaning: When facing hardships like drought, we should turn to God, confess our sins, and seek His help. God responds by forgiving us and providing rain for crops.
christianity_1_kings_8_35.context: This verse is also from 1 Kings, where King Solomon continues his prayer. The people are experiencing drought because of their sins. They pray towards the temple, asking for God's guidance and forgiveness.

christianity_1_kings_8_36.meaning: When we pray and ask for forgiveness, God listens and helps us. It's important to teach others the right way and seek blessings from God, showing His love for us.
christianity_1_kings_8_36.context: King Solomon prays for Israel's well-being. He asks God to hear their prayers, forgive their sins, and guide them to the right path.

christianity_1_kings_8_29.meaning: Believe in God and keep praying, especially when worshipping in sacred places like temples. God will listen and guide in decisions.
christianity_1_kings_8_29.context: This verse is from the Christian Old Testament book of 1 Kings, during the time of King Solomon. It is spoken by the prophet Solomon, who is building the temple in Jerusalem. He prays for the eyes of God to be open to the temple, especially when prayers are offered.

christianity_1_kings_8_30.meaning: Trust in God as your heavenly home and listen to our prayers, especially when we pray towards sacred places like temples.
christianity_1_kings_8_30.context: Solomon continues his prayer, addressing God as the 'dwelling place' in heaven. He asks God to hear the prayers of his people when they pray towards the temple.

christianity_1_kings_8_31.meaning: If someone wrongs you, seek justice by swearing before sacred places like temples. God will judge and guide in decisions.
christianity_1_kings_8_31.context: This verse is about a situation where someone wrongs another and takes an oath. They come to the temple to swear before the altar. The verse is part of a prayer by Solomon.

christianity_1_kings_8_32.meaning: Trust in God to guide in decisions between good and bad people. God will punish the wicked and help the righteous.
christianity_1_kings_8_32.context: Solomon continues his prayer, asking God to judge between righteous and wicked people. God will bring the wicked's wrong deeds upon them and support the righteous.

christianity_1_kings_8_25.meaning: The verse emphasizes faith and trust in God, as King Solomon is asking God to keep His promise to David. It highlights the importance of obedience and following God's word for blessings and protection.
christianity_1_kings_8_25.context: This verse is from the book of 1 Kings in the Christian Bible. It is spoken by King Solomon, who is addressing God, asking Him to fulfill the promise given to his father, King David, regarding the continuation of the royal lineage and the preservation of the Israelite kingdom.

christianity_1_kings_8_26.meaning: The verse demonstrates humility and respect towards God, as King Solomon is seeking God's confirmation of His promise to David. It highlights the significance of trusting in God's word and keeping faith.
christianity_1_kings_8_26.context: This verse is also from the book of 1 Kings in the Christian Bible. King Solomon is speaking to God, asking Him to confirm the word He spoke to his father, King David, regarding the continuation of the royal lineage and the stability of the Israelite kingdom.

christianity_1_kings_8_27.meaning: The verse emphasizes the infinite nature of God and His transcendence over physical boundaries. King Solomon is seeking understanding of God's greatness and the limitations of human understanding when dealing with divine matters.
christianity_1_kings_8_27.context: This verse is also from the book of 1 Kings in the Christian Bible. King Solomon is addressing God, expressing his amazement at God's greatness and questioning if God can dwell on earth. He acknowledges that even heaven and the heavens cannot contain God's presence.

christianity_1_kings_8_28.meaning: The verse highlights the importance of prayer and supplication to God. King Solomon is appealing to God to listen to the requests and concerns of his people.
christianity_1_kings_8_28.context: This verse is also from the book of 1 Kings in the Christian Bible. King Solomon is talking to God, asking for His attention to the prayers and supplications of the people.

christianity_1_kings_8_45.meaning: God hears every honest plea and stands up for people who are treated unfairly by others.
christianity_1_kings_8_45.context: Solomon asks God to listen to prayers from the temple and help people who are wronged.

christianity_1_kings_8_46.meaning: We all fail sometimes, and facing hard consequences can happen when we ignore God's clear guidance.
christianity_1_kings_8_46.context: Solomon admits that everyone makes mistakes and God might punish them by letting enemies take them away.

christianity_1_kings_8_47.meaning: It is never too late to say sorry and change your ways, no matter where you are.
christianity_1_kings_8_47.context: Even in enemy lands, people can turn back to God and admit their wrong actions openly.

christianity_1_kings_8_48.meaning: True faith means keeping your heart connected to God and your home, even in hard times.
christianity_1_kings_8_48.context: Captives pray toward their home land and the temple, showing they still remember God's promise.

christianity_1_kings_8_41.meaning: God cares about everyone, not just one group. He welcomes all who seek him with a sincere heart.
christianity_1_kings_8_41.context: Solomon asks God to listen to people from other lands who travel far to worship.

christianity_1_kings_8_42.meaning: God's strength is known everywhere. People turn to him when they feel his mighty presence in their lives.
christianity_1_kings_8_42.context: People from far away hear about God's power and come to the temple to pray.

christianity_1_kings_8_43.meaning: When God answers prayers, it shows his love. This helps everyone on earth respect and know the true God.
christianity_1_kings_8_43.context: God hears prayers from heaven and answers them so all nations can learn his name.

christianity_1_kings_8_44.meaning: Praying toward the temple shows trust in God. He guides his people even when they face danger in battle.
christianity_1_kings_8_44.context: Israel goes to war and prays toward the city and temple where God chose to live.

christianity_1_kings_8_37.meaning: God cares about all our hard times, whether they come from nature or from other people.
christianity_1_kings_8_37.context: Solomon asks God to listen when bad things like hunger or war hit the people.

christianity_1_kings_8_38.meaning: You can always talk to God about your true feelings, even when you are very sad.
christianity_1_kings_8_38.context: People can pray to God at the temple when they feel deep pain in their hearts.

christianity_1_kings_8_39.meaning: God understands your true heart and will forgive you if you ask him with a sincere mind.
christianity_1_kings_8_39.context: God hears prayers from heaven and forgives people because he knows exactly what is in their hearts.

christianity_1_kings_8_40.meaning: Knowing God helps us live with respect and care for the world he has given us.
christianity_1_kings_8_40.context: The goal is for people to respect God while they live in the land he gave them.

christianity_1_kings_8_49.meaning: God hears every prayer and stands up for his people, making sure justice is done for them.
christianity_1_kings_8_49.context: Solomon asks God to listen to his people's prayers from heaven and help them win their cases.

christianity_1_kings_8_50.meaning: God forgives mistakes and can change the hearts of enemies to show mercy and kindness to his people.
christianity_1_kings_8_50.context: Solomon asks God to forgive sins and make enemy nations feel sorry for the captured Israelites.

christianity_1_kings_8_51.meaning: God chose his people and saved them from hard times, so he cares deeply about their well-being.
christianity_1_kings_8_51.context: Solomon reminds God that Israel is his special people, saved from slavery in Egypt long ago.

christianity_1_kings_8_52.meaning: God is always ready to hear and answer the cries of those who truly seek his help.
christianity_1_kings_8_52.context: Solomon asks God to always listen when his servant and the people cry out for help.

christianity_1_kings_8_53.meaning: God picked us out of the crowd to belong to Him, just like He did for ancient Israel.
christianity_1_kings_8_53.context: Solomon asks God to remember He chose Israel from all other nations to be His special people.

christianity_1_kings_8_54.meaning: We should finish our prayers with confidence, knowing God hears us and is ready to act.
christianity_1_kings_8_54.context: Solomon finishes his long prayer and stands up from kneeling before the altar with arms raised.

christianity_1_kings_8_55.meaning: We should share God's love and good news with others in a clear and joyful way.
christianity_1_kings_8_55.context: Solomon stands up and loudly blesses the whole group of Israelites gathered in the temple.

christianity_1_kings_8_56.meaning: God always keeps His word, so we can trust Him to do exactly what He said He would.
christianity_1_kings_8_56.context: Solomon praises God for keeping every promise He made to bring rest and safety to His people.

christianity_1_kings_8_57.meaning: We want God to always be near us and never abandon us in hard times.
christianity_1_kings_8_57.context: King Solomon asks God to stay close to his people just like before.

christianity_1_kings_8_58.meaning: We need God to help us follow his rules and live the right way.
christianity_1_kings_8_58.context: Solomon prays for God to guide the hearts of his people daily.

christianity_1_kings_8_59.meaning: God should always hear our needs and help us when we face daily problems.
christianity_1_kings_8_59.context: The king asks God to listen to his prayers every single day.

christianity_1_kings_8_60.meaning: Everyone should know that God is the only real power and there are no others.
christianity_1_kings_8_60.context: Solomon wants all nations to know that only one true God exists.

christianity_1_kings_9_3.meaning: God promises to watch over the temple and keep his name there forever with care.
christianity_1_kings_9_3.context: God speaks to King Solomon after the temple is finished and dedicated to him.

christianity_1_kings_9_4.meaning: You must follow God's rules with a true heart to keep your special relationship with him.
christianity_1_kings_9_4.context: God tells Solomon he must stay faithful and honest, just like his father David did.

christianity_1_kings_9_5.meaning: Staying faithful to God ensures your family and kingdom will last for many generations to come.
christianity_1_kings_9_5.context: God promises Solomon that his family will keep ruling Israel if they stay loyal to him.

christianity_1_kings_9_6.meaning: If you stop following God and worship false things, you will lose his protection and blessing.
christianity_1_kings_9_6.context: God warns Solomon that leaving him for other gods will break the promise he made.

christianity_1_kings_8_61.meaning: We should love God fully and obey his laws every single day without any doubt.
christianity_1_kings_8_61.context: Solomon asks the people to stay loyal and follow God's rules with a whole heart.

christianity_1_kings_8_62.meaning: We should come together as a group to show our thanks and respect to God.
christianity_1_kings_8_62.context: The king and the whole nation gathered together to give gifts to God at the temple.

christianity_1_kings_8_63.meaning: We should give our best to God and show that he is truly important to us.
christianity_1_kings_8_63.context: Solomon gave many animals as gifts to God to finish the special dedication of the temple.

christianity_1_kings_8_64.meaning: We must make room for God in our lives and be ready to serve him fully.
christianity_1_kings_8_64.context: The king set aside a special area outside the temple because the main altar was too small.

christianity_1_kings_8_65.meaning: We should take time to celebrate God's blessings together with joy and gratitude.
christianity_1_kings_8_65.context: Solomon hosted a huge celebration for the temple opening with people from all over Israel.

christianity_1_kings_8_66.meaning: When God is good to us, we should feel deep joy and thank Him sincerely.
christianity_1_kings_8_66.context: After the long feast, the people left happy and praised the king for God's kindness.

christianity_1_kings_9_1.meaning: God helps us finish important work when we stay focused and do our best.
christianity_1_kings_9_1.context: Solomon finished building the temple, his own palace, and everything else he wanted to build.

christianity_1_kings_9_2.meaning: God continues to talk to us and guide us even after we finish big tasks.
christianity_1_kings_9_2.context: God spoke to Solomon again after the temple was finished, just like before at Gibeon.

christianity_1_kings_9_15.meaning: God rewards faithful leadership with resources, and the king uses them to strengthen worship and protect the nation.
christianity_1_kings_9_15.context: King Solomon raised money to build the temple, his palace, and walls in Jerusalem and nearby cities.

christianity_1_kings_9_16.meaning: Powerful rulers can give or take lands, but true blessings come from God’s plans, not human gifts.
christianity_1_kings_9_16.context: Pharaoh captured Gezer, destroyed it, and gave the city to Solomon’s wife as a wedding gift.

christianity_1_kings_9_17.meaning: Investing in community projects shows how leadership builds lasting foundations for people’s well-being.
christianity_1_kings_9_17.context: Solomon constructed buildings in Gezer and Beth Horon, expanding his kingdom’s infrastructure.

christianity_1_kings_9_18.meaning: Even in remote areas, faith and community matter, reminding us that God cares for all people.
christianity_1_kings_9_18.context: Baalath and Tamar were places in the wilderness where people lived and worshiped.

christianity_1_kings_9_11.meaning: We should honor our agreements and pay back those who help us build our lives and dreams.
christianity_1_kings_9_11.context: Solomon repays King Hiram for building materials with twenty cities in the northern region of Galilee.

christianity_1_kings_9_12.meaning: Giving something of poor quality shows disrespect and fails to meet the true needs of others.
christianity_1_kings_9_12.context: Hiram travels to inspect the cities Solomon gave him and finds them lacking in quality or value.

christianity_1_kings_9_13.meaning: When we give poorly, it creates disappointment and leaves a lasting negative memory for everyone involved.
christianity_1_kings_9_13.context: Hiram complains about the bad gift and names the area Cabul, which means useless or worthless.

christianity_1_kings_9_14.meaning: True partnership continues even after disagreements, showing that business and friendship can survive minor conflicts.
christianity_1_kings_9_14.context: Despite the dispute over cities, Hiram still sends a large amount of gold to King Solomon.

christianity_1_kings_9_7.meaning: Disobeying God leads to serious consequences for everyone. We must stay faithful to avoid losing His blessing and protection in life.
christianity_1_kings_9_7.context: God warns Solomon that if the people sin, He will remove them from their land and reject the temple.

christianity_1_kings_9_8.meaning: When bad things happen, people often ask why. It reminds us that our actions have visible results for the whole community.
christianity_1_kings_9_8.context: People will look at the ruined temple and wonder why God allowed such destruction to happen to this holy place.

christianity_1_kings_9_9.meaning: Abandoning God for other things brings trouble. We must remember His help and stay loyal to Him always.
christianity_1_kings_9_9.context: The answer is that the people forgot God who saved them and started worshipping false gods instead of Him.

christianity_1_kings_9_10.meaning: Great work takes time and dedication. We should be patient and committed when building important things in our lives.
christianity_1_kings_9_10.context: Solomon spent twenty years building the temple for God and his own palace, completing these major construction projects.

christianity_1_kings_9_19.meaning: A king uses his wealth to create strong, organized cities and personal comforts for his rule.
christianity_1_kings_9_19.context: Solomon built many storage cities, chariot cities, horse cities, and pleasure buildings in Jerusalem, Lebanon, and his whole kingdom.

christianity_1_kings_9_20.meaning: These peoples stayed in the land, showing that not all were conquered or removed.
christianity_1_kings_9_20.context: The remaining Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites were not Israelites.

christianity_1_kings_9_21.meaning: The king used remaining enemies as laborers to support his projects and maintain power.
christianity_1_kings_9_21.context: The children left in the land were not fully destroyed, so Solomon kept them as servants.

christianity_1_kings_9_22.meaning: The Israelites were valued for their strength and leadership, not for forced labor.
christianity_1_kings_9_22.context: Israelites were not made servants; they served as soldiers, leaders, and commanders.

christianity_1_kings_9_23.meaning: Big tasks need good organization and clear leadership to keep everyone working together smoothly and efficiently.
christianity_1_kings_9_23.context: Solomon used many leaders to manage the large groups of workers building his projects.

christianity_1_kings_9_24.meaning: We should honor our guests and family by providing them with comfortable and safe places to live.
christianity_1_kings_9_24.context: Pharaohs daughter lived in a special house Solomon built for her in Jerusalem city.

christianity_1_kings_9_25.meaning: Regular worship and gratitude to God show that we value our relationship with him above all else.
christianity_1_kings_9_25.context: Solomon regularly offered sacrifices and incense to God at the temple he had just finished building.

christianity_1_kings_9_26.meaning: Using resources wisely allows us to expand our reach and connect with people from distant lands.
christianity_1_kings_9_26.context: Solomon built a fleet of ships at a port on the Red Sea coast.

christianity_1_kings_9_27.meaning: God gives skilled people to help others when they work together for a common goal.
christianity_1_kings_9_27.context: Hiram, king of Tyre, sent skilled sailors to help Solomon build his palace.

christianity_1_kings_9_28.meaning: Hard work and good trade bring resources that can build great things for everyone.
christianity_1_kings_9_28.context: The sailors went to Ophir, brought gold, and delivered it to Solomon for his palace.

christianity_1_kings_10_1.meaning: People learn from each other, and curiosity can lead to great discoveries and friendships.
christianity_1_kings_10_1.context: The queen of Sheba heard about Solomon’s wisdom and decided to visit him in Jerusalem.

christianity_1_kings_10_2.meaning: Sharing gifts and thoughts builds respect and shows that true wisdom is shared, not hidden.
christianity_1_kings_10_2.context: She brought a large caravan with spices, gold, and jewels, and spoke openly with Solomon.

christianity_1_kings_10_11.meaning: Rich trade shows how gifts can build great things for people and faith.
christianity_1_kings_10_11.context: Hiram's fleet brought gold, trees, and stones from Ophir to Solomon.

christianity_1_kings_10_12.meaning: Beautiful, rare materials help create lasting, meaningful art and worship.
christianity_1_kings_10_12.context: Solomon used the special trees to make pillars and musical instruments.

christianity_1_kings_10_13.meaning: Generosity and respect for others can lead to lasting friendships and peace.
christianity_1_kings_10_13.context: Solomon gave the queen of Sheba everything she wanted, then she left.

christianity_1_kings_10_14.meaning: Abundant wealth can support great projects, but it should be used wisely.
christianity_1_kings_10_14.context: Solomon received 666 talents of gold in one year.

christianity_1_kings_10_3.meaning: Honesty and wisdom are valuable traits. When we possess these qualities, people from different backgrounds will seek our guidance and knowledge.
christianity_1_kings_10_3.context: In the Bible, King Solomon was known for his wisdom. Queen Sheba, from a faraway land, heard about his wisdom and decided to visit him. She asked him many questions, and Solomon answered all of them truthfully.

christianity_1_kings_10_4.meaning: Appreciating and valuing wisdom and prosperity can lead to admiration and awe from others. However, true wisdom comes from a connection with God.
christianity_1_kings_10_4.context: Queen Sheba visited King Solomon and saw the magnificence of his palace, the servants, officials, and their attire. She was amazed by his wisdom and the splendor of his kingdom.

christianity_1_kings_10_5.meaning: A well-organized life and dedication to our responsibilities can create a harmonious environment. Seeing the beauty of a kingdom doesn't compare to the inner peace and connection with God.
christianity_1_kings_10_5.context: Queen Sheba observed the orderliness and dedication of Solomon's court, from the food, seating arrangements, and the officials' duties. She was overwhelmed by the grandeur of his kingdom.

christianity_1_kings_10_6.meaning: Trustworthiness and wisdom are essential qualities that can earn respect and admiration from others. Our words should reflect the truth and honor the wisdom of God.
christianity_1_kings_10_6.context: Queen Sheba expressed her admiration for the truthful reports she heard about King Solomon and his wisdom. She recognized the truthfulness of the reports and acknowledged his wisdom.

christianity_1_kings_10_7.meaning: Real life is often better than what people tell you, so you should see things yourself.
christianity_1_kings_10_7.context: The queen saw the palace and realized her reports were too small to describe it.

christianity_1_kings_10_8.meaning: People who stay close to wise leaders and listen carefully are truly happy and blessed.
christianity_1_kings_10_8.context: The queen praised the king's workers for their daily service and smart listening habits.

christianity_1_kings_10_9.meaning: God gives leaders power so they can treat everyone fairly and do what is right.
christianity_1_kings_10_9.context: The queen thanked God for choosing Solomon to rule Israel with love and care.

christianity_1_kings_10_10.meaning: Generous giving can be so big that it becomes a famous story for many years.
christianity_1_kings_10_10.context: The queen gave the king huge amounts of gold, spices, and gems as a gift.

christianity_1_kings_10_15.meaning: The king’s wealth shows how many people respected and valued his wisdom and power.
christianity_1_kings_10_15.context: King Solomon received gifts from traders, merchants, kings, and governors from many lands.

christianity_1_kings_10_16.meaning: His wealth allowed him to create luxurious armor, showing his great resources and artistic skill.
christianity_1_kings_10_16.context: Solomon made two hundred gold bucklers, each costing six hundred shekels of gold.

christianity_1_kings_10_17.meaning: The king’s riches were used to build beautiful, valuable items for protection and display.
christianity_1_kings_10_17.context: He also made three hundred gold shields, each costing three minas of gold, stored in Lebanon’s forest.

christianity_1_kings_10_18.meaning: The throne symbolizes his supreme authority and the lavish splendor of his reign.
christianity_1_kings_10_18.context: Solomon crafted a large ivory throne, covered with the finest gold.

christianity_1_kings_10_23.meaning: God gave Solomon great wealth and wisdom, showing that true greatness comes from God.
christianity_1_kings_10_23.context: King Solomon was richer and wiser than all other kings worldwide.

christianity_1_kings_10_24.meaning: Everyone wanted to learn from Solomon, proving that wisdom is valuable and sought after.
christianity_1_kings_10_24.context: People from all over the world came to hear Solomon’s wisdom.

christianity_1_kings_10_25.meaning: The gifts showed respect and admiration for Solomon’s wisdom and power.
christianity_1_kings_10_25.context: Each year, people sent gifts of silver, gold, clothes, armor, spices, horses, and mules.

christianity_1_kings_10_26.meaning: His strong army protected the kingdom and displayed his wealth and influence.
christianity_1_kings_10_26.context: Solomon had 1,400 chariots and 12,000 horsemen for his army and Jerusalem.

christianity_1_kings_10_19.meaning: The detailed design shows how powerful and wealthy Solomon was, making his rule look very impressive.
christianity_1_kings_10_19.context: This verse describes the physical look of King Solomon's royal throne in his palace.

christianity_1_kings_10_20.meaning: The unique and grand design proved that Solomon's kingdom was unlike any other place on earth.
christianity_1_kings_10_20.context: The text continues describing the lions carved on the steps leading up to the throne.

christianity_1_kings_10_21.meaning: Solomon had so much gold that he did not even bother using silver for anything.
christianity_1_kings_10_21.context: The writer explains that Solomon used only gold for his cups and palace items.

christianity_1_kings_10_22.meaning: Regular trade brought rare and valuable items, showing how connected and rich his kingdom was.
christianity_1_kings_10_22.context: Solomon shared a fleet of ships with Hiram to trade goods across the sea.

christianity_1_kings_10_27.meaning: Solomon's wealth was so great that silver and cedar trees were as common as everyday stones and trees.
christianity_1_kings_10_27.context: The king made silver as common as stones in Jerusalem, and cedars as common as the sycamore trees that are in the lowland.

christianity_1_kings_10_28.meaning: Solomon bought many horses from Egypt, and merchants sold them for a high price to many buyers.
christianity_1_kings_10_28.context: The horses which Solomon had were brought out of Egypt. The king’s merchants received them in droves, each drove at a price.

christianity_1_kings_10_29.meaning: Egypt sold chariots and horses to many kings, showing how much trade happened between nations.
christianity_1_kings_10_29.context: A chariot came up and went out of Egypt for six hundred shekels of silver, and a horse for one hundred fifty shekels; and so they exported them to all the kings of the Hittites, and to the kings of Syria.

christianity_1_kings_11_1.meaning: Solomon married many foreign women, which led him away from his faith and caused trouble for his kingdom.
christianity_1_kings_11_1.context: Now king Solomon loved many foreign women, together with the daughter of Pharaoh, women of the Moabites, Ammonites, Edomites, Sidonians, and Hittites.

christianity_1_kings_11_6.meaning: When we ignore God’s guidance, we lose His favor and make mistakes.
christianity_1_kings_11_6.context: Solomon chose bad ways and did not fully follow God like his father David did.

christianity_1_kings_11_7.meaning: Building places for other gods shows disrespect to God and invites trouble.
christianity_1_kings_11_7.context: Solomon built a shrine for the Moabite god Chemosh near Jerusalem.

christianity_1_kings_11_8.meaning: Allowing others’ beliefs to influence us can lead us away from God’s truth.
christianity_1_kings_11_8.context: Solomon’s foreign wives worshiped their own gods and offered sacrifices.

christianity_1_kings_11_9.meaning: A heart that forgets God’s promises brings anger and loss of blessings.
christianity_1_kings_11_9.context: God was upset because Solomon’s heart turned away from Him after two visits.

christianity_1_kings_11_2.meaning: Solomon ignored this clear warning and loved foreign women. This shows how ignoring wise advice can lead to serious spiritual trouble later.
christianity_1_kings_11_2.context: God warned Israel not to mix with foreign nations because their gods would lead people astray from the true path.

christianity_1_kings_11_3.meaning: Having too many bad influences can change your heart. We must choose our close relationships carefully to stay on the right path.
christianity_1_kings_11_3.context: Solomon had many wives and concubines from different lands. These women influenced his thoughts and actions in negative ways.

christianity_1_kings_11_4.meaning: Even wise people can lose their way if they do not stay faithful. We must keep our hearts pure until the end.
christianity_1_kings_11_4.context: In his old age, Solomon followed the gods of his wives. His devotion to God faded compared to his father David.

christianity_1_kings_11_5.meaning: Chasing after wrong things leads us away from truth. We should focus on what is good and holy in our lives.
christianity_1_kings_11_5.context: Solomon worshipped false gods like Ashtoreth and Milcom. He abandoned the one true God who had blessed him greatly.

christianity_1_kings_11_14.meaning: When leaders ignore God, trouble often comes from enemies who were once part of their own family or land.
christianity_1_kings_11_14.context: God sent Hadad to trouble Solomon because the king had turned away from following true faith and worship.

christianity_1_kings_11_15.meaning: Past violence creates deep hatred that lasts for generations, causing future conflicts between nations and families.
christianity_1_kings_11_15.context: David sent his army commander Joab to Edom to bury the dead soldiers after a major battle took place.

christianity_1_kings_11_16.meaning: Extreme cruelty leaves survivors with deep pain and a strong desire for revenge against the attackers.
christianity_1_kings_11_16.context: The army stayed in Edom for six months to kill every single male person living in that region.

christianity_1_kings_11_17.meaning: Running away to save your life is wise, but it can lead to new alliances against your home.
christianity_1_kings_11_17.context: Young Hadad escaped with some servants to Egypt to save his life from the violent army invasion.

christianity_1_kings_11_18.meaning: God can provide safety and resources for those who seek refuge, showing that help often comes from unexpected places.
christianity_1_kings_11_18.context: Hadad fled to Egypt where the king gave him a home, food, and land to live safely.

christianity_1_kings_11_19.meaning: Kindness and favor can lead to deep personal connections and blessings that improve your life situation significantly.
christianity_1_kings_11_19.context: Pharaoh liked Hadad so much that he gave him his own wife's sister as a new wife.

christianity_1_kings_11_20.meaning: Being accepted into a new community can bring your family into a place of honor and care.
christianity_1_kings_11_20.context: Hadad's wife had a son who was raised in the royal palace alongside the king's own children.

christianity_1_kings_11_21.meaning: When the time is right, you should seize the opportunity to return home and reclaim your rightful place.
christianity_1_kings_11_21.context: Hadad heard his enemies were dead, so he asked Pharaoh for permission to return to his homeland.

christianity_1_kings_11_10.meaning: Disobeying clear instructions leads to serious trouble. We must stay faithful to our promises and not follow wrong paths.
christianity_1_kings_11_10.context: Solomon broke God's clear rule by worshiping false gods instead of staying loyal to the one true God.

christianity_1_kings_11_11.meaning: Breaking trust has heavy costs. When we ignore sacred rules, we risk losing what we value most in life.
christianity_1_kings_11_11.context: God tells Solomon that his betrayal of their agreement means he will lose his kingdom to another leader soon.

christianity_1_kings_11_12.meaning: Mercy can delay consequences. Past loyalty and family history sometimes bring grace, but justice will eventually arrive.
christianity_1_kings_11_12.context: God delays the punishment until after Solomon dies because of his respect for Solomon's father David.

christianity_1_kings_11_13.meaning: Grace remains even in judgment. God keeps some blessings for faithful ancestors and chosen places despite our failures.
christianity_1_kings_11_13.context: God promises to keep one tribe for Solomon's son to honor David and the city of Jerusalem.

christianity_1_kings_11_26.meaning: Power can make people turn against their leaders when they feel wronged or seek their own glory.
christianity_1_kings_11_26.context: Jeroboam was a worker for King Solomon who decided to rebel and fight against his ruler.

christianity_1_kings_11_27.meaning: Unfair treatment and heavy burdens often create deep resentment that leads to conflict and rebellion later.
christianity_1_kings_11_27.context: Solomon forced Jeroboam to do hard labor on city walls which made the worker very angry.

christianity_1_kings_11_28.meaning: Hard work and talent can bring success but pride may still lead to dangerous choices.
christianity_1_kings_11_28.context: Jeroboam was strong and worked very hard so Solomon gave him a high job position.

christianity_1_kings_11_29.meaning: God often uses quiet private moments to deliver important messages that change the course of history.
christianity_1_kings_11_29.context: A prophet met Jeroboam alone in a field while wearing a new coat to speak.

christianity_1_kings_11_22.meaning: Sometimes people leave comfort to return home. It shows a desire for freedom and belonging in one's own land.
christianity_1_kings_11_22.context: Pharaoh asks Joab why he wants to leave Egypt. Joab says he has nothing else needed but wants to go home.

christianity_1_kings_11_23.meaning: God can raise up challenges to test leaders. It reminds us that power is temporary and requires humility always.
christianity_1_kings_11_23.context: God sends Rezon as an enemy to Solomon. Rezon fled from his master who was the king of Zobah.

christianity_1_kings_11_24.meaning: Hardship can build strong leaders. Rezon used his skills to create a new life and rule a city.
christianity_1_kings_11_24.context: Rezon gathered followers and became a leader. He moved to Damascus and established his own kingdom there.

christianity_1_kings_11_25.meaning: Enemies can persist for a long time. It shows how conflict affects nations and requires constant vigilance.
christianity_1_kings_11_25.context: Rezon fought against Israel during Solomon's reign. He hated Israel and ruled over Syria as a constant threat.

christianity_1_kings_11_30.meaning: This act shows that God will divide the nation. It is a clear sign of judgment for the king's disobedience.
christianity_1_kings_11_30.context: The prophet Ahijah tears his new robe into twelve pieces to show a coming split in the kingdom.

christianity_1_kings_11_31.meaning: God promises to give most of the kingdom to Jeroboam. This shows that power comes from God alone.
christianity_1_kings_11_31.context: Ahijah tells Jeroboam to take ten pieces, symbolizing the ten tribes that will leave Solomon's rule.

christianity_1_kings_11_32.meaning: God keeps his promises to David. Mercy remains for one tribe despite the king's many serious sins.
christianity_1_kings_11_32.context: One tribe remains with Solomon because of God's promise to David and the city of Jerusalem.

christianity_1_kings_11_33.meaning: Idolatry breaks our relationship with God. We must stay faithful and follow his ways always.
christianity_1_kings_11_33.context: The people turned away from God to worship false gods of neighboring nations like Sidon and Moab.

christianity_1_kings_11_42.meaning: Long reigns show stability but also remind us that earthly power is temporary and will eventually end.
christianity_1_kings_11_42.context: Solomon ruled over the united kingdom of Israel for a long period of forty years in Jerusalem.

christianity_1_kings_11_43.meaning: Life passes from one generation to the next, so we must prepare our hearts for change.
christianity_1_kings_11_43.context: Solomon died and was buried with his ancestors, while his son Rehoboam took over the throne.

christianity_1_kings_12_1.meaning: Leaders must face their people directly to accept responsibility and begin their service with humility.
christianity_1_kings_12_1.context: Rehoboam traveled to Shechem because the people gathered there to officially crown him as their new king.

christianity_1_kings_12_2.meaning: Running away from problems does not solve them, and past conflicts often resurface in new ways.
christianity_1_kings_12_2.context: Jeroboam heard the news while hiding in Egypt, having fled there to escape King Solomon's anger.

christianity_1_kings_11_38.meaning: When you obey God and do what is right, He will support you and give you a strong foundation.
christianity_1_kings_11_38.context: God promises to support Jeroboam if he stays faithful and follows the rules like David did.

christianity_1_kings_11_39.meaning: Even when we face hard times or consequences, God's discipline is temporary and meant to teach us.
christianity_1_kings_11_39.context: God says He will cause trouble for David's family line, but this punishment will not last forever.

christianity_1_kings_11_40.meaning: Sometimes we must flee from danger to survive, trusting that God will protect us in exile.
christianity_1_kings_11_40.context: Solomon tried to kill Jeroboam, so Jeroboam ran away to Egypt to stay safe until Solomon died.

christianity_1_kings_11_41.meaning: Not every detail is written here, but we can trust that history records the full story.
christianity_1_kings_11_41.context: The writer notes that more details about Solomon's life and wisdom are recorded in another book.

christianity_1_kings_11_34.meaning: God honors his promises to faithful people even when their descendants make bad choices and disobey his clear rules.
christianity_1_kings_11_34.context: God tells Jeroboam that Solomon keeps his throne because of the special promise made to David.

christianity_1_kings_11_35.meaning: Consequences for breaking trust are real and serious, showing that leadership requires faithfulness to God's laws.
christianity_1_kings_11_35.context: God says he will remove the kingdom from Solomon's son and give ten tribes to Jeroboam.

christianity_1_kings_11_36.meaning: God shows mercy by preserving a line of hope and worship for those who loved him deeply.
christianity_1_kings_11_36.context: God keeps one tribe for Solomon's son to maintain a light for David in Jerusalem.

christianity_1_kings_11_37.meaning: God can raise up new leaders to guide his people when old leaders fail their sacred duties.
christianity_1_kings_11_37.context: God promises Jeroboam that he will become king and rule over Israel as he wishes.

christianity_1_kings_12_11.meaning: Us about leaders who inherit responsibilities from their parents (fathers). They should not make life harder for their people by adding more burdens or using harsh punishments. Instead, they should lead with compassion and understanding, following the good examples of their predecessors.
christianity_1_kings_12_11.context: King Rehoboam is addressing the people after his father, King Solomon, passed away. His father had a heavy burden on the people, and now Rehoboam promises to add to that burden and punish them with painful scorpion stings instead of using whips.

christianity_1_kings_12_12.meaning: This verse shows the importance of listening to the people's concerns and meeting their expectations. Leaders should be approachable and responsive to their subjects' needs and requests.
christianity_1_kings_12_12.context: The verse describes a conversation between King Rehoboam and the people of Israel after they requested a meeting on the third day. Jeroboam and the other leaders had planned to meet with Rehoboam on the third day as well.

christianity_1_kings_12_13.meaning: Us about the importance of seeking wise counsel from experienced individuals. Leaders should not solely rely on the opinions of young or inexperienced advisors. Instead, they should gather advice from a diverse group of people to make well-informed decisions.
christianity_1_kings_12_13.context: King Rehoboam rejected the wise counsel from the older, experienced advisors and instead chose to listen to the younger, inexperienced advisors who advised a harsher approach.

christianity_1_kings_12_14.meaning: The importance of considering the advice of experienced individuals. Leaders should not only rely on the opinions of young or inexperienced advisors. Instead, they should seek advice from a diverse group of people to make wise decisions.
christianity_1_kings_12_14.context: King Rehoboam ignored the advice of the older, experienced advisors and chose to listen to the younger, inexperienced advisors who advised a harsher approach.

christianity_1_kings_12_3.meaning: Us the importance of communication and negotiation in resolving conflicts between leaders and their subjects. It highlights the need for empathy and understanding when addressing the concerns of those we lead.
christianity_1_kings_12_3.context:
This verse describes a situation where the leaders of Israel send messengers to Rehoboam, the son of King Solomon, to discuss their concerns about the kingdom's rule.
In the story, Jeroboam and the people of Israel approach Rehoboam to negotiate with him.

christianity_1_kings_12_4.meaning:
The significance of listening to the concerns of others and trying to alleviate their struggles.
It encourages leaders to balance authority with compassion for their subjects' well-being.
christianity_1_kings_12_4.context:
The people of Israel complain to Rehoboam about the heavy yoke of his father, King Solomon.
They request him to ease the burdens they face under the old king's rule.

christianity_1_kings_12_5.meaning:
Patience and giving others time to deliberate on important matters.
It highlights the importance of open communication and collective decision-making in leadership.
christianity_1_kings_12_5.context:
Rehoboam gives the people three days to think about their demands.
Afterward, they return and discuss their decision with Rehoboam.

christianity_1_kings_12_6.meaning:
The value of seeking wise counsel from experienced advisors.
It encourages leaders to rely on knowledgeable individuals for guidance and decision-making.
christianity_1_kings_12_6.context:
Rehoboam consults with the wise elders who advised Solomon during his reign.
They offer their guidance to help Rehoboam make a wise decision.

christianity_1_kings_12_7.meaning: Us the importance of listening to wise elders and considering their advice. By choosing to follow the counsel of young, inexperienced advisors, King Rehoboam made a wrong decision and lost the support of the northern tribes of Israel.
christianity_1_kings_12_7.context: In the Bible, this verse is from the book of 1 Kings 12:7. It narrates a conversation between King Rehoboam, the son of King Solomon, and his advisors. The people of Israel had requested a lighter yoke (burden) from King Rehoboam, as the yoke imposed by his father, King Solomon, was too heavy for them.

christianity_1_kings_12_8.meaning: The value of seeking wisdom from experienced individuals. By disregarding the older, wiser leaders, King Rehoboam made a mistake and lost the trust of the northern tribes of Israel.
christianity_1_kings_12_8.context: 1 Kings 12:8 (NIV) - King Rehoboam disregarded the advice of the older, wiser leaders and instead sought counsel from younger, less experienced advisors.

christianity_1_kings_12_9.meaning: Us about the importance of humility and seeking knowledge. King Rehoboam's response demonstrates his immaturity and lack of wisdom, leading to further division among the people of Israel.
christianity_1_kings_12_9.context: 1 Kings 12:9 (NIV) - King Rehoboam replies to the people's request for a lighter yoke by quoting his own size comparing himself to his father, King Solomon. This shows his inexperience and lack of understanding.

christianity_1_kings_12_10.meaning: Us about the consequences of making poor decisions. King Rehoboam's choice to disregard the advice of the older leaders caused division among the people, leading to the formation of two separate kingdoms: Israel in the north and Judah in the south.
christianity_1_kings_12_10.context: 1 Kings 12:10 (NIV) - The people of Israel rebelled against King Rehoboam and formed the Kingdom of Israel in the north, while Judah remained loyal to Rehoboam in the south.

christianity_1_kings_12_19.meaning: Israel's disobedience towards David's family remains a problem, showing the lasting consequences of their choice.
christianity_1_kings_12_19.context: This verse talks about Israel's rebellion against King David's lineage, which continues to this day.

christianity_1_kings_12_20.meaning: Israel's support shifted from David's family to Jeroboam, highlighting the importance of choosing righteous leaders.
christianity_1_kings_12_20.context: When Jeroboam returned, the people of Israel gathered to support him and only the tribe of Judah supported David's lineage.

christianity_1_kings_12_21.meaning: Conflict and force often lead to unnecessary suffering; seeking peaceful solutions is essential.
christianity_1_kings_12_21.context: Rehoboam tried to fight against the house of Israel with a large army, aiming to regain the kingdom for his son Rehoboam.

christianity_1_kings_12_22.meaning: God communicates with His messengers to guide people and maintain righteousness.
christianity_1_kings_12_22.context: The prophet Shemaiah received a divine message from God.

christianity_1_kings_12_15.meaning: Us to respect authority and follow divine guidance, as ignoring them can cause conflicts and negative consequences. God's word through prophets holds significance.
christianity_1_kings_12_15.context: King Rehoboam refuses to listen to the people's demands and God's prophet Ahijah foretells the kingdom's division. This leads to the people rebelling against Rehoboam.

christianity_1_kings_12_16.meaning: The verse highlights the importance of listening to people's concerns and prioritizing family responsibilities. Disobedience may provoke unrest and lead to secession.
christianity_1_kings_12_16.context: When Rehoboam doesn't respond to the people, they express discontent and urge him to focus on his own family. Israel declares independence.

christianity_1_kings_12_17.meaning: The significance of acknowledging one's responsibilities and focusing on a specific territory. Ignoring these responsibilities may result in further division and challenges.
christianity_1_kings_12_17.context: Rehoboam continues to rule over the tribe of Judah.

christianity_1_kings_12_18.meaning: Us the importance of protecting leaders and respecting their authority. When faced with danger, humility and seeking help are crucial.
christianity_1_kings_12_18.context: King Rehoboam tries to flee after being threatened by the people, but they stone him and he seeks refuge in his chariot.

christianity_1_kings_12_23.meaning: Us to follow divine guidance and avoid conflicts with our relatives or family members. God's word should be our ultimate authority.
christianity_1_kings_12_23.context: This verse is from the Christian Bible, specifically in the book of 1 Kings. It talks about a message given to Rehoboam, the son of King Solomon, and the people of Judah and Benjamin, along with other Israelites. The message is from God and instructs them not to fight against their relatives from the northern tribes of Israel.

christianity_1_kings_12_24.meaning: The importance of listening to and following God's word. It shows that obeying His guidance prevents conflicts and brings peace.
christianity_1_kings_12_24.context: Specifically in the book of 1 Kings, God speaks to the people of Israel through His prophet. He instructs them not to fight against their relatives from the northern tribes of Israel and asks them to return home. They obey God's message and follow His word.

christianity_1_kings_12_25.meaning: Jeroboam's actions and his aspiration to restore the kingdom to the house of David. It shows the importance of perseverance and determination in achieving one's goals.
christianity_1_kings_12_25.context: Verse 3 from the Christian Bible, in the book of 1 Kings, tells us about Jeroboam, who built Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim and lived there. Later, he built Penuel.

christianity_1_kings_12_26.meaning: This verse reveals Jeroboam's thoughts and plans. It teaches us the importance of believing in our abilities and having confidence in our ideas, even when others may not support us.
christianity_1_kings_12_26.context: In verse 4 from the Christian Bible, specifically in the book of 1 Kings, Jeroboam is thinking about restoring the kingdom to the house of David. He believes that the northern tribes should support him.

christianity_1_kings_12_31.meaning: He broke the rules by letting unqualified people lead worship, which showed his desire for control.
christianity_1_kings_12_31.context: King Jeroboam built new worship spots and picked regular people as priests to lead them.

christianity_1_kings_12_32.meaning: He created a fake religious event to keep people loyal to him instead of the true God.
christianity_1_kings_12_32.context: Jeroboam set up a new holiday in the eighth month to copy the real festival in Judah.

christianity_1_kings_12_33.meaning: He proudly led the people in wrong worship, showing how far he had strayed from truth.
christianity_1_kings_12_33.context: The king went to his new altar in Bethel to burn incense during his made up feast.

christianity_1_kings_13_1.meaning: God sent a messenger to confront the king directly, showing that no one can hide from truth.
christianity_1_kings_13_1.context: A prophet from Judah arrived in Bethel with a message from God while the king was praying.

christianity_1_kings_12_27.meaning: People often choose comfort and easy paths over truth, leading them to follow the wrong leaders.
christianity_1_kings_12_27.context: The northern tribes wanted to return to Jerusalem, which would make Rehoboam king again.

christianity_1_kings_12_28.meaning: Leaders sometimes create false shortcuts to keep power, tricking people into forgetting the true God.
christianity_1_kings_12_28.context: King Jeroboam made two gold calves to stop people from going to Jerusalem to worship.

christianity_1_kings_12_29.meaning: Bad ideas spread easily when they are placed in convenient spots for everyone to see and use.
christianity_1_kings_12_29.context: The king placed one gold calf in Bethel and the other in Dan for worship.

christianity_1_kings_12_30.meaning: Following easy false worship leads people away from God and into deep spiritual danger.
christianity_1_kings_12_30.context: The people traveled to Dan to worship the calf, which was a serious sin against God.

christianity_1_kings_13_2.meaning: God uses messengers to warn people before judgment comes so they have a chance to change.
christianity_1_kings_13_2.context: A prophet stands at a royal altar and warns that a future king will destroy it.

christianity_1_kings_13_3.meaning: True spiritual messages often come with clear proof so people know they are not lying.
christianity_1_kings_13_3.context: The prophet gives a clear sign to prove his message is true and from God.

christianity_1_kings_13_4.meaning: Trying to stop God's truth with force only leads to your own immediate punishment and shame.
christianity_1_kings_13_4.context: The angry king tries to grab the prophet, but his hand becomes stuck and cannot move.

christianity_1_kings_13_5.meaning: God's word always comes true, showing that his power is real and his promises are certain.
christianity_1_kings_13_5.context: The altar breaks apart and spills its ashes, exactly as the prophet had predicted earlier.

christianity_1_kings_13_10.meaning: It emphasizes the importance of adapting to situations and choosing better paths, showing flexibility in decision-making.
christianity_1_kings_13_10.context: The person avoided going back to Bethel after leaving there. This refers to making wise decisions and changing one's path when necessary.

christianity_1_kings_13_11.meaning: Open communication within families and sharing knowledge about righteous individuals and their deeds.
christianity_1_kings_13_11.context: An old prophet and his son discussed the miracles performed by the man of God in Bethel. The son informed his father about the man's actions and words.

christianity_1_kings_13_12.meaning: Asking for information and considering multiple perspectives before making choices.
christianity_1_kings_13_12.context: The sons of the old prophet asked about the direction the man of God went. They had seen him leave in the opposite direction.

christianity_1_kings_13_13.meaning: Following instructions, seeking assistance from family, and being open to using alternative means of transportation.
christianity_1_kings_13_13.context: The man instructed his sons to prepare a donkey for him. He then rode on it.

christianity_1_kings_13_6.meaning: The king's request shows his faith in prayer and the prophet's role as a mediator with God. The restored hand symbolizes spiritual healing and guidance.
christianity_1_kings_13_6.context: The verse narrates a situation where King Jeroboam II of Israel asks a prophet (man of God) to pray for the restoration of his hand, which was withered. Jeroboam II believes in the power of prayer and faith.

christianity_1_kings_13_7.meaning: The prophet prioritizes obeying God's word over personal gain, demonstrating faith and commitment to his calling.
christianity_1_kings_13_7.context: King Jeroboam II invites the prophet to his palace for rest and hospitality, offering a reward. The prophet chooses to trust in God's commandments over worldly benefits.

christianity_1_kings_13_8.meaning: The prophet adheres to divine instructions without personal preferences, showing unwavering faith and commitment to God's will.
christianity_1_kings_13_8.context: The prophet refuses King Jeroboam II's generous offer to stay at the palace and eat and drink. He follows God's instructions without questioning.

christianity_1_kings_13_9.meaning: The prophet follows God's instructions without questioning, demonstrating trust in divine guidance and obedience.
christianity_1_kings_13_9.context: The prophet receives a divine command from God not to eat, drink, or return the way he came. He trusts God's guidance.

christianity_1_kings_13_14.meaning: The king tries to identify the prophet to see if he can change the man's mind about his mission.
christianity_1_kings_13_14.context: The king finds the prophet sitting under a tree and asks if he is the man from Judah.

christianity_1_kings_13_15.meaning: The king uses a friendly offer of food to try and win the prophet's trust and cooperation.
christianity_1_kings_13_15.context: The king invites the prophet to come to his house and share a meal together.

christianity_1_kings_13_16.meaning: The prophet stays firm in his duty and does not let personal comfort or kindness change his obedience.
christianity_1_kings_13_16.context: The prophet refuses the king's kind invitation to eat and drink with him in that specific place.

christianity_1_kings_13_17.meaning: True faith means following God's clear instructions even when they seem hard or go against social norms.
christianity_1_kings_13_17.context: The prophet explains that God gave him a strict command not to eat, drink, or turn back.

christianity_1_kings_13_18.meaning: The prophet lies, showing that claiming divine authority without truth leads to deception and harm.
christianity_1_kings_13_18.context: A prophet claims to be a prophet too, and an angel tells him to bring a man home.

christianity_1_kings_13_19.meaning: He obeys the prophet’s instruction, but his actions will later be judged by God’s command.
christianity_1_kings_13_19.context: The man goes back, eats bread, and drinks water in the prophet’s house.

christianity_1_kings_13_20.meaning: God reminds the prophet of his duty to obey divine instructions, even when others are involved.
christianity_1_kings_13_20.context: While they eat, God’s message reaches the prophet who had brought the man.

christianity_1_kings_13_21.meaning: Disobedience to God’s words brings judgment, and warning is necessary to prevent further sin.
christianity_1_kings_13_21.context: The prophet warns the man from Judah that God is angry because he disobeyed the command.

christianity_1_kings_13_22.meaning: Disobeying God’s clear instructions can lead to serious consequences and loss of trust.
christianity_1_kings_13_22.context: A prophet was told not to eat or drink in a certain place, but he did.

christianity_1_kings_13_23.meaning: Even after breaking rules, people often try to act normal, forgetting the danger of their actions.
christianity_1_kings_13_23.context: After eating and drinking, the man saddled a donkey for the prophet he had rescued.

christianity_1_kings_13_24.meaning: Ignoring warnings can bring danger, and sometimes help or witnesses remain silent while tragedy occurs.
christianity_1_kings_13_24.context: A lion attacked the man, killing him, and the donkey stayed beside the body.

christianity_1_kings_13_25.meaning: Witnesses share news of bad events, reminding others to be careful and learn from mistakes.
christianity_1_kings_13_25.context: Other people saw the dead body and the lion, then reported it to the prophet’s town.

christianity_1_kings_13_26.meaning: God keeps His promises, even when they involve serious consequences for those who ignore His direct instructions.
christianity_1_kings_13_26.context: The old prophet learns the young man died for breaking God's clear command.

christianity_1_kings_13_27.meaning: We should be ready to act quickly when we need to help others or face a situation.
christianity_1_kings_13_27.context: The old prophet tells his sons to prepare the donkey for a quick journey.

christianity_1_kings_13_28.meaning: God can protect what He wants to keep safe, even in the middle of a tragic event.
christianity_1_kings_13_28.context: He finds the dead prophet, the donkey, and the lion standing calmly nearby.

christianity_1_kings_13_29.meaning: We should show deep respect and care for those who have passed away, even if they made mistakes.
christianity_1_kings_13_29.context: The old prophet carries the body back to his city to prepare for burial.

christianity_1_kings_14_4.meaning: Old age can limit vision, but people still seek help and guidance from wise elders.
christianity_1_kings_14_4.context: Jeroboam’s wife went to Shiloh to visit Ahijah, but he could not see because of age.

christianity_1_kings_14_5.meaning: Honesty matters; lying about identity can lead to trouble and miscommunication.
christianity_1_kings_14_5.context: God told Ahijah to warn Jeroboam’s wife about her sick son and her false identity.

christianity_1_kings_14_6.meaning: Truthful communication is important, especially when bad news must be shared.
christianity_1_kings_14_6.context: Ahijah greeted the wife, questioning her deception and warning her of bad news.

christianity_1_kings_14_7.meaning: God honors those who serve faithfully, reminding leaders of their responsibilities.
christianity_1_kings_14_7.context: Ahijah told the wife to inform Jeroboam that God praised him as Israel’s leader.

christianity_1_kings_13_34.meaning: A warning that disobedience can lead to a family’s downfall and loss of legacy.
christianity_1_kings_13_34.context: Jeroboam’s house was cursed, and the curse said it would be cut off and destroyed from the earth.

christianity_1_kings_14_1.meaning: Health problems can happen to anyone, even leaders, reminding us to care for our bodies.
christianity_1_kings_14_1.context: Abijah, son of Jeroboam, fell ill during his father’s reign in Israel.

christianity_1_kings_14_2.meaning: He sought guidance secretly, showing that leaders sometimes need help from wise advisors.
christianity_1_kings_14_2.context: Jeroboam asked his wife to hide her identity and go to Shiloh to meet prophet Ahijah.

christianity_1_kings_14_3.meaning: She was instructed to seek advice and support, illustrating the importance of asking for help.
christianity_1_kings_14_3.context: Jeroboam’s wife was told to bring food and ask the prophet about the child’s future.

christianity_1_kings_13_30.meaning: True respect for a holy person means giving them a proper and honorable resting place.
christianity_1_kings_13_30.context: The king of Judah placed the dead prophet in his own family burial place.

christianity_1_kings_13_31.meaning: We should honor those who spoke truth, even if we disagree with them in life.
christianity_1_kings_13_31.context: The king told his sons to bury him next to the prophet when he dies.

christianity_1_kings_13_32.meaning: God's warnings are serious and will happen if people refuse to change their bad ways.
christianity_1_kings_13_32.context: The king believed the prophet's warning about the altar would come true soon.

christianity_1_kings_13_33.meaning: Some leaders ignore clear warnings and keep doing wrong things because they want power.
christianity_1_kings_13_33.context: King Jeroboam kept making new priests for his false worship spots after the event.

christianity_1_kings_14_16.meaning: God warns that bad leaders bring trouble for the whole nation.
christianity_1_kings_14_16.context: Jeroboam's sins caused Israel to be punished by God.

christianity_1_kings_14_17.explanation:
Jeroboam’s wife returns home to Tirzah after visiting a prophet to seek healing for her sick son. Upon crossing her threshold, she discovers that the child has passed away as prophesied.

This verse illustrates the inevitability of divine judgment and the reality that human efforts cannot alter God’s sovereign decrees. It serves as a somber reminder that consequences for past actions often reach us exactly when we return home.
christianity_1_kings_14_17.meaning: This verse illustrates the inevitability of divine judgment and the reality that human efforts cannot alter God’s sovereign decrees. It serves as a somber reminder that consequences for past actions often reach us exactly when we return home.
christianity_1_kings_14_17.context: Jeroboam’s wife returns home to Tirzah after visiting a prophet to seek healing for her sick son. Upon crossing her threshold, she discovers that the child has passed away as prophesied.

christianity_1_kings_14_18.meaning: People should respect God's guidance even when it is difficult.
christianity_1_kings_14_18.context: Israel buried Jeroboam, following God's instruction through prophet Ahijah.

christianity_1_kings_14_19.explanation:
This passage serves as a concluding historical summary for King Jeroboam, the first ruler of the northern kingdom of Israel. It references official royal records that documented his military conflicts and political reign.

Life is fleeting, and our earthly achievements are eventually reduced to historical records. It encourages us to consider what legacy we are building, as our actions will ultimately be evaluated by a higher authority than human chronicles.
christianity_1_kings_14_19.meaning: Life is fleeting, and our earthly achievements are eventually reduced to historical records. It encourages us to consider what legacy we are building, as our actions will ultimately be evaluated by a higher authority than human chronicles.
christianity_1_kings_14_19.context: This passage serves as a concluding historical summary for King Jeroboam, the first ruler of the northern kingdom of Israel. It references official royal records that documented his military conflicts and political reign.

christianity_1_kings_14_8.meaning: You ignore God’s commands and fail to love Him, unlike David who obeyed and loved God wholeheartedly.
christianity_1_kings_14_8.context: God cuts the kingdom from David’s house and gives it to you, but you do not follow His ways.

christianity_1_kings_14_9.meaning: Your idolatry angers God, showing that turning to other gods brings His displeasure.
christianity_1_kings_14_9.context: You have done worse than earlier kings, making false gods and turning away from God.

christianity_1_kings_14_10.meaning: Those who oppose God will face complete destruction, like a man sweeping away everything.
christianity_1_kings_14_10.context: God warns that He will punish Jeroboam’s house, destroying all who defy Him in Israel.

christianity_1_kings_14_11.meaning: God’s judgment is harsh, showing that disobedience leads to ruin and suffering.
christianity_1_kings_14_11.context: Dogs will eat Jeroboam’s dead in the city, birds will eat those dead in the field, as God says.

christianity_1_kings_14_12.meaning: This shows that divine judgment is certain and immediate. We must respect the truth and accept the consequences of our actions.
christianity_1_kings_14_12.context: The prophet tells Jeroboams wife to return home. The child will die as soon as she enters the city gates.

christianity_1_kings_14_13.meaning: Even in a bad family, one good person stands out. Kindness toward God brings respect and a peaceful end to life.
christianity_1_kings_14_13.context: The child will be buried with honor. He is the only one in the family who showed kindness toward the true God.

christianity_1_kings_14_14.meaning: God actively removes those who lead people astray. Justice comes quickly for those who oppose divine will and truth.
christianity_1_kings_14_14.context: God promises to raise a new king soon. This new ruler will destroy Jeroboams family line completely and take their power away.

christianity_1_kings_14_15.meaning: Idolatry leads to chaos and loss of home. Staying faithful to God keeps us grounded and secure in our lives.
christianity_1_kings_14_15.context: God will shake Israel like a reed. He will scatter them from their land because they worshipped false idols and angered Him.

christianity_1_kings_14_28.meaning: We should protect what is precious and sacred in our lives by keeping it secure and safe.
christianity_1_kings_14_28.context: The king moved valuable items into the temple for safekeeping during times of danger or threat.

christianity_1_kings_14_29.meaning: We should seek out reliable sources to learn the full truth about history and people around us.
christianity_1_kings_14_29.context: The writer points readers to other historical records for more details about the kings actions and deeds.

christianity_1_kings_14_30.meaning: Constant fighting destroys peace and unity, so we should strive for harmony and resolve our differences.
christianity_1_kings_14_30.context: Two rival kings fought against each other constantly, creating a long period of conflict and division.

christianity_1_kings_14_31.meaning: Life continues through generations, reminding us that leadership and responsibility are passed down to the next.
christianity_1_kings_14_31.context: The king died and was buried with his ancestors, while his son took over the throne.

christianity_1_kings_14_24.meaning: When we copy bad habits from others, we break God's rules and bring trouble upon ourselves and our community.
christianity_1_kings_14_24.context: The people in the land practiced wrong acts just like the bad nations that God had removed earlier.

christianity_1_kings_14_25.meaning: Disobedience to God often leads to serious consequences, showing that ignoring spiritual truth invites danger and loss.
christianity_1_kings_14_25.context: Five years after Rehoboam became king, the powerful Egyptian ruler Shishak marched his army up to attack Jerusalem.

christianity_1_kings_14_26.meaning: Material wealth cannot protect us from the results of our sins, so we should value faith over gold.
christianity_1_kings_14_26.context: The enemy took all the gold treasures from the temple and the palace, including the special shields Solomon made.

christianity_1_kings_14_27.meaning: We must adapt to loss with humility, finding strength in simple solutions rather than relying on past glory.
christianity_1_kings_14_27.context: Rehoboam made new shields out of bronze to replace the stolen gold ones and gave them to guards.

christianity_1_kings_14_20.meaning: Leaders pass away and new ones rise, showing that human power is temporary and changes over time.
christianity_1_kings_14_20.context: Jeroboam ruled for twenty two years before he died and his son Nadab took the throne.

christianity_1_kings_14_21.meaning: God chose Jerusalem as his special place, reminding us that sacred spaces hold deep spiritual significance.
christianity_1_kings_14_21.context: Rehoboam became king of Judah at age forty one and ruled in Jerusalem for seventeen years.

christianity_1_kings_14_22.meaning: When we ignore God, we hurt our relationship with him and set a bad example for others.
christianity_1_kings_14_22.context: The people of Judah did evil things that made God jealous, sinning more than their ancestors had.

christianity_1_kings_14_23.meaning: We must avoid false worship and keep our hearts focused on the one true God alone.
christianity_1_kings_14_23.context: They built idols and worship poles on hills and under trees, ignoring God's clear commands.

christianity_1_kings_15_1.meaning: God allows leaders to rise at specific times in history to guide people through difficult political changes.
christianity_1_kings_15_1.context: Abijam starts ruling Judah during the eighteenth year of King Jeroboam's reign over the northern kingdom of Israel.

christianity_1_kings_15_2.meaning: Even short lives have a place in history and family connections shape who we become as leaders.
christianity_1_kings_15_2.context: Abijam rules for three short years in Jerusalem and his mother is named Maacah daughter of Abishalom.

christianity_1_kings_15_3.meaning: Following bad examples leads to spiritual failure while true faith requires a heart fully devoted to God.
christianity_1_kings_15_3.context: He copies his father's bad sins and lacks the wholehearted devotion to God that David his ancestor had.

christianity_1_kings_15_4.meaning: God's promises to faithful ancestors can protect future generations even when current leaders fail to follow Him.
christianity_1_kings_15_4.context: God keeps the royal line alive for David's sake by giving Abijam a successor to rule in Jerusalem.

christianity_1_kings_15_5.meaning: Even good people make mistakes, but staying faithful to God most of the time is what truly matters in life.
christianity_1_kings_15_5.context: David was a good king who followed God most of the time, but he made one big mistake with Uriah.

christianity_1_kings_15_6.meaning: Division and pride often lead to endless conflict, showing us how important unity and peace are for everyone.
christianity_1_kings_15_6.context: Rehoboam and Jeroboam fought constantly because the kingdom was split into two parts and they could not agree on anything.

christianity_1_kings_15_7.meaning: History records our actions, reminding us that our choices leave a lasting mark on the world around us.
christianity_1_kings_15_7.context: Abijam continued the fighting with Jeroboam, and his full story is recorded in other historical books for future generations to read.

christianity_1_kings_15_8.meaning: Life passes from one generation to the next, so we must prepare our children to lead with wisdom.
christianity_1_kings_15_8.context: Abijam died and was buried in Jerusalem, while his son Asa took over the throne to lead the people.

christianity_1_kings_15_9.meaning: God places leaders in specific times to guide His people with wisdom and care.
christianity_1_kings_15_9.context: King Asa started ruling Judah during the reign of King Jeroboam in Israel.

christianity_1_kings_15_10.meaning: Long service shows dedication to duty and family history shapes our personal identity.
christianity_1_kings_15_10.context: Asa ruled for forty one years in Jerusalem and his mother was named Maacah.

christianity_1_kings_15_11.meaning: We should follow good examples from the past to live a life that pleases God.
christianity_1_kings_15_11.context: Asa followed God faithfully just like his ancestor King David did in the past.

christianity_1_kings_15_12.meaning: We must remove bad habits and false beliefs to keep our hearts pure and clean.
christianity_1_kings_15_12.context: Asa removed immoral people and false idols from the land to honor the true God.

christianity_1_kings_15_13.meaning: We must remove harmful influences from our lives to stay faithful and keep our spiritual path clear.
christianity_1_kings_15_13.context: King Asa removed his mother from her royal role because she created a pagan idol for worship.

christianity_1_kings_15_14.meaning: God values sincere devotion over perfect actions, showing that a pure heart matters more than flawless religious rituals.
christianity_1_kings_15_14.context: Asa did not remove all local shrines, yet his heart remained fully devoted to God throughout his entire life.

christianity_1_kings_15_15.meaning: We should honor God by giving our best resources and treasures to support the community of faith.
christianity_1_kings_15_15.context: Asa brought silver, gold, and sacred utensils into the temple that his father and he had dedicated.

christianity_1_kings_15_16.meaning: Life often brings long conflicts, but we must remain steadfast in our duties despite ongoing challenges and opposition.
christianity_1_kings_15_16.context: King Asa fought against Baasha, the king of Israel, in a continuous war that lasted their whole lives.

christianity_1_kings_15_21.meaning: Sometimes we must change our plans when new information arrives. Flexibility allows us to adapt to changing circumstances and make better decisions for our future.
christianity_1_kings_15_21.context: King Baasha stopped his building project after hearing news. He moved his residence to the city of Tirzah instead.

christianity_1_kings_15_22.meaning: Community effort achieves great results when everyone participates. Working together allows a group to complete large tasks that would be impossible for one person alone.
christianity_1_kings_15_22.context: King Asa ordered all people in Judah to help. They moved stones and wood from Ramah to build new cities.

christianity_1_kings_15_23.meaning: Even strong leaders face physical decline and illness as they age. Our history remains important, but our bodies eventually weaken and require care during later years.
christianity_1_kings_15_23.context: The text notes Asa's deeds are recorded in history books. It mentions he suffered from a foot disease in his old age.
