christianity_psalms_144_13.context: The writer talks about having enough food and animals for the whole family.

christianity_psalms_144_14.meaning: Peace and safety allow people to work and live without worry.
christianity_psalms_144_14.context: The land is safe, and people work hard without fear of thieves.

christianity_psalms_144_15.meaning: Real happiness comes from knowing God is on your side.
christianity_psalms_144_15.context: David concludes that having God as your protector makes life truly happy.

christianity_psalms_145_14.meaning: When you feel crushed by life, God lifts you up and gives you the strength to keep going.
christianity_psalms_145_14.context: God helps people who are weak or struggling to stand back up on their feet.

christianity_psalms_145_15.meaning: God feeds everyone at the right time, so you can trust that your needs will be met.
christianity_psalms_145_15.context: All creatures look to God for their daily needs and wait for him to provide.

christianity_psalms_145_16.meaning: God is generous and fills the hearts of all living things with what they truly need.
christianity_psalms_145_16.context: God freely gives food and resources to every living creature that exists on the earth.

christianity_psalms_145_17.meaning: You can trust God because he is always right, fair, and shows kindness in all his actions.
christianity_psalms_145_17.context: The psalmist declares that God is always fair, kind, and does everything with perfect love.

christianity_psalms_145_10.meaning: All of creation should honor God because he is the source of all good things.
christianity_psalms_145_10.context: The psalmist says that everything God made will praise him and show his goodness.

christianity_psalms_145_11.meaning: Believers should tell others about God's strength so everyone can see his great power.
christianity_psalms_145_11.context: God's holy people will share stories about how powerful and glorious his rule really is.

christianity_psalms_145_12.meaning: We should share God's amazing acts so others can understand his true greatness.
christianity_psalms_145_12.context: God wants people to learn about his mighty deeds and the splendor of his royal rule.

christianity_psalms_145_13.meaning: God is always true and loving, so we can trust him completely in every situation.
christianity_psalms_145_13.context: God's rule lasts forever, and he always keeps his promises and acts with deep love.

christianity_psalms_145_18.meaning: You can trust that God hears your prayers when you speak to him with sincerity and truth.
christianity_psalms_145_18.context: God is close to people who pray to him with honest hearts and true faith.

christianity_psalms_145_19.meaning: If you respect God and ask for help, he will hear you and save you from trouble.
christianity_psalms_145_19.context: God listens to the cries of people who respect him and want to follow his ways.

christianity_psalms_145_20.meaning: Loving God keeps you safe, while those who do evil will face judgment and destruction.
christianity_psalms_145_20.context: God protects those who love him deeply but will remove evil people from the world.

christianity_psalms_145_21.meaning: We should all praise God forever because his name is holy and deserves our constant thanks.
christianity_psalms_145_21.context: The psalmist promises to praise God loudly and asks all living things to join in.

christianity_psalms_146_5.meaning: Trusting in God brings happiness and peace. He is faithful and always there for His children.
christianity_psalms_146_5.context: This verse is from the Christian Psalms, written by the prophet David. It talks about trusting in God for help and relying on His faithfulness.

christianity_psalms_146_6.meaning: God created the world and takes care of everything in it. He remains faithful and just.
christianity_psalms_146_6.context: Psalm 146 is a praise song that highlights God's creation and attributes.

christianity_psalms_146_7.meaning: God defends the weak, feeds the hungry, and sets captives free. He values righteousness.
christianity_psalms_146_7.context: Psalm 146 continues with God's attributes, emphasizing His care for the oppressed and provision for those in need.

christianity_psalms_146_8.meaning: God helps the downtrodden, raises the fallen, and has a special love for the righteous.
christianity_psalms_146_8.context: Psalm 146 continues with more praise to God for His miraculous acts.

christianity_psalms_146_1.meaning: Psalm 146:1 teaches us to focus on praising and worshipping God, rather than relying on humans or material possessions. By doing so, we find true peace and fulfillment in life.
christianity_psalms_146_1.context: Psalms 146:1 is a verse from the Christian Bible, specifically the Old Testament book of Psalms. It is written by the psalmist David, who is expressing his gratitude and worship towards God, Yahweh.

christianity_psalms_146_2.meaning: This verse encourages us to dedicate our lives to praising and serving God, as it brings joy and a sense of purpose.
christianity_psalms_146_2.context: Psalms 146:2 is also from the book of Psalms, written by David. It emphasizes the psalmist's commitment to praise God throughout his lifetime.

christianity_psalms_146_3.meaning: Psalm 146:3 teaches us to rely on God and not trust in mortals, as they are mortal and cannot provide lasting help or security.
christianity_psalms_146_3.context: Psalms 146:3 is part of the Psalms written by David. It highlights the psalmist's warning against trusting in princes and humans, emphasizing their limitations.

christianity_psalms_146_4.meaning: Psalm 146:4 reminds us to acknowledge our mortality and focus on eternal values, rather than being deceived by worldly possessions or power.
christianity_psalms_146_4.context: Psalms 146:4 is also from the book of Psalms, written by David. It reminds us that humans are mortal and their lives are fleeting.

christianity_psalms_146_9.meaning: The verse teaches us about God's love and protection for all, especially those in need. It reminds us to be just and fair in our dealings with others. Yahweh corrects wrongdoers, showing His commitment to righteousness.
christianity_psalms_146_9.context: This verse is from the Christian Psalms, written by the prophet David. It speaks about the qualities of God, Yahweh, who takes care of foreigners, supports the fatherless and widows, and corrects the wicked. In the context of the Psalms, it highlights God's compassion and justice.

christianity_psalms_146_10.meaning: This verse encourages faith in God's unchanging nature and His eternal kingdom. It reminds us to trust in God's promises and plan for our lives.
christianity_psalms_146_10.context: Psalm 146:9 is part of the Psalms, where the author, David, praises God. This verse emphasizes that Yahweh will rule forever and that Zion, representing Jerusalem, is the eternal home of God's people. It highlights the eternal nature of God's kingdom.

christianity_psalms_147_1.meaning: This verse encourages us to express gratitude and joy towards God. It reminds us that praising God brings us peace and satisfaction.
christianity_psalms_147_1.context: Psalm 147:1 is from the Psalms, where David praises God. This verse starts with a declaration of praise to Yahweh, the God of Israel. It highlights the goodness of God and the pleasure in singing praises to Him.

christianity_psalms_147_2.meaning: God's sovereignty and His care for His people. It reminds us that God is in control and takes care of those who follow Him.
christianity_psalms_147_2.context: Psalm 147:2 is also from the Psalms by David. In this verse, David praises God for His abilities, including building up Jerusalem and gathering the outcasts of Israel. It highlights God's power and care for His people.

christianity_psalms_147_3.meaning: God fixes your broken feelings and helps you heal when you are in great pain.
christianity_psalms_147_3.context: This verse describes how God cares for people who are deeply sad or hurt inside.

christianity_psalms_147_4.meaning: God knows every single star by name, showing he pays close attention to all things.
christianity_psalms_147_4.context: The writer looks up at the night sky and sees how many stars there are.

christianity_psalms_147_5.meaning: God is incredibly powerful and smart, and his knowledge has no limit at all.
christianity_psalms_147_5.context: The psalmist praises God for being very strong and having endless knowledge and wisdom.

christianity_psalms_147_6.meaning: God helps the humble stand up, but he makes the wicked fall down to the ground.
christianity_psalms_147_6.context: This part talks about how God treats people who are humble versus those who do evil.

christianity_psalms_147_7.meaning: Psalms 147:7 teaches us to express gratitude and worship God through songs and music. It highlights the importance of recognizing His blessings and care for us.
christianity_psalms_147_7.context: Psalms 147:7 is a verse from the Christian Bible, specifically in the Old Testament book of Psalms. It speaks about singing praises to God with gratitude.

christianity_psalms_147_8.meaning: Psalms 147:8 emphasizes the majesty and strength of God, who controls the sky, rain, and provides for all living creatures.
christianity_psalms_147_8.context: Psalms 147:8 is part of the same Psalms chapter, describing God's control over nature and His power.

christianity_psalms_147_9.meaning: Psalms 147:9 highlights God's generosity and love for all living beings, taking care of even the smallest creatures like ravens.
christianity_psalms_147_9.context: Psalms 147:9 continues the description of God's care for nature, mentioning His provision for birds.

christianity_psalms_147_10.meaning: Psalms 147:10-11 teaches us that God values humility and does not favor human pride or material possessions like horses.
christianity_psalms_147_10.context: Psalms 147:10-11 describes God's preference for humility over human strength or horses.

christianity_psalms_147_11.meaning: We should show deep respect for God and trust his love because he truly enjoys being close to faithful people.
christianity_psalms_147_11.context: God loves people who respect him and trust in his gentle care and kindness every single day.

christianity_psalms_147_12.meaning: We should express our gratitude and joy to God openly because he deserves our highest praise and worship.
christianity_psalms_147_12.context: The people of Jerusalem are called to sing praises to their God who lives in their holy city.

christianity_psalms_147_13.meaning: God keeps us safe from harm and blesses our families so we can live with peace and security.
christianity_psalms_147_13.context: God protects the city gates and blesses the children living inside the walls with safety and care.

christianity_psalms_147_14.meaning: God gives us peace in our lives and provides all the basic needs we require to survive and thrive.
christianity_psalms_147_14.context: God brings peace to the land and provides plenty of good food for everyone to eat daily.

christianity_psalms_148_3.meaning: All creation should honor God because he made them. This shows that worship is for everything in the universe.
christianity_psalms_148_3.context: The psalmist calls upon celestial bodies like the sun, moon, and stars to join in worship.

christianity_psalms_148_4.meaning: Even the highest parts of creation must honor God. This teaches us that his authority reaches everywhere.
christianity_psalms_148_4.context: The writer invites the highest heavens and the waters above them to praise the Lord together.

christianity_psalms_148_5.meaning: We praise God because he created us. His word has power to bring life and order to all things.
christianity_psalms_148_5.context: Heavenly bodies praise God because he spoke and they came into existence by his direct command.

christianity_psalms_148_6.meaning: God's rules are permanent and reliable. We can trust his word because it stands firm forever.
christianity_psalms_148_6.context: God set the laws of nature forever and established rules that will never change or disappear.

christianity_psalms_147_15.meaning: Gods power is instant and total. We should trust that his plans move forward with speed and perfect timing for all.
christianity_psalms_147_15.context: God speaks his will to the whole world. His message travels fast and reaches every corner of the earth quickly.

christianity_psalms_147_16.meaning: Nature shows Gods gentle care. Even cold seasons have beauty and purpose, reminding us to appreciate his creative hand in life.
christianity_psalms_147_16.context: The psalmist describes winter weather. God creates soft snow that looks like wool and spreads frost like fine dust.

christianity_psalms_147_17.meaning: We are small compared to nature. This teaches humility and reminds us to respect the mighty forces God controls daily.
christianity_psalms_147_17.context: God throws hail stones down like small rocks. The cold is so intense that no human can resist its power.

christianity_psalms_147_18.meaning: God brings change and renewal. Just as winter turns to spring, he can bring hope and life to our difficult situations.
christianity_psalms_147_18.context: God speaks again to melt the ice. He sends warm winds that make the frozen rivers start flowing freely again.

christianity_psalms_147_19.meaning: God specifically communicates his teachings to the people he has chosen, Jacob (Israel), showing his care and connection with them.
christianity_psalms_147_19.context: This verse is from the Christian Bible, specifically in Psalms 147:19. It talks about God revealing his word, statutes, and ordinances to his chosen people, Jacob (Israel).

christianity_psalms_147_20.meaning: God has special guidelines for his chosen people, Israel, setting them apart from other nations.
christianity_psalms_147_20.context: Psalms 147:20 is part of a larger psalm praising God. This verse highlights that God has unique ordinances for his people, Israel, and they are the only nation blessed with this knowledge.

christianity_psalms_148_1.meaning: Let's join together and give glory to God from the heavens and in the highest places.
christianity_psalms_148_1.context: Psalms 148:1 is the first verse of a psalm that praises God and invites all to join in this praise.

christianity_psalms_148_2.meaning: Let's unite and give praise to God, including heavenly beings and armies.
christianity_psalms_148_2.context: Psalms 148:2 is the second verse of the same psalm. It encourages everyone, including angels and armies, to praise God.

christianity_psalms_148_11.meaning: Everyone, even powerful leaders, should honor God because He is the true King above all.
christianity_psalms_148_11.context: The psalm calls on rulers and leaders from every land to join in worship.

christianity_psalms_148_12.meaning: God wants everyone to praise Him, no matter how old or young you are.
christianity_psalms_148_12.context: The song invites people of every age, from babies to the elderly, to sing.

christianity_psalms_148_13.meaning: God is the most important being, and His greatness shines over all creation.
christianity_psalms_148_13.context: The psalm says God is higher than the sky and the whole world.

christianity_psalms_148_14.meaning: God supports His people, and they should praise Him for giving them strength.
christianity_psalms_148_14.context: God has helped His chosen people stand strong and feel proud again.

christianity_psalms_148_7.meaning: Every part of nature, even the deep sea, should show thanks to the Creator.
christianity_psalms_148_7.context: The psalm asks all living things in the ocean to join in praising God.

christianity_psalms_148_8.meaning: Natural forces follow God's plan and show that he controls the weather perfectly.
christianity_psalms_148_8.context: Weather events like storms and snow are listed as part of God's creation.

christianity_psalms_148_9.meaning: Even silent, strong parts of the earth reflect God's power and beauty daily.
christianity_psalms_148_9.context: Tall mountains and strong trees are named as things that should praise God.

christianity_psalms_148_10.meaning: Every living creature, big or small, belongs to God and should honor him.
christianity_psalms_148_10.context: All kinds of animals, from wild beasts to small birds, are included here.

christianity_psalms_149_1.meaning: We should express our gratitude to God with new and heartfelt songs in our community gatherings.
christianity_psalms_149_1.context: The psalmist calls believers to gather together and sing fresh songs of worship to God.

christianity_psalms_149_2.meaning: Gods chosen people should feel deep joy because of their relationship with their divine Creator and King.
christianity_psalms_149_2.context: Israel is invited to celebrate their Creator and the people of Zion to honor their King.

christianity_psalms_149_3.meaning: Physical expression and music are wonderful ways to show our love and admiration for the Lord.
christianity_psalms_149_3.context: Worshipers are encouraged to use dance and musical instruments like tambourines and harps to praise God.

christianity_psalms_149_4.meaning: God loves us and saves those who stay humble, showing that kindness comes to the lowly heart.
christianity_psalms_149_4.context: God delights in his people and rewards those who are humble by giving them salvation and protection.

christianity_psalms_149_9.meaning: Follow divine rules to show honor to God and bring praise to his name through righteous actions.
christianity_psalms_149_9.context: God commands his people to carry out justice as written in his holy laws for all believers.

christianity_psalms_150_1.meaning: Celebrate God everywhere for his powerful deeds and let your worship fill the whole world with joy.
christianity_psalms_150_1.context: The psalmist calls everyone to praise God in his holy temple and in the vast sky above.

christianity_psalms_150_2.meaning: Give thanks for God's mighty works and match your praise to his infinite greatness and loving power.
christianity_psalms_150_2.context: Worshippers are urged to honor God for his strong actions and his wonderful greatness that shines forth.

christianity_psalms_150_3.meaning: Use music and joy to express your love for God and celebrate his presence with happy sounds.
christianity_psalms_150_3.context: People use loud trumpets and stringed instruments like harps and lyres to make music for God.

christianity_psalms_150_4.meaning: Use all your talents and joy to honor God with music and dance today.
christianity_psalms_150_4.context: The psalmist lists musical instruments used to celebrate God in the temple worship service.

christianity_psalms_150_5.meaning: Make a loud noise of joy to show your deep love for God.
christianity_psalms_150_5.context: Loud cymbals are mentioned as the final instruments in this list of praise offerings.

christianity_psalms_150_6.meaning: Every living thing should thank God for the gift of life and breath.
christianity_psalms_150_6.context: The psalm ends by calling every living creature to join in the worship.

christianity_proverbs_1_1.meaning: Wisdom comes from listening to the teachings of those who know God well.
christianity_proverbs_1_1.context: This opening line introduces the book of Proverbs written by King Solomon of Israel.

christianity_psalms_149_5.meaning: True happiness comes from knowing God. Let your heart sing with gladness every single day.
christianity_psalms_149_5.context: Gods holy people feel deep joy and honor because they are close to Him and safe.

christianity_psalms_149_6.meaning: Praise God with your voice. Stand firm in truth and defend what is right and good.
christianity_psalms_149_6.context: Believers praise God loudly while holding a sword to show they are ready to fight.

christianity_psalms_149_7.meaning: Justice must happen. Wrongdoers will face consequences for their bad actions against others and God.
christianity_psalms_149_7.context: Gods people act against nations that do evil and punish those who harm the innocent.

christianity_psalms_149_8.meaning: No one is above the law. Evil leaders will be stopped and held accountable for their crimes.
christianity_psalms_149_8.context: Leaders who rule with evil are captured and bound tightly with strong iron chains.

christianity_proverbs_1_9.meaning: Following good advice makes you look noble and respected by others in your community and family life.
christianity_proverbs_1_9.context: Wisdom is described as beautiful jewelry that brings honor and dignity to the person who wears it daily.

christianity_proverbs_1_10.meaning: You must say no to peer pressure and never agree to join others in doing wrong or evil acts.
christianity_proverbs_1_10.context: A father warns his child to refuse invitations from bad friends who want to do harmful things.

christianity_proverbs_1_11.meaning: Evil people often try to trick you into hurting others who are harmless and deserve no harm at all.
christianity_proverbs_1_11.context: Bad friends invite the listener to hide and ambush innocent people who have done nothing wrong to them.

christianity_proverbs_1_12.meaning: Sinners view violence as a way to destroy others without mercy, treating life as something to be wasted.
christianity_proverbs_1_12.context: The sinners speak of destroying victims completely, comparing their violent plans to the grave swallowing people whole.

christianity_proverbs_1_4.meaning: It teaches that learning helps simple people become wise and guides young men to make smart choices every single day.
christianity_proverbs_1_4.context: This verse introduces the goal of the book, aiming to help young people gain wisdom and good judgment in life.

christianity_proverbs_1_5.meaning: It shows that smart people should keep learning to grow wiser and find better guidance for their lives and decisions.
christianity_proverbs_1_5.context: The text explains that even those who are already wise can learn more by listening to these teachings and advice.

christianity_proverbs_1_6.meaning: It encourages readers to study these stories and puzzles to understand deep truths and apply them to daily living.
christianity_proverbs_1_6.context: This part lists the types of wisdom literature included, such as proverbs, riddles, and sayings from wise men of old.

christianity_proverbs_1_8.meaning: It teaches that respecting parents and following their teachings helps children stay on the right path in life.
christianity_proverbs_1_8.context: A father speaks to his son, urging him to listen carefully to parental advice and not ignore their guidance.

christianity_proverbs_1_13.meaning: Do not be tempted by easy money or greed. Stealing brings trouble and destroys your character and peace.
christianity_proverbs_1_13.context: Bad friends invite the young man to steal money and fill their homes with stolen goods.

christianity_proverbs_1_14.meaning: Sharing in sin makes you guilty too. Do not join groups that plan to do wrong things together.
christianity_proverbs_1_14.context: The group suggests sharing all their stolen goods equally so everyone benefits from their criminal activities together.

christianity_proverbs_1_15.meaning: Stay far from people who lead you into trouble. Protect your life by avoiding their harmful paths.
christianity_proverbs_1_15.context: The wise father warns his son to stay away from these bad friends and their dangerous plans.

christianity_proverbs_1_16.meaning: Evil people act fast to harm others. Recognize their dangerous nature and refuse to follow their violent ways.
christianity_proverbs_1_16.context: These friends rush quickly to do bad things and are eager to hurt or kill innocent people.

christianity_proverbs_1_21.meaning: Truth is always available to those who are willing to stop and listen.
christianity_proverbs_1_21.context: Wisdom stands at busy city gates, calling out to everyone who passes by.

christianity_proverbs_1_22.meaning: Choosing not to learn is a bad habit that keeps you stuck in the dark.
christianity_proverbs_1_22.context: Wisdom asks why people keep choosing to stay ignorant and make fun of learning.

christianity_proverbs_1_24.meaning: If you ignore good advice, you miss the chance to fix your mistakes.
christianity_proverbs_1_24.context: Wisdom says she called out to people, but they ignored her completely.

christianity_proverbs_1_25.meaning: Pride makes you reject help, which leads to more problems in your life.
christianity_proverbs_1_25.context: People refused to listen to wise counsel and rejected any gentle correction.

christianity_proverbs_1_26.meaning: If you ignore wise words now, you will face hard times and feel foolish later.
christianity_proverbs_1_26.context: The wise teacher warns that ignoring good advice leads to trouble and pain later.

christianity_proverbs_1_27.meaning: Trouble can arrive quickly and without warning, catching you off guard when you are not ready.
christianity_proverbs_1_27.context: Bad luck hits hard and fast, like a sudden storm or a strong wind.

christianity_proverbs_1_28.meaning: Waiting until you are in deep trouble to ask for help means you will not get any.
christianity_proverbs_1_28.context: People who ignored help before will cry for it later, but it will be too late.

christianity_proverbs_1_29.meaning: Bad things happen when people refuse to learn right from wrong and ignore what is truly good.
christianity_proverbs_1_29.context: The reason for their bad luck is that they chose to ignore wisdom and God.

christianity_proverbs_1_17.meaning: Evil plans often look harmless at first, so you must stay alert to avoid getting hurt.
christianity_proverbs_1_17.context: A bird cannot see the hidden trap, so it flies right into the danger.

christianity_proverbs_1_18.meaning: When you try to harm others, you are really just digging your own grave and hurting yourself.
christianity_proverbs_1_18.context: The wicked people are actually setting traps that will end up killing them themselves.

christianity_proverbs_1_19.meaning: Chasing wealth without care can ruin your health, relationships, and peace of mind in the end.
christianity_proverbs_1_19.context: People who want money too badly will find that their greed destroys their own lives.

christianity_proverbs_1_20.meaning: Good advice is available to everyone, so you should listen carefully when it speaks to you.
christianity_proverbs_1_20.context: Wisdom is like a loud voice calling out to everyone in the busy public streets.

christianity_proverbs_1_30.meaning: When we refuse to listen, we miss chances to avoid danger and grow wiser.
christianity_proverbs_1_30.context: People ignored the wise man's advice and scorned his warnings.

christianity_proverbs_1_31.meaning: Doing harmful things brings bad results that we must face alone.
christianity_proverbs_1_31.context: They will suffer the consequences of their own bad choices.

christianity_proverbs_1_32.explanation:
This proverb is spoken by Wisdom personified, addressing humanity. It warns against the attitudes of the naive and those who reject moral guidance.

The core takeaway is that complacency, apathy, and ignoring wise counsel lead to personal ruin. Active self-improvement and mindfulness are essential to avoiding destructive life choices.
christianity_proverbs_1_32.meaning: The core takeaway is that complacency, apathy, and ignoring wise counsel lead to personal ruin. Active self-improvement and mindfulness are essential to avoiding destructive life choices.
christianity_proverbs_1_32.context: This proverb is spoken by Wisdom personified, addressing humanity. It warns against the attitudes of the naive and those who reject moral guidance.

christianity_proverbs_1_33.meaning: Listening to wise advice gives security, calm, and protection from danger.
christianity_proverbs_1_33.context: Those who follow the wise man's counsel will live safely and peacefully.

christianity_proverbs_2_8.meaning: Staying on good roads keeps you safe and helps others stay on right paths.
christianity_proverbs_2_8.context: A wise man keeps honest ways and protects his friends from wrong paths.

christianity_proverbs_2_11.meaning: Good judgment and knowledge protect you from danger and help you make wise choices.
christianity_proverbs_2_11.context: Being careful and smart will watch over you and keep you safe.

christianity_proverbs_2_13.meaning: Leaving right paths leads to trouble and bad decisions that hurt yourself and others.
christianity_proverbs_2_13.context: People who leave honest ways walk into dark, bad places.

christianity_proverbs_2_14.meaning: Finding joy in evil shows a heart that is far from good and harms everyone around.
christianity_proverbs_2_14.context: Some people enjoy doing bad things and love wickedness.

christianity_proverbs_2_1.meaning: If you listen and remember good advice, you will grow wiser and live better.
christianity_proverbs_2_1.context: A father urges his son to listen and keep wise teachings in his heart.

christianity_proverbs_2_3.meaning: Seek clarity and speak up; this helps you learn and make good choices.
christianity_proverbs_2_3.context: The father says to ask for insight and speak loudly for understanding.

christianity_proverbs_2_4.meaning: Look for wisdom with the same excitement as finding valuable treasures.
christianity_proverbs_2_4.context: He compares searching for wisdom to looking for precious silver or hidden treasure.

christianity_proverbs_2_5.meaning: When you learn, you will honor God and understand His ways.
christianity_proverbs_2_5.context: Finding wisdom brings knowledge of God and respect for Him.

christianity_proverbs_2_15.meaning: Living a dishonest life leads you away from truth and causes you to lose your way.
christianity_proverbs_2_15.context: This verse describes people who choose to live in a twisted and dishonest manner every day.

christianity_proverbs_2_16.meaning: Guard your heart against sweet lies that hide danger and lead you into serious trouble.
christianity_proverbs_2_16.context: Wisdom protects you from a woman who uses sweet lies to trick you into bad choices.

christianity_proverbs_2_17.meaning: Breaking your promises shows a lack of respect for commitments and damages trust deeply.
christianity_proverbs_2_17.context: She abandons the partner she promised to love and ignores the sacred vows she made.

christianity_proverbs_2_18.meaning: Bad choices create a path that ends in destruction and separates you from life.
christianity_proverbs_2_18.context: Her home is a place of danger that leads people toward death and spiritual ruin.

christianity_proverbs_2_19.meaning: Sinful choices trap you in darkness and prevent you from finding true life and happiness.
christianity_proverbs_2_19.context: This verse warns about the dangerous path of adultery and how it leads to death.

christianity_proverbs_2_21.meaning: Living with honesty and kindness ensures you have a stable and peaceful place to live.
christianity_proverbs_2_21.context: This verse promises that good people will stay safe and secure in the promised land.

christianity_proverbs_2_22.meaning: Bad behavior eventually leads to being cast out and losing your place in society.
christianity_proverbs_2_22.context: This verse states that evil people will be removed from the community and the land.

christianity_proverbs_3_1.meaning: Hold onto good advice in your heart so you can make wise choices every day.
christianity_proverbs_3_1.context: A father urges his son to remember his advice and keep the rules in mind.

christianity_proverbs_3_2.meaning: When you trust God fully, he rewards you with a long life and deep peace in your daily journey.
christianity_proverbs_3_2.context: This verse promises that trusting God brings long life and peace to those who follow his ways.

christianity_proverbs_3_4.meaning: Relying on God helps you earn respect from people and shows you have good sense in all matters.
christianity_proverbs_3_4.context: Trusting in God helps you gain respect and good judgment from both divine and human observers around you.

christianity_proverbs_3_6.meaning: When you let God guide your choices, he clears the road ahead so you can walk without confusion or fear.
christianity_proverbs_3_6.context: This advice tells you to include God in every decision you make during your daily life activities.

christianity_proverbs_3_7.meaning: Stop trusting only your own smarts. Respect God deeply and choose to walk away from wrong actions every single day.
christianity_proverbs_3_7.context: This warning stops you from thinking you know everything and tells you to respect God and avoid bad acts.

christianity_proverbs_3_14.meaning: Wisdom is more valuable than money or physical possessions. Pursuing wisdom brings greater benefits than gold.
christianity_proverbs_3_14.context: This verse is from the Christian book of Proverbs, written by Solomon. It talks about the value and blessings of wisdom.

christianity_proverbs_3_15.meaning: Wisdom is more valuable than any material possessions. Seeking wisdom brings unparalleled satisfaction.
christianity_proverbs_3_15.context: This verse is also from Proverbs, emphasizing the worth of wisdom. It compares wisdom to precious things like rubies.

christianity_proverbs_3_16.meaning: Wisdom brings a long and prosperous life, along with wealth and respect.
christianity_proverbs_3_16.context: The hands of wisdom represent her qualities. Longevity is in her right hand, while riches and honor are in her left.

christianity_proverbs_3_17.explanation:
King Solomon writes these words to his son, personifying wisdom as a noble woman. He describes the journey of living a life guided by divine insight.

Choosing wisdom leads to a life of harmony and inner tranquility. When we follow righteous paths, we find true contentment and avoid unnecessary conflict.
christianity_proverbs_3_17.meaning: Choosing wisdom leads to a life of harmony and inner tranquility. When we follow righteous paths, we find true contentment and avoid unnecessary conflict.
christianity_proverbs_3_17.context: King Solomon writes these words to his son, personifying wisdom as a noble woman. He describes the journey of living a life guided by divine insight.

christianity_proverbs_3_18.meaning: Acquiring wisdom is like finding a life-giving tree. Hold onto wisdom tightly and be happy. Those who keep wisdom safe are blessed.
christianity_proverbs_3_18.context: This verse is from the Christian book of Proverbs, written by Solomon. It talks about a woman who represents wisdom, guidance, and blessings in life.

christianity_proverbs_3_20.meaning: By understanding God's teachings, we can uncover hidden truths and bring rain for growth.
christianity_proverbs_3_20.context: This verse is also from Proverbs, discussing the power of knowledge. It refers to God revealing His wisdom and creating through His word.

christianity_proverbs_3_22.meaning: Wisdom provides comfort and helps you navigate life's challenges gracefully.
christianity_proverbs_3_22.context: This verse is from Proverbs 3:21, where wisdom is compared to a garment that brings comfort and protection.

christianity_proverbs_3_23.meaning: By relying on God, you can walk confidently without fear or stumbling.
christianity_proverbs_3_23.context: This verse is from Proverbs 3:23, emphasizing the importance of trusting in God for safety and security.

christianity_proverbs_3_8.meaning: This verse means that when you trust in God and follow His teachings, it will bring good health to your body and nourishment to your bones. In simpler terms, obeying God brings physical and spiritual well-being.
christianity_proverbs_3_8.context: This verse is from the book of Proverbs in the Christian Bible, written by King Solomon. It is part of a chapter (3:1-10) that emphasizes the importance of trusting in God and following His guidance for a prosperous life.

christianity_proverbs_3_9.meaning: Us to give priority to God and use our resources, especially money and possessions, to honor and serve Him first. By doing so, we show our gratitude and commitment to Him.
christianity_proverbs_3_9.context: This verse is also from the book of Proverbs in the Christian Bible. It is part of a chapter (3:1-10) that encourages believers to prioritize God's will and trust in His guidance for success.

christianity_proverbs_3_10.meaning: This verse encourages believers to trust in God and follow His path for prosperity and abundance in their life. By obeying God, your life will be filled with blessings and success.
christianity_proverbs_3_10.context: This verse is also from the book of Proverbs in the Christian Bible. It is part of a chapter (3:1-10) that emphasizes trusting in God and following His guidance for prosperity and blessings in life.

christianity_proverbs_3_11.meaning: God's discipline can be challenging, but it helps us grow stronger and wiser. Trusting in God and following His path leads to a fulfilling life.
christianity_proverbs_3_11.context: This verse is from the book of Proverbs in the Christian Bible. It is part of a chapter (3:1-10) that emphasizes trusting in God and following His guidance for a successful life.

christianity_proverbs_3_24.meaning: When you trust God fully, your mind stays calm. You will sleep well without any worry or fear.
christianity_proverbs_3_24.context: This verse tells you that trusting God brings deep peace and safety to your daily life.

christianity_proverbs_3_25.meaning: Do not worry when evil people face trouble. God protects you, so you do not need to fear their fate.
christianity_proverbs_3_25.context: The writer warns you not to panic when bad things happen to people who do wrong.

christianity_proverbs_3_26.meaning: God is your safe place. He will hold your feet steady so you do not stumble into harm.
christianity_proverbs_3_26.context: God acts as a strong shield that protects you from falling into danger or traps.

christianity_proverbs_3_27.meaning: If you can help someone, do it now. Do not hold back kindness when you have the power to give.
christianity_proverbs_3_27.context: This rule tells you to help others right away when you have the chance to do so.

christianity_proverbs_3_28.meaning: Do not keep people waiting when you can help them right now. Be prompt and kind.
christianity_proverbs_3_28.context: A neighbor asks for help, but you delay giving what you already have ready.

christianity_proverbs_3_29.meaning: Do not plan bad things against people who trust you. Treat those near you with care.
christianity_proverbs_3_29.context: Your neighbor lives safely near you, trusting that you will not hurt them.

christianity_proverbs_3_30.meaning: Do not fight with people without a real reason. Avoid starting trouble over small or imagined issues.
christianity_proverbs_3_30.context: You feel angry at someone, but they have not actually done anything wrong to you.

christianity_proverbs_3_31.meaning: Do not admire or copy people who use violence. Stay away from their harmful and dangerous ways.
christianity_proverbs_3_31.context: Some people use force or violence to get what they want in life.

christianity_proverbs_3_33.meaning: Living a good life brings peace and joy while doing wrong leads to trouble and sadness.
christianity_proverbs_3_33.context: God brings trouble to evil homes but gives blessings to the homes of good people.

christianity_proverbs_3_34.meaning: Being proud and mocking others is foolish while staying humble earns God's favor and grace.
christianity_proverbs_3_34.context: God laughs at those who make fun of others but shows kindness to those who are humble.

christianity_proverbs_3_35.meaning: Making smart choices leads to a good reputation while acting foolishly brings embarrassment and regret.
christianity_proverbs_3_35.context: Wise people gain honor and respect while foolish people end up with shame and disgrace.

christianity_proverbs_4_1.meaning: Listening to wise guidance helps you understand life better and make good choices every day.
christianity_proverbs_4_1.context: A father asks his children to listen carefully to his advice so they can learn wisdom.

christianity_proverbs_4_2.meaning: The importance of learning from wise mentors and not neglecting their teachings. It reminds us to treasure knowledge and obey the guidance of those who care for our growth and well-being.
christianity_proverbs_4_2.context: This verse is from the book of Proverbs in the Christian Bible, written by King Solomon. It is part of a longer passage that encourages the reader to seek wisdom and not forget the teachings of their parents or spiritual guides.

christianity_proverbs_4_3.meaning: This verse illustrates the strong bond between Solomon and his father, David. It emphasizes the importance of having a close relationship with our parents, mentors, or spiritual guides, who can guide us and teach us valuable life lessons.
christianity_proverbs_4_3.context: This verse is also from the book of Proverbs, describing the relationship between King Solomon and his father, King David. It highlights the bond between a father and son.

christianity_proverbs_4_4.meaning: The importance of listening to and following the advice of our parents, mentors, or spiritual guides. It encourages us to internalize their wisdom and apply it in our lives.
christianity_proverbs_4_4.context: This verse continues from the previous one, showing how Solomon received wisdom from his father and was encouraged to keep the teachings of his parents.

christianity_proverbs_4_8.meaning: This verse advises us to value wisdom and seek it, as it will bring honor and success to our lives. It encourages us to embrace wisdom from various sources and apply it wisely.
christianity_proverbs_4_8.context: This verse is also from the book of Proverbs, giving advice on how to value and benefit from wisdom.

christianity_proverbs_4_13.meaning: The verse emphasizes the need to embrace wisdom and not let go of it. It is essential to cherish and follow wisdom for a fulfilling life.
christianity_proverbs_4_13.context: This verse comes from the book of Proverbs in the Christian Bible, written by Solomon. It talks about the importance of grasping and holding onto wisdom, which is represented as a woman (instruction).

christianity_proverbs_4_14.meaning: The verse encourages us to stay away from evil paths and the company of people who engage in wrongdoing. Doing so will protect you from negative influences and harmful actions.
christianity_proverbs_4_14.context: This verse is also from the book of Proverbs, where Solomon advises against associating with wicked people and their ways.

christianity_proverbs_4_15.meaning: The verse advises us to stay away from evil and not merely observe it. By taking action and turning away from evil, we demonstrate our commitment to goodness.
christianity_proverbs_4_15.context: This verse continues the theme of avoiding evil paths and emphasizes the importance of not passing by or ignoring it.

christianity_proverbs_4_16.meaning: The verse cautions us about the evil intentions of those who seek to harm others while they sleep. It is essential to be aware of such people and protect ourselves from their negative influence.
christianity_proverbs_4_16.context: This verse is also from the book of Proverbs, where Solomon warns about the wicked people who don't sleep unless they cause harm to others.

christianity_proverbs_4_9.meaning: That a wise and loving mother or mentor can bestow upon her child a symbol of beauty (a garland) and success (a crown) through her guidance and blessings.
christianity_proverbs_4_9.context: This verse is from the Christian book of Proverbs, written by Solomon. It speaks about a woman (usually interpreted as a mother or a wise woman) bestowing blessings upon her son. The verse is part of a larger passage that encourages children to listen to and follow the wisdom of their parents.

christianity_proverbs_4_10.meaning: The importance of listening to and following the advice of wise elders, as it promises that a long and fulfilling life awaits those who do so.
christianity_proverbs_4_10.context: This verse is also from the Christian book of Proverbs. It addresses a son and encourages him to listen to his father's wisdom. The verse is part of a collection of teachings aimed at guiding children to make good choices in life.

christianity_proverbs_4_11.meaning: The significance of being guided by wise mentors who lead us on the right path, ensuring that we learn and grow in wisdom.
christianity_proverbs_4_11.context: This verse is also from the Christian book of Proverbs. It continues the teachings for the son, describing how the mother or mentor has taught and guided the child in the right path. The verse is part of a collection of teachings on wisdom and guidance.

christianity_proverbs_4_12.meaning: This verse encourages children to trust and follow the advice of their parents, promising that they will have a safe and successful life path.
christianity_proverbs_4_12.context: This verse is also from the Christian book of Proverbs. It speaks about a son's journey, assuring him that his steps will be secure and he will not stumble while following the wisdom of his parents.

christianity_proverbs_4_22.meaning: True wisdom keeps your mind and spirit healthy, helping you live a full and strong life.
christianity_proverbs_4_22.context: A father tells his son that wisdom acts like food and medicine for your soul.

christianity_proverbs_4_25.meaning: Stay focused on your goals and do not let distractions or bad habits pull your attention away.
christianity_proverbs_4_25.context: The wise man advises his son to keep his eyes focused on the right path.

christianity_proverbs_4_26.meaning: Plan your life carefully and walk steadily so you do not stumble into trouble or make mistakes.
christianity_proverbs_4_26.context: The father urges his son to walk steadily and plan his life with careful thought.

christianity_proverbs_4_27.meaning: Stay on the right path and refuse to do wrong things, even if they seem easy or tempting.
christianity_proverbs_4_27.context: The advice warns against taking shortcuts or bending the rules to get what you want.

christianity_proverbs_5_1.meaning: The verse encourages children to seek wisdom from their parents and learn from their experiences, fostering a strong family bond and passing on valuable knowledge.
christianity_proverbs_5_1.context: This verse is from the book of Proverbs in the Christian Bible. It is addressed to a son, advising him to pay attention to his father's wisdom and listen to his understanding.

christianity_proverbs_5_2.meaning: The verse emphasizes the value of listening and learning from elders, as it helps one grow wisely and keep valuable knowledge safe.
christianity_proverbs_5_2.context: This verse continues the advice given in verse 1, emphasizing the importance of maintaining discretion and preserving knowledge through listening to one's parents.

christianity_proverbs_5_3.meaning: The verse highlights the danger of being deceived by a seductive person, using sweet words and attractive appearance to lure others into harmful situations.
christianity_proverbs_5_3.context: This verse describes the allure of a deceitful woman, using similes comparing her words to honey and her appearance to oil.

christianity_proverbs_5_4.meaning: The verse cautions against being deceived by a seductive person, as she can cause great pain and harm to those who trust her.
christianity_proverbs_5_4.context: This verse continues the warning against a deceitful woman, mentioning the harsh consequences she brings upon those who trust her.

christianity_proverbs_4_17.meaning: Gaining money by hurting others is wrong. True peace comes from honest work and treating people with kindness.
christianity_proverbs_4_17.context: People who choose evil paths often gain wealth through unfair means and hurting others deeply.

christianity_proverbs_4_19.meaning: Bad choices hide dangers from you. Stay in the light of good advice to avoid falling into trouble.
christianity_proverbs_4_19.context: Living a bad life is like walking in total darkness where you cannot see the ground.

christianity_proverbs_4_20.meaning: Listen closely to good advice. Paying attention to wisdom helps you make better choices in your daily life.
christianity_proverbs_4_20.context: A wise parent asks their child to listen carefully and pay close attention to their guidance.

christianity_proverbs_4_21.meaning: Hold good advice close to your heart. Let it guide your thoughts and actions every single day.
christianity_proverbs_4_21.context: Keep wise words in your mind and heart so you never forget them or ignore them.

christianity_proverbs_5_13.meaning: Ignoring good advice leads to bad choices. You should listen to wise people to avoid making serious mistakes in life.
christianity_proverbs_5_13.context: A person admits they ignored wise advice and refused to listen to those who taught them right from wrong.

christianity_proverbs_5_14.meaning: Bad decisions can ruin your reputation. You may end up feeling ashamed and alone when everyone sees your failure.
christianity_proverbs_5_14.context: The speaker describes reaching a point of total disaster and shame in front of the community because of their bad choices.

christianity_proverbs_5_15.meaning: Be faithful to your spouse. Find joy and satisfaction in your own marriage rather than looking for excitement elsewhere.
christianity_proverbs_5_15.context: The writer uses water as a metaphor for sexual intimacy, urging men to enjoy their own wives instead of others.

christianity_proverbs_5_16.meaning: Keep your intimate life private. Do not share your personal joys with the public or risk losing your dignity.
christianity_proverbs_5_16.context: This verse asks if your private joys should be displayed publicly for everyone to see and judge like open streams.

christianity_proverbs_5_5.meaning: Bad choices have serious consequences. Avoiding temptation protects your life and keeps you safe from harm.
christianity_proverbs_5_5.context: This verse warns that following a seductive woman leads directly to spiritual ruin and eternal death.

christianity_proverbs_5_6.meaning: Ignorance does not excuse bad behavior. You must seek wisdom to recognize and avoid harmful paths.
christianity_proverbs_5_6.context: The woman described here is unaware that her path is wrong and leads away from life.

christianity_proverbs_5_7.meaning: Listen carefully to wise guidance. Following good advice helps you make better choices in life.
christianity_proverbs_5_7.context: The father urges his sons to pay close attention to his wise advice and instructions.

christianity_proverbs_5_8.meaning: Avoid places that tempt you. Keeping distance from sin helps you stay pure and faithful.
christianity_proverbs_5_8.context: The speaker commands his sons to stay far away from the tempting woman and her home.

christianity_proverbs_5_9.meaning: The verse warns against giving away one's dignity and authority to others, as well as entrusting one's life to a cruel person. This can lead to a life of suffering and regret.
christianity_proverbs_5_9.context: This verse is from the book of Proverbs in the Christian Bible, written by King Solomon. It is part of a collection of wisdom teachings meant to guide individuals in making wise decisions and avoiding harmful choices. In this verse, the 'cruel one' refers to someone who takes advantage of others and does not show mercy.

christianity_proverbs_5_10.meaning: The verse advises against allowing others to benefit from one's hard work and resources, as it can lead to a life of emptiness and regret. Instead, it is better to use one's talents and possessions wisely.
christianity_proverbs_5_10.context: This verse is also from the book of Proverbs in the Christian Bible. It continues the teachings on wise living and cautions against making poor choices that can harm oneself and others. In this verse, 'strangers' refer to people who take advantage of one's wealth.

christianity_proverbs_5_11.meaning: The verse warns about the regret one feels when they disregard wisdom and instruction, leading to a life of emptiness and disappointment. It encourages listening to wise counselors and embracing life's lessons.
christianity_proverbs_5_11.context: This verse is also from the book of Proverbs in the Christian Bible. It talks about the consequences of ignoring wisdom and not listening to those who try to guide and teach us. In this verse, 'consumed' refers to the end of one's life when all their energy and strength are gone.

christianity_proverbs_5_12.meaning: The verse advises against rejecting wisdom and ignoring the guidance of wise individuals. By embracing instruction and learning from experiences, one can avoid regret and lead a fulfilling life.
christianity_proverbs_5_12.context: This verse is also from the book of Proverbs in the Christian Bible. It speaks about the importance of learning from experiences and not repeating mistakes. In this verse, 'hated instruction' refers to rejecting wisdom and ignoring advice from wise individuals.

christianity_proverbs_5_17.meaning: Your spouse is for you alone. Do not let outside people or temptations come between you and your partner.
christianity_proverbs_5_17.context: A father tells his son to keep his wife close and not share her with others.

christianity_proverbs_5_18.meaning: Find true happiness in your marriage. Celebrate the love you built together from the very beginning of your life.
christianity_proverbs_5_18.context: The father encourages his son to find deep joy and blessing in his own marriage.

christianity_proverbs_5_19.meaning: Your partner should bring you constant comfort and peace. Let their steady love keep your heart full and happy.
christianity_proverbs_5_19.context: The text uses gentle animal images to describe the beauty and comfort of a loving wife.

christianity_proverbs_5_20.meaning: Do not let another person steal your heart. Stay faithful to your spouse and do not seek love outside your marriage.
christianity_proverbs_5_20.context: The father warns his son against the danger of cheating on his wife with another woman.

christianity_proverbs_5_21.meaning: You are never truly alone because God sees your actions and understands your true heart.
christianity_proverbs_5_21.context: God watches everything you do and sees every choice you make in your daily life.

christianity_proverbs_5_22.meaning: Bad habits can feel like a trap that holds you tight and stops you from moving forward.
christianity_proverbs_5_22.context: A person who does bad things gets trapped by their own wrong actions and choices.

christianity_proverbs_5_23.meaning: Ignoring good advice leads to big mistakes that can ruin your life and future plans.
christianity_proverbs_5_23.context: Someone who refuses to learn or listen to wise advice will make very poor decisions.

christianity_proverbs_6_1.meaning: Be careful before you promise to help someone with money, as it can cause you big trouble.
christianity_proverbs_6_1.context: A father warns his son about the danger of promising to pay another person's debt.

christianity_proverbs_6_2.meaning: Your careless promises have caused you trouble. You must take responsibility for your words and fix the mess you made.
christianity_proverbs_6_2.context: You promised to help a friend but now you cannot pay back the debt you owe.

christianity_proverbs_6_3.meaning: Humble yourself and ask for help. Do not be proud. Take action now to resolve the conflict and free yourself from trouble.
christianity_proverbs_6_3.context: You are stuck in a bad deal with a neighbor. You need to act fast to save yourself.

christianity_proverbs_6_4.meaning: Stay alert and determined. Do not let laziness stop you. Work hard and stay focused until you solve the problem completely.
christianity_proverbs_6_4.context: Do not ignore the problem by sleeping or resting. You must stay awake and focused on fixing things.

christianity_proverbs_6_5.meaning: Act with speed and urgency. Do not wait. Break free from your bad situation before it gets worse or traps you forever.
christianity_proverbs_6_5.context: Escape quickly like a fast animal running away from a hunter or a bird flying from a trap.

christianity_proverbs_6_14.meaning: People who always try to hurt others and create trouble will eventually face the negative results of their own actions.
christianity_proverbs_6_14.context: This verse describes a person who constantly plans bad things and tries to cause fights between friends.

christianity_proverbs_6_15.meaning: Bad deeds lead to sudden disaster that cannot be fixed, so it is wise to avoid evil paths.
christianity_proverbs_6_15.context: The text warns that the trouble for such a wicked person will arrive quickly and without any warning.

christianity_proverbs_6_16.meaning: God has clear standards for behavior, and we should avoid actions that he considers deeply wrong and hateful.
christianity_proverbs_6_16.context: The writer introduces a list of specific behaviors that God strongly dislikes and finds very offensive to him.

christianity_proverbs_6_17.meaning: We should be humble, speak the truth, and protect others from harm because these are things God hates.
christianity_proverbs_6_17.context: This verse lists three specific sins: being proud, telling lies, and hurting innocent people who did nothing wrong.

christianity_proverbs_6_10.meaning: Small delays in work add up quickly. You must stay active and focused to avoid falling behind in life.
christianity_proverbs_6_10.context: The writer warns against laziness and sleeping too much during the day instead of working hard.

christianity_proverbs_6_11.meaning: Poverty arrives fast when you are lazy. Hard work protects you from sudden lack and financial ruin.
christianity_proverbs_6_11.context: Laziness leads to sudden financial trouble that strikes you like a thief in the night.

christianity_proverbs_6_12.meaning: Bad people use tricky speech to fool others. Avoid those who twist the truth to manipulate you.
christianity_proverbs_6_12.context: This describes a dishonest person who uses twisted words to deceive others and cause harm.

christianity_proverbs_6_13.meaning: Watch for hidden signals from sneaky people. Their secret gestures show they are planning something bad.
christianity_proverbs_6_13.context: The deceitful person uses secret signals with eyes, feet, and fingers to plot mischief.

christianity_proverbs_6_6.meaning: The verse tells us to observe the hardworking ants and understand their discipline, organization, and teamwork. It urges us to apply these qualities in our daily life to achieve success and avoid being lazy.
christianity_proverbs_6_6.context: This verse is from the Christian book of Proverbs, written by Solomon. It encourages the reader to learn from the habits of ants, small insects, and apply those lessons to their own life.

christianity_proverbs_6_7.meaning: The ants' independence and unity without needing a boss or authority figure. It teaches us the importance of self-reliance and cooperation.
christianity_proverbs_6_7.context: This verse is a continuation from the previous one, describing the ants' lack of a leader or hierarchy.

christianity_proverbs_6_8.meaning: The ants' foresight and planning, storing food when resources are abundant. It encourages us to be wise with our resources and plan for the future.
christianity_proverbs_6_8.context: This verse continues the story of ants, explaining how they prepare food for the upcoming seasons.

christianity_proverbs_6_9.meaning: This verse encourages us to stop procrastinating and take action. It reminds us that idleness leads to failure, while diligence brings success.
christianity_proverbs_6_9.context: This verse addresses a lazy person, asking them to wake up and start working.

christianity_proverbs_6_22.meaning: Good wisdom helps you make right choices every day and keeps you safe even when you sleep.
christianity_proverbs_6_22.context: The writer says that wisdom guides your daily actions and protects you while you rest.

christianity_proverbs_6_23.meaning: God's laws guide your life like a light in the dark, helping you find the right path.
christianity_proverbs_6_23.context: This verse compares God's rules to a lamp that shows the way in the dark.

christianity_proverbs_6_24.meaning: Wisdom helps you avoid bad relationships and protects you from people who lie to gain your trust.
christianity_proverbs_6_24.context: The text warns that wisdom protects you from people who use sweet words to lead you astray.

christianity_proverbs_6_25.meaning: Do not let your mind be controlled by someone's looks, because that can lead you into serious trouble.
christianity_proverbs_6_25.context: The speaker advises you not to let your heart be taken over by someone's physical looks.

christianity_proverbs_6_18.meaning: A wicked person plans evil, and acts swiftly to cause harm. Such a person should be avoided.
christianity_proverbs_6_18.context: This verse from the Bible's Book of Proverbs (6:18) describes a person with a wicked heart and quick feet to cause trouble.

christianity_proverbs_6_19.meaning: A person who tells lies to harm others, especially among family or close friends, is harmful and untrustworthy.
christianity_proverbs_6_19.context: In Proverbs 6:19, a false witness is someone who lies and creates conflict among siblings or friends.

christianity_proverbs_6_20.meaning: Listen to and obey your parents' advice, as their wisdom can protect and guide you.
christianity_proverbs_6_20.context: Proverbs 6:20 advises a child to follow the teachings of their parents for guidance and wisdom.

christianity_proverbs_6_21.meaning: Meditate on and follow God's wisdom daily, keeping His guidance close to your heart for guidance and growth.
christianity_proverbs_6_21.context: Proverbs 6:21 encourages us to keep God's teachings close to our hearts as a constant reminder.

christianity_proverbs_6_26.meaning: Bad choices drain your energy and spirit. You lose your best self when you break trust with others.
christianity_proverbs_6_26.context: The writer warns that cheating with another person costs you your health and your very life.

christianity_proverbs_6_27.meaning: You cannot do harmful things without getting hurt. Bad actions always bring pain to the person who does them.
christianity_proverbs_6_27.context: The text asks if you can hold fire in your lap without burning your clothes.

christianity_proverbs_6_28.meaning: Sin causes immediate damage. You cannot ignore the pain that comes from doing what is wrong.
christianity_proverbs_6_28.context: The writer asks if you can walk on hot coals without burning your feet badly.

christianity_proverbs_6_29.meaning: Cheating brings serious consequences. You cannot harm another family without facing justice and losing your own peace.
christianity_proverbs_6_29.context: The passage compares cheating to touching fire. It says you will face punishment for this act.

christianity_proverbs_7_3.meaning: Keep good advice deep inside your mind so you can make right choices every single day.
christianity_proverbs_7_3.context: The father tells his son to keep wise words close to his body and heart always.

christianity_proverbs_7_5.meaning: Stay away from people who use flattery to trick you into doing things that are wrong.
christianity_proverbs_7_5.context: The father warns his son about a woman who uses sweet words to lead him astray.

christianity_proverbs_7_6.meaning: Sometimes we observe life from a safe distance to understand what is happening around us.
christianity_proverbs_7_6.context: The speaker describes looking out from his home window through the wooden lattice bars outside.

christianity_proverbs_7_7.meaning: Lack of wisdom makes young people vulnerable to bad influences and poor decisions in life.
christianity_proverbs_7_7.context: The speaker sees a young man who lacks wisdom and understanding among other simple people nearby.

christianity_proverbs_6_30.meaning: Basic needs can explain bad actions, but this does not make the act of stealing right or acceptable.
christianity_proverbs_6_30.context: People might understand stealing food when hunger drives a person to take what they need to survive.

christianity_proverbs_6_31.meaning: Wrongdoing brings heavy consequences. You must make full restitution for the harm you cause to others.
christianity_proverbs_6_31.context: If a thief is caught, he must pay back seven times what he stole from the victim.

christianity_proverbs_6_32.meaning: Betraying trust is foolish and destructive. It ruins your character and damages your inner peace and soul.
christianity_proverbs_6_32.context: Cheating on a partner shows a lack of wisdom and deeply harms the person who commits the act.

christianity_proverbs_6_33.meaning: Bad choices leave lasting scars. The shame and pain from betrayal cannot be easily hidden or forgotten.
christianity_proverbs_6_33.context: The adulterer faces physical pain and social shame that will follow him for the rest of his life.

christianity_proverbs_6_34.meaning: The verse teaches that jealousy can lead to extreme anger and revenge in relationships. Husbands should seek understanding and forgiveness instead of taking revenge.
christianity_proverbs_6_34.context: This verse is from the Christian book of Proverbs, written by Solomon. It talks about jealousy causing a husband's anger and intense desire for revenge against the person who caused the jealousy.

christianity_proverbs_6_35.meaning: The verse highlights the persistence of the husband in seeking revenge despite offers of ransom or gifts. It teaches that one should not be easily appeased or distracted when pursuing their goals.
christianity_proverbs_6_35.context: This verse is also from the Christian book of Proverbs. It emphasizes that even when someone offers a ransom or gifts, the person being pursued (in this case, the husband) will not stop pursuing the object of his desire.

christianity_proverbs_7_1.meaning: The verse instructs the reader to treasure and internalize the wisdom of their parents or elders. It emphasizes the importance of following guidance and preserving valuable knowledge.
christianity_proverbs_7_1.context: This verse begins a section in Proverbs where Solomon advises his son to keep his words and commandments close to his heart.

christianity_proverbs_7_2.meaning: The verse encourages the reader to protect and prioritize the wisdom they have been taught, comparing it to protecting one's eyesight (the apple of one's eye).
christianity_proverbs_7_2.context: This verse continues the advice to the reader, urging them to protect and cherish the wisdom they have received.

christianity_proverbs_7_12.meaning: Danger often hides in plain sight, so you must stay alert and avoid risky spots.
christianity_proverbs_7_12.context: A wicked woman is seen moving around the city at night, hiding in public places.

christianity_proverbs_7_13.meaning: False friends may act boldly to win your trust, so do not let their charm fool you.
christianity_proverbs_7_13.context: The woman grabs the young man and kisses him to show her bold and shameless attitude.

christianity_proverbs_7_14.meaning: People may use good deeds as an excuse to do bad things, so check their true motives.
christianity_proverbs_7_14.context: She claims she has finished her religious duties and is free to enjoy the rest of the day.

christianity_proverbs_7_15.meaning: Flattery can be a trap, so be careful when someone acts too eager to please you.
christianity_proverbs_7_15.context: She says she went out specifically to find him and that she is very happy to see him.

christianity_proverbs_7_16.meaning: She uses nice things to hide her bad plans and trick him into doing something wrong.
christianity_proverbs_7_16.context: A woman describes her fancy room to make a young man want to come inside.

christianity_proverbs_7_17.meaning: Pleasant smells can make you lower your guard and forget about the real danger ahead.
christianity_proverbs_7_17.context: She adds that her bed smells very sweet with expensive spices and perfumes.

christianity_proverbs_7_18.meaning: She promises short term fun to distract him from the long term pain and shame.
christianity_proverbs_7_18.context: She invites him to stay all night and enjoy physical pleasure together with her.

christianity_proverbs_7_19.meaning: Lies are often used to create a false sense of safety when you are about to sin.
christianity_proverbs_7_19.context: She claims her husband is away on a trip so no one will see them.

christianity_proverbs_7_8.meaning: Walking alone in risky places without good advice leads you straight into trouble and bad choices.
christianity_proverbs_7_8.context: A young man walks alone near a woman's home without any wise friend to guide him.

christianity_proverbs_7_9.meaning: Sin often hides in the dark and quiet times when no one is watching your actions closely.
christianity_proverbs_7_9.context: The scene happens during dark times like evening or night when visibility is low and shadows hide things.

christianity_proverbs_7_10.meaning: Deceitful people often look attractive but have hidden plans to harm you and lead you astray.
christianity_proverbs_7_10.context: A woman dressed like a prostitute meets him on the street with a plan to trick him.

christianity_proverbs_7_11.meaning: People who lack self-control and respect for boundaries often cause chaos and lead others into sin.
christianity_proverbs_7_11.context: She is loud and rebellious, refusing to stay inside her home and wandering the streets instead.

christianity_proverbs_8_1.meaning: God wants everyone to know the truth. We should listen carefully to spiritual guidance because it is always available for those who seek it.
christianity_proverbs_8_1.context: Wisdom is personified as a woman who speaks loudly to attract the attention of people passing by in public spaces.

christianity_proverbs_8_2.meaning: Truth is not hidden away. It is placed in plain sight for everyone to see, so we must look for it in our daily lives.
christianity_proverbs_8_2.context: She stands on high hills and at busy crossroads where many travelers meet to ensure her message reaches as many people as possible.

christianity_proverbs_8_3.meaning: We should pay attention to wise advice in public places. Ignoring clear guidance leads to poor choices and unnecessary trouble in life.
christianity_proverbs_8_3.context: She shouts near city gates and entrances where crowds gather, making sure her voice is heard by everyone entering the community.

christianity_proverbs_8_4.meaning: God offers wisdom to everyone equally. We do not need special status to receive it. We only need to be willing to listen and learn.
christianity_proverbs_8_4.context: She addresses all human beings directly, calling out to men and women alike without excluding any group or social class.

christianity_proverbs_7_20.meaning: Bad influences often use lies about timing and opportunity to trick you into doing things you should not do.
christianity_proverbs_7_20.context: A seducer tells a young man that his husband is away on a trip with money.

christianity_proverbs_7_21.meaning: Flattery can cloud your judgment. Do not let smooth talking convince you to ignore your better sense.
christianity_proverbs_7_21.context: The woman uses sweet and flattering words to persuade the young man to follow her desires.

christianity_proverbs_7_22.meaning: Acting on impulse without thinking leads to disaster. Stop and consider the consequences before you move.
christianity_proverbs_7_22.context: The young man follows her blindly without thinking, like an animal walking toward its death.

christianity_proverbs_7_23.meaning: Sin often hides its deadly cost. Be aware that wrong choices can destroy you before you see danger.
christianity_proverbs_7_23.context: He does not realize that his actions will bring sudden and fatal harm to his life.

christianity_proverbs_7_24.meaning: The verse encourages children to listen to their parents and respect their guidance, as their words hold valuable knowledge and experience.
christianity_proverbs_7_24.context: This verse is from the book of Proverbs in the Christian Bible, written by the wise man Solomon. It is addressed to his sons, advising them to listen and pay attention to his words of wisdom.

christianity_proverbs_7_25.meaning: The verse advises children to stay away from harmful relationships and not to be misled by the alluring ways of the world.
christianity_proverbs_7_25.context: Solomon continues his speech to his sons, warning them against following the wrong path and the temptations of a dangerous woman.

christianity_proverbs_7_26.meaning: The negative outcomes of making bad choices and emphasizes the importance of making wise decisions.
christianity_proverbs_7_26.context: Solomon describes the destructive consequences of following the wrong path, mentioning that the woman's ways have caused many to suffer and fall into trouble.

christianity_proverbs_7_27.meaning: The verse warns against blindly following the wrong path and emphasizes the need to seek guidance from reliable sources.
christianity_proverbs_7_27.context: The verse describes the woman's house as a path leading to death and destruction, representing the dangers of following her guidance.

christianity_proverbs_8_19.meaning: True wisdom is far more valuable than money or wealth, so seek it above all else.
christianity_proverbs_8_19.context: Wisdom speaks about her value, saying she is more precious than gold or silver.

christianity_proverbs_8_22.meaning: Wisdom has existed since the very start, showing it is an eternal part of God's plan.
christianity_proverbs_8_22.context: Wisdom claims she was with God before He started creating the world and its history.

christianity_proverbs_8_23.meaning: Wisdom is older than the physical world, proving it is a timeless and unchanging truth.
christianity_proverbs_8_23.context: Wisdom says she was established before the earth was formed or the world came into being.

christianity_proverbs_8_24.meaning: Wisdom existed before nature was formed, showing it is the foundation of all creation.
christianity_proverbs_8_24.context: Wisdom describes her birth before deep oceans or water springs existed in the early world.

christianity_proverbs_8_15.meaning: Good leaders need wisdom to rule fairly. Without it, their power becomes blind and often causes harm.
christianity_proverbs_8_15.context: Wisdom speaks about how she helps leaders make fair and just decisions for their people.

christianity_proverbs_8_16.meaning: True power comes from wisdom. Leaders who follow wisdom bring peace and order to their nations.
christianity_proverbs_8_16.context: The text says that wise guidance is behind the actions of all good rulers on earth.

christianity_proverbs_8_17.meaning: God loves those who love him. If you truly seek him, you will find his guidance and help.
christianity_proverbs_8_17.context: Wisdom promises a close relationship with people who actively look for her in their daily lives.

christianity_proverbs_8_18.meaning: Wisdom brings real value. It gives you respect, stability, and a life that lasts long and feels full.
christianity_proverbs_8_18.context: Wisdom claims that following her leads to lasting wealth, respect, and a good life for everyone.

christianity_proverbs_8_6.meaning: Pay close attention to good advice because it leads to right choices and helps you live a better life.
christianity_proverbs_8_6.context: Wisdom calls out to people, asking them to listen carefully to her important and truthful words.

christianity_proverbs_8_9.meaning: When you seek knowledge with an open heart, the truth becomes clear and guides you toward doing what is right.
christianity_proverbs_8_9.context: The words of wisdom are clear and easy to see for anyone who truly wants to understand them.

christianity_proverbs_8_10.meaning: Learning how to live well is far more valuable than money because wealth cannot buy true understanding or peace.
christianity_proverbs_8_10.context: Wisdom tells us to value her teaching more than precious metals like silver or fine gold.

christianity_proverbs_8_11.meaning: Nothing in the world is as valuable as wisdom because it helps you make good choices and find lasting joy.
christianity_proverbs_8_11.context: Wisdom is described as being more precious than rubies and better than anything else you might want.

christianity_proverbs_8_33.meaning: You should listen to good advice and learn from it. Refusing to learn keeps you from becoming a wise person.
christianity_proverbs_8_33.context: The speaker urges listeners to accept teaching and gain wisdom without rejecting the advice offered to them.

christianity_proverbs_8_34.meaning: People who stay focused on learning and listening to wisdom every day are truly happy and blessed in their lives.
christianity_proverbs_8_34.context: The text describes a person who pays close attention to wisdom every single day without ever looking away.

christianity_proverbs_8_35.meaning: Finding true wisdom leads to a full life and helps you earn the love and favor of God.
christianity_proverbs_8_35.context: The verse promises that anyone who discovers wisdom will receive life and gain approval from the divine creator.

christianity_proverbs_9_1.meaning: True wisdom is solid and well built. It provides a strong foundation for your life and decisions.
christianity_proverbs_9_1.context: Wisdom is pictured as a woman who has constructed a strong house supported by seven sturdy pillars.

christianity_proverbs_8_25.meaning: Gods wisdom existed before the world began. It shows that wisdom is eternal and part of God.
christianity_proverbs_8_25.context: Wisdom speaks about being present before God created the mountains and hills on earth.

christianity_proverbs_8_26.meaning: Wisdom is older than the physical world. It teaches us that true understanding comes from God.
christianity_proverbs_8_26.context: Wisdom was there before the earth, fields, or dust of the world were made.

christianity_proverbs_8_27.meaning: God used wisdom to create order. We should seek wisdom to bring order to our lives.
christianity_proverbs_8_27.context: Wisdom was present when God created the heavens and set boundaries on the deep waters.

christianity_proverbs_8_28.meaning: Gods power and wisdom work together. Trusting God brings peace and stability in life.
christianity_proverbs_8_28.context: Wisdom watched as God made the clouds and strengthened the springs of the deep waters.

christianity_proverbs_8_29.meaning: God is in total control of nature and keeps everything in its proper place.
christianity_proverbs_8_29.context: God set limits for the ocean and shaped the earth during creation.

christianity_proverbs_8_30.meaning: True wisdom brings joy and happiness when we spend time close to God.
christianity_proverbs_8_30.context: Wisdom stood beside God during creation and enjoyed being near him every single day.

christianity_proverbs_8_31.meaning: God cares deeply about people and wants us to find joy in his world.
christianity_proverbs_8_31.context: Wisdom found joy in all of creation and especially loved being with human beings.

christianity_proverbs_8_32.meaning: You will be happy and blessed if you choose to follow God's good ways.
christianity_proverbs_8_32.context: Wisdom calls out to young people to listen carefully and follow her guidance.

christianity_proverbs_9_6.meaning: Stop acting foolishly; choose to live with understanding and make good choices.
christianity_proverbs_9_6.context: A wise woman invites people to leave foolish habits and live wisely.
