christianity_proverbs_9_7.meaning: Be careful when correcting others; it can lead to more conflict and hurt feelings.
christianity_proverbs_9_7.context: People who correct a mocking person or a wicked man often face more insults.

christianity_proverbs_9_10.meaning: Respecting God gives real wisdom and helps you understand life better.
christianity_proverbs_9_10.context: Knowing and respecting God starts true wisdom and understanding.

christianity_proverbs_9_11.meaning: Living with God can bring more time and a longer, fuller life.
christianity_proverbs_9_11.context: God promises to give more days and longer life to those who follow Him.

christianity_proverbs_9_2.meaning: God offers us spiritual nourishment and joy. We should accept his generous gifts with a grateful heart.
christianity_proverbs_9_2.context: Wisdom prepares a feast with food and drink to welcome guests into her home.

christianity_proverbs_9_3.meaning: God actively reaches out to everyone. We should listen to his call and not ignore his invitation.
christianity_proverbs_9_3.context: Wisdom sends servants to call people from the busy streets of the city to come.

christianity_proverbs_9_4.meaning: God welcomes everyone who admits they need help. Humility opens the door to true understanding.
christianity_proverbs_9_4.context: She invites those who are naive or lack sense to enter her house and learn.

christianity_proverbs_9_5.meaning: Accepting God's wisdom brings life and satisfaction. We should partake in his teachings daily.
christianity_proverbs_9_5.context: She urges guests to eat her bread and drink the wine she has carefully prepared.

christianity_proverbs_9_12.meaning: Being wise protects you; mocking others brings problems back to you, showing the importance of respect.
christianity_proverbs_9_12.context: A wise person keeps good choices for themselves, while a mocker faces their own trouble.

christianity_proverbs_9_13.meaning: Her loudness and lack of discipline show how ignorance can lead to trouble and harm.
christianity_proverbs_9_13.context: A foolish woman is noisy, uncontrolled, and lacks understanding or good judgment.

christianity_proverbs_9_14.meaning: Her position shows she is ready to speak, but her words may not be wise or helpful.
christianity_proverbs_9_14.context: She sits on a high city gate, watching people pass by her house.

christianity_proverbs_9_15.meaning: Her invitation warns that even those on good paths can be misled by foolish voices.
christianity_proverbs_9_15.context: She calls out to travelers who walk straight on their paths, inviting them to listen.

christianity_proverbs_10_8.meaning: Listening to good advice keeps you safe, but talking too much can lead to trouble.
christianity_proverbs_10_8.context: A wise person listens to rules, while a noisy fool keeps making mistakes.

christianity_proverbs_10_9.meaning: Doing right things keeps you steady, but lying or cheating will be discovered and hurt you.
christianity_proverbs_10_9.context: Someone who acts honestly walks safely, but a dishonest person will eventually be caught.

christianity_proverbs_10_10.meaning: Careful words prevent pain, but careless talk can cause problems for yourself.
christianity_proverbs_10_10.context: A quick smile can bring sadness, and a foolish chatter will end badly.

christianity_proverbs_10_12.meaning: Holding anger creates conflict, while showing love covers faults and keeps harmony.
christianity_proverbs_10_12.context: Hatred causes fights, but love hides mistakes and keeps peace.

christianity_proverbs_9_16.meaning: This verse encourages seeking wisdom from reliable sources, as those who are simple-minded or lacking understanding may be easily deceived by false teachings or misleading advice.
christianity_proverbs_9_16.context: In the Bible, Proverbs 9:16, this verse is part of a conversation between a wise woman (representing God) and those who seek wisdom. She invites simple and understanding individuals to come inside her house for guidance.

christianity_proverbs_9_17.meaning: The temporary satisfaction from worldly pleasures and encourages seeking wisdom, which brings true happiness and guidance in life.
christianity_proverbs_9_17.context: Proverbs 9:17 is a continuation of the conversation between the wise woman and those seeking wisdom. She compares the temporary pleasure from stolen water or secretly obtained food to the lasting joy of wisdom.

christianity_proverbs_9_18.meaning: The importance of wisdom in guiding our choices and avoiding the consequences of ignoring spiritual truths.
christianity_proverbs_9_18.context: In Proverbs 9:18, the verse describes the afterlife and the realm of the dead, known as Sheol. It mentions the presence of departed spirits and the consequences of ignoring wisdom.

christianity_proverbs_10_1.meaning: This verse begins a series of proverbs by Solomon, highlighting the significance of raising children to be wise and understanding, bringing joy to their parents.
christianity_proverbs_10_1.context: Proverbs 10:1 introduces a collection of wisdom sayings by Solomon, emphasizing the value of a wise son or daughter to a parent.

christianity_proverbs_10_2.meaning: Bad money does not help you, but living a good life keeps you safe from serious harm.
christianity_proverbs_10_2.context: This verse compares the value of evil gains versus the safety found in doing what is right.

christianity_proverbs_10_3.meaning: Good people will always have enough to eat, while bad people will not get what they want.
christianity_proverbs_10_3.context: God promises to take care of those who follow his ways and reject those who do evil.

christianity_proverbs_10_4.meaning: Being lazy leads to poverty, but working hard and staying busy will bring you money and success.
christianity_proverbs_10_4.context: This proverb links your work habits directly to your financial results and overall success in life.

christianity_proverbs_10_5.meaning: Smart people work when they should, but lazy people sleep through important times and bring shame.
christianity_proverbs_10_5.context: Farmers must work hard during the summer harvest season to store food for the rest of the year.

christianity_proverbs_10_14.meaning: The verse teaches us to prioritize learning and gaining knowledge for personal growth and to avoid making hasty decisions without considering the consequences. It also warns against judging others based on their wealth or social status.
christianity_proverbs_10_14.context: That wise individuals gather knowledge for personal growth and benefit, while foolish people often face difficulties due to their lack of wisdom.

christianity_proverbs_10_15.meaning: The verse emphasizes the importance of being grateful for what we have and not being deceived by material possessions. It also reminds us that the poor face more challenges and risks compared to the rich.
christianity_proverbs_10_15.context: The vulnerability of the poor who lack resources and protection.

christianity_proverbs_10_17.meaning: The verse encourages us to seek guidance and learn from others' experiences. It warns against ignoring advice and the negative impact it can have on others.
christianity_proverbs_10_17.context: The consequences of disregarding advice and leading others astray.

christianity_proverbs_10_18.meaning: The verse warns against harboring hatred and spreading false information about others. It encourages speaking honestly and kindly, reflecting positively on ourselves and others.
christianity_proverbs_10_18.context: The importance of speaking truthfully and kindly.

christianity_proverbs_10_27.meaning: The verse teaches us to fear and respect God, as it leads to a fulfilling life. On the other hand, ignoring God's teachings results in a short and challenging life.
christianity_proverbs_10_27.context: This verse from the Christian book of Proverbs talks about the importance of fearing God (Yahweh) and its impact on one's life. It mentions that those who fear God will have a long and prosperous life, while the wicked who don't fear God will face short and difficult lives.

christianity_proverbs_10_28.meaning: The joy and hope that righteous people experience, while warning that wicked people's hopes will fade away. It demonstrates the difference in perspectives between good and evil individuals.
christianity_proverbs_10_28.context: This verse from Proverbs talks about the happiness and hope experienced by righteous people, while the perishable fate of wicked people. It highlights the contrast between the outlook of good and evil individuals.

christianity_proverbs_10_29.meaning: The verse explains that following God's path provides safety and protection for the righteous, while disobeying Him leads to destruction for those who stray from His ways.
christianity_proverbs_10_29.context: This verse from the Christian book of Proverbs discusses the protective nature of following God's ways for the righteous and the destructive nature for those who disobey Him.

christianity_proverbs_11_1.meaning: The verse highlights the value of being truthful and fair in measurements, as it brings pleasure to God and shows respect for His teachings.
christianity_proverbs_11_1.context: This verse from Proverbs talks about the importance of honesty and integrity in dealing with weights and measures, as it pleases God.

christianity_proverbs_10_19.meaning: The verse means that saying too much can lead to misunderstandings and disobedience. Wise people know when to keep silent.
christianity_proverbs_10_19.context: This verse from the Christian book of Proverbs talks about the relationship between the quantity of words and potential for disobedience. It is set in a cultural context where people value communication and speaking one's mind.

christianity_proverbs_10_22.meaning: That when God blesses someone, their wealth grows without any additional problems. It highlights the importance of trusting in God's plan.
christianity_proverbs_10_22.context: Proverbs 10:22 is a verse from the Christian Bible, specifically in the book of Proverbs. It is written in the context of discussing blessings and their consequences.

christianity_proverbs_10_24.meaning: This verse says that the fears of wicked people will come true, while the desires of righteous people will be fulfilled.
christianity_proverbs_10_24.context: Proverbs 10:24 is part of the Christian Proverbs book, discussing the consequences of wickedness and righteousness. It is set in a culture that values wisdom and morality.

christianity_proverbs_10_26.meaning: This verse compares the negative effects of laziness to unpleasant sensations, such as sour vinegar on the teeth and smoke in the eyes. It highlights the harmfulness of being idle.
christianity_proverbs_10_26.context: Proverbs 10:26 is from the Christian Bible, focusing on the consequences of laziness and the importance of diligence. It is written in a culture that values hard work.

christianity_proverbs_11_14.meaning: Asking many people for help leads to success, while ignoring advice causes failure.
christianity_proverbs_11_14.context: A leader needs many smart advisors to make good choices for the whole country.

christianity_proverbs_11_15.meaning: Saying no to risky promises keeps you safe, while agreeing to them brings trouble.
christianity_proverbs_11_15.context: Promising to pay for a stranger's debt is a risky and dangerous financial move.

christianity_proverbs_11_16.meaning: Being kind earns you true respect, but using force only gets you money.
christianity_proverbs_11_16.context: This verse compares how kind women and aggressive men gain different kinds of respect.

christianity_proverbs_11_17.meaning: Being kind to others makes you feel good inside, while being mean hurts you.
christianity_proverbs_11_17.context: This proverb looks at how your daily actions affect your own body and spirit.

christianity_proverbs_11_9.meaning: Knowing the truth protects you from harm, but spreading lies only brings destruction to those around you.
christianity_proverbs_11_9.context: A bad person uses lies to hurt others, while a good person stays safe through wisdom.

christianity_proverbs_11_10.meaning: A community thrives when honest people succeed, and people feel relief when dishonest people finally face consequences.
christianity_proverbs_11_10.context: The whole city feels happy when good people do well, but they celebrate when bad people fail.

christianity_proverbs_11_11.meaning: Honesty and good deeds build up society, while evil speech and actions can cause a community to collapse.
christianity_proverbs_11_11.context: Good people help a city grow strong, but bad people use their words to bring it down.

christianity_proverbs_11_13.meaning: You can trust a person who keeps quiet about private matters, but gossipers will always betray your confidence.
christianity_proverbs_11_13.context: Someone who talks too much shares private things, but a reliable person keeps secrets safe and secure.

christianity_proverbs_11_3.meaning: Living with honesty helps you make good choices, but being deceitful will eventually ruin your life.
christianity_proverbs_11_3.context: This verse compares how honest people and dishonest people live their daily lives.

christianity_proverbs_11_4.meaning: Money is useless when you are in deep trouble, but doing what is right saves your life.
christianity_proverbs_11_4.context: The writer warns that money cannot save you when you face serious trouble or judgment.

christianity_proverbs_11_7.meaning: When a bad person dies, all their plans and power disappear, leaving nothing behind for them.
christianity_proverbs_11_7.context: This line describes what happens to the hopes of people who live evil and cruel lives.

christianity_proverbs_11_8.meaning: Good people are kept safe from danger, but the wicked person ends up in that same trouble.
christianity_proverbs_11_8.context: The text shows how God protects good people from danger while bad people face the consequences.

christianity_proverbs_11_22.meaning: A person looks good on the outside, but if they act badly, their beauty does not matter.
christianity_proverbs_11_22.context: A gold ring looks nice, but it is useless and dirty when stuck in a pig nose.

christianity_proverbs_11_23.meaning: When you have good intentions, good things happen. When you are mean, trouble and anger will find you.
christianity_proverbs_11_23.context: Good people want good things for themselves and others, while bad people only think about harm.

christianity_proverbs_11_24.meaning: Giving to others helps you grow richer in life. Being too tight with your money leads to real poverty.
christianity_proverbs_11_24.context: One person gives away money freely, while another person is too stingy and keeps everything for themselves.

christianity_proverbs_11_25.meaning: When you give freely to others, life will give back to you. Generosity makes your own life fuller.
christianity_proverbs_11_25.context: A generous person shares their time and resources with others, just like a farmer waters their crops.

christianity_proverbs_11_18.meaning: The moral of this verse is that being wicked and dishonest leads to temporary gains, but eventually, one will face negative consequences. On the other hand, those who act righteously and with integrity will reap a stable and sure reward.
christianity_proverbs_11_18.context: This verse from the Christian Proverbs book talks about the consequences of wicked actions. It mentions that wicked people who engage in deceitful activities will not receive lasting benefits or rewards.

christianity_proverbs_11_19.meaning: That living a righteous life brings joy and prosperity, while engaging in evil deeds leads to suffering and death. It emphasizes the importance of choosing good over evil.
christianity_proverbs_11_19.context: The importance of righteousness and the consequences of evil actions. It says that those who are truly righteous will experience life, while those who engage in evil deeds will face death.

christianity_proverbs_11_20.meaning: The importance of having a pure heart and pleasing God. It contrasts the favor of God with those who have wicked hearts, emphasizing the need to lead a blameless life.
christianity_proverbs_11_20.context: This verse from the Christian Proverbs book discusses the difference between righteous and wicked individuals. It mentions that those with a pure heart are pleasing to God, while those with wicked hearts are detestable to God.

christianity_proverbs_11_21.meaning: This verse warns that evil-doers will face the consequences of their actions and their offspring will also be affected by their choices. It emphasizes the importance of living a righteous life for one's own well-being and the well-being of future generations.
christianity_proverbs_11_21.context: This verse from the Christian Proverbs book talks about the consequences of wicked actions. It says that wicked people will not go unpunished and their descendants will face the same fate.

christianity_proverbs_11_26.meaning: Selfishness brings shame and anger from others. Generosity brings respect and blessings because it helps people survive and thrive.
christianity_proverbs_11_26.context: Hoarding food during hard times hurts others. Sharing supplies brings honor and divine favor to the generous seller.

christianity_proverbs_11_27.meaning: Your focus shapes your life. Seeking good brings favor. Seeking evil brings harm. Choose what you want to attract.
christianity_proverbs_11_27.context: Actively looking for good deeds earns approval. Chasing bad actions leads to trouble and negative consequences for the person.

christianity_proverbs_11_29.meaning: Creating trouble at home wastes your energy. Wise people lead. Foolish people suffer the results of their own bad choices.
christianity_proverbs_11_29.context: Causing chaos in your family leads to loss. The foolish end up serving those who are wise and calm.

christianity_proverbs_11_31.meaning: Justice is certain. If the righteous suffer, the wicked will suffer more. Trust that fairness will eventually prevail for all.
christianity_proverbs_11_31.context: Even good people face hard times on earth. Wicked people will face even greater judgment and consequences for their sins.

christianity_proverbs_12_22.meaning: Always tell the truth because God loves honesty. Lying makes God sad, but being truthful brings joy and peace to your heart.
christianity_proverbs_12_22.context: God hates false speech and lies. He loves people who speak the truth and act with honesty in their daily lives.

christianity_proverbs_12_24.meaning: Work hard today so you can lead your life. Laziness leads to trouble, but effort brings freedom and success for you.
christianity_proverbs_12_24.context: Hard workers gain control over their lives. Lazy people often end up in debt or working for others against their will.

christianity_proverbs_12_27.meaning: Effort brings good rewards. If you work hard, you will enjoy valuable things. Laziness means missing out on good opportunities.
christianity_proverbs_12_27.context: Lazy people do not even cook their food. Hard workers enjoy the valuable results of their effort and careful planning.

christianity_proverbs_13_1.meaning: Listen to wise advice from elders. Accepting correction helps you grow. Ignoring help keeps you stuck in bad habits.
christianity_proverbs_13_1.context: Smart children listen to their parents advice. Foolish people refuse to accept correction and ignore the wisdom of those who care.

christianity_proverbs_12_2.meaning: Doing good brings God's blessing, while planning evil leads to judgment and trouble for the wicked person.
christianity_proverbs_12_2.context: God looks at the heart and rewards those who live with honesty and kindness every day.

christianity_proverbs_12_4.meaning: A good wife brings honor to her home, but a bad wife causes deep pain and ruin.
christianity_proverbs_12_4.context: A wife's character greatly affects her husband's life, bringing either pride or deep shame to him.

christianity_proverbs_12_9.meaning: It is better to be humble and have help than to be proud but have no food.
christianity_proverbs_12_9.context: Some people seek fame but have nothing, while others work hard with help and have enough to eat.

christianity_proverbs_12_11.meaning: Hard work brings real food, while chasing empty dreams shows a lack of sense and leads to poverty.
christianity_proverbs_12_11.context: Working hard on your farm gives you food, but dreaming about easy riches leads to hunger and loss.

christianity_proverbs_12_12.meaning: The verse teaches us that wicked people focus on evil deeds and the rewards they bring, while righteous people grow in wisdom and goodness. Following righteousness leads to a prosperous life.
christianity_proverbs_12_12.context: This verse from the Christian book of Proverbs (12:12) talks about the contrast between wicked people and righteous people. Wicked people desire to benefit from the evil actions of others, while the righteous person's foundation or roots grow strong and prosper.

christianity_proverbs_12_14.meaning: That a person's happiness comes from doing good and experiencing the results of their efforts. Hard work and righteous actions bring rewards.
christianity_proverbs_12_14.context: Proverbs 12:14 (Christianity) describes the satisfaction a person gets from good deeds and the consequences of their actions.

christianity_proverbs_12_15.meaning: The verse emphasizes the value of seeking guidance and considering the opinions of others. Being wise involves listening to counsel and adjusting one's perspective.
christianity_proverbs_12_15.context: Proverbs 12:15 (Christianity) highlights the importance of seeking advice and wisdom.

christianity_proverbs_12_16.meaning: The verse teaches that being patient and ignoring insults contributes to maintaining harmony and avoiding unnecessary conflicts. Being wise involves controlling one's emotions and choosing forgiveness.
christianity_proverbs_12_16.context: Proverbs 12:16 (Christianity) talks about handling conflicts and maintaining peace.

christianity_proverbs_13_8.meaning: Money can buy safety for the rich, but the poor must face threats without any financial protection.
christianity_proverbs_13_8.context: Rich people can pay to avoid trouble, but poor people have no money to bribe officials.

christianity_proverbs_13_11.meaning: Money made by lying or stealing will disappear quickly, but honest work helps your savings grow steadily.
christianity_proverbs_13_11.context: This verse compares how money gained through cheating versus honest hard work behaves over time.

christianity_proverbs_13_12.meaning: Long waits can make you feel sad, but when your hopes come true, it feels like new life.
christianity_proverbs_13_12.context: Waiting for something you really want can feel painful, but finally getting it brings great joy.

christianity_proverbs_13_14.meaning: Learning from wise people gives you fresh strength and helps you avoid choices that lead to ruin.
christianity_proverbs_13_14.context: Wise teachers share knowledge that helps people avoid dangerous traps and make better life choices.

christianity_proverbs_13_15.meaning: Being wise and kind helps you win friends. Ignoring truth makes your life much harder to live.
christianity_proverbs_13_15.context: This verse compares two different life paths. One path uses wisdom, while the other ignores truth.

christianity_proverbs_13_16.meaning: Smart people learn before they act. Foolish people show their lack of sense by acting rashly.
christianity_proverbs_13_16.context: The text contrasts smart people who think first with foolish people who act without thinking.

christianity_proverbs_13_18.meaning: Refusing to learn leads to shame and loss. Listening to advice brings you respect and honor.
christianity_proverbs_13_18.context: This proverb warns about the results of refusing to learn or accept help from others.

christianity_proverbs_13_19.meaning: Getting what you want feels good. But foolish people hate giving up their bad choices.
christianity_proverbs_13_19.context: The verse describes the joy of getting what you want and the pain of staying in bad habits.

christianity_proverbs_13_2.meaning: By choosing good words and speaking positively, a person can experience blessings and happiness. On the other hand, the unfaithful person who talks violently will face difficulties.
christianity_proverbs_13_2.context: The importance of choosing good words and avoiding harmful speech.

christianity_proverbs_13_3.meaning: Guarding one's mouth means being careful with the words we speak. By doing so, we protect our own well-being. However, those who talk excessively or without thinking will face problems.
christianity_proverbs_13_3.context: The significance of controlling one's tongue and being mindful of what they say. It warns that those who talk excessively or without thought will face consequences.

christianity_proverbs_13_4.meaning: The lazy person desires many things but never gains them. In contrast, the person who works hard will achieve their desires and find satisfaction.
christianity_proverbs_13_4.context: That those who are diligent in their efforts will achieve their desires.

christianity_proverbs_13_7.meaning: There are individuals who show off their wealth but actually lack true riches. On the other hand, those who humbly acknowledge their poverty can possess invaluable wisdom and blessings.
christianity_proverbs_13_7.context: This verse from Proverbs contrasts two types of people: those who pretend to be rich but lack true wealth, and those who pretend to be poor but possess true riches within themselves.

christianity_proverbs_14_7.meaning: Staying away from foolish people helps you maintain wisdom and knowledge. Choose companions who value learning and growth.
christianity_proverbs_14_7.context: The importance of seeking wisdom from wise individuals.

christianity_proverbs_14_9.meaning: Differentiating between wise and foolish people. Wise individuals embrace forgiveness, while fools reject it.
christianity_proverbs_14_9.context: The focus is on the contrast between foolish individuals who mock atonement for sins and the righteous who seek forgiveness and reconciliation. It highlights the importance of understanding and embracing forgiveness.

christianity_proverbs_14_11.meaning: Destruction awaits the wicked, while the righteous enjoy prosperity and success.
christianity_proverbs_14_11.context: This verse from Proverbs discusses the consequences of wickedness and righteousness. It talks about the downfall of wicked dwellings and the prosperity of righteous dwellings.

christianity_proverbs_14_12.meaning: Be cautious of following blindly. Wise decisions consider outcomes and the path they lead.
christianity_proverbs_14_12.context: The importance of considering the outcomes of our choices.

christianity_proverbs_13_21.meaning: The verse teaches us that living a sinful life brings difficulties and negative outcomes, while being righteous and following God's teachings leads to blessings and success.
christianity_proverbs_13_21.context: This verse from the Bible, found in Proverbs 13:21, talks about the consequences of sin and righteousness. In the story, misfortune follows those who commit sins, while those who lead a righteous life experience prosperity.

christianity_proverbs_13_22.meaning: Us that doing good deeds and passing on values to future generations brings blessings, while accumulating wealth without righteousness results in it being inherited by the righteous.
christianity_proverbs_13_22.context: Proverbs 13:22 is a biblical verse that discusses the consequences of one's actions. It mentions a good person passing on their values and wealth to their descendants, while a sinner's wealth is stored for the righteous.

christianity_proverbs_13_24.meaning: Us that loving children involves guiding and disciplining them, while neglecting to do so can lead to negative outcomes for both the child and the family.
christianity_proverbs_13_24.context: Proverbs 13:24 tells us about the importance of discipline and the consequences of parental actions. In this verse, sparing the rod (disciplining a child) is associated with love for one's children, while not disciplining them leads to destruction.

christianity_proverbs_14_1.meaning: The significance of wisdom and righteousness in shaping our lives and the well-being of our families.
christianity_proverbs_14_1.context: Proverbs 14:1 speaks about the contrast between a wise woman and a foolish woman. The verse highlights the importance of wisdom in building a strong family and a prosperous life.

christianity_proverbs_14_2.meaning: In simple terms, this verse says that people who live good lives and follow God will be afraid of God, while those who don't follow God will not care about Him. It teaches us the importance of living righteously and respecting God.
christianity_proverbs_14_2.context: This verse from the Christian book of Proverbs (14:2) talks about the difference between a righteous person and a wicked person. It mentions that a righteous person who lives according to God's teachings (Yahweh) will fear or respect God, while a wicked person who does not follow God's ways will disrespect Him.

christianity_proverbs_14_3.meaning: Us that being wise and thinking before we speak can protect us from problems. On the other hand, foolish talk can lead to trouble.
christianity_proverbs_14_3.context: Proverbs 14:3 is a verse from the Christian Bible that highlights the consequences of foolish talk and wise talk. It mentions that foolish people who speak without thinking can get into trouble, while wise people who speak carefully protect themselves.

christianity_proverbs_14_4.meaning: This verse from the Bible talks about the value of hard work. When people don't work, the place remains clean. But when people work hard, it leads to more growth and prosperity.
christianity_proverbs_14_4.context: Proverbs 14:4 is a verse from the Christian Bible that discusses the importance of hard work and its rewards. It says that when there are no oxen (animals used for plowing) around, the place will be clean, but with the strength of oxen, there will be a lot of increase in crops.

christianity_proverbs_14_5.meaning: Us the value of honesty. People who tell the truth are trustworthy, while those who lie will be known for spreading false information.
christianity_proverbs_14_5.context: Proverbs 14:5 is a verse from the Christian Bible that emphasizes the importance of telling the truth. It says that a truthful person will not lie, while a deceitful person will spread lies.

christianity_proverbs_14_20.meaning: True friends stay with you in hard times, not just when you have plenty of cash.
christianity_proverbs_14_20.context: People often ignore the poor but gather around those who have money and power.

christianity_proverbs_14_23.meaning: Hard work brings real rewards, but empty promises and idle chatter lead to having nothing at all.
christianity_proverbs_14_23.context: This verse compares the results of doing real work versus just talking about what you will do.

christianity_proverbs_14_24.meaning: Smart choices lead to a good life, but acting silly only makes your problems much worse.
christianity_proverbs_14_24.context: Wisdom brings true honor and wealth, while foolishness only brings more shame and bad decisions.

christianity_proverbs_14_25.meaning: Honest words protect people and save lives, while lying tricks others and causes real harm.
christianity_proverbs_14_25.context: This speaks about the power of telling the truth in court or when judging right from wrong.

christianity_proverbs_14_15.meaning: Do not believe everything you hear. Take your time to think carefully about your choices before you make them.
christianity_proverbs_14_15.context: This verse compares two types of people. One trusts too easily, while the other thinks before acting.

christianity_proverbs_14_16.meaning: Being wise means staying away from bad things. Being foolish means acting on impulse without thinking about the results.
christianity_proverbs_14_16.context: The text contrasts a wise person with a foolish one. The wise person avoids danger, but the fool acts without care.

christianity_proverbs_14_17.meaning: Anger makes you do stupid things. People who are sneaky or crafty are not liked by others because they are not honest.
christianity_proverbs_14_17.context: This line warns about anger and trickery. It says that getting mad fast leads to mistakes, and schemers are disliked.

christianity_proverbs_14_18.meaning: If you are not careful, you will make mistakes. If you are thoughtful, you will gain true understanding and respect.
christianity_proverbs_14_18.context: The verse looks at the results of being simple versus being careful. The simple get into trouble, but the careful gain wisdom.

christianity_proverbs_14_26.meaning: When you truly respect God, you feel safe and protected, and your family will find shelter in that trust.
christianity_proverbs_14_26.context: This verse talks about how respecting God gives you a safe place to hide from danger.

christianity_proverbs_14_27.meaning: Respecting God gives you true life and helps you avoid the deadly traps that sin sets for you.
christianity_proverbs_14_27.context: The writer compares God to a spring of water that keeps people alive and away from traps.

christianity_proverbs_14_28.meaning: A leader is strong when people support him, but he becomes weak and fails when he has no followers.
christianity_proverbs_14_28.context: This part explains that a king looks powerful when many people support him and follow his lead.

christianity_proverbs_14_34.meaning: When a nation does what is right, it rises in honor, but when it sins, it becomes a source of shame.
christianity_proverbs_14_34.context: This verse looks at how the moral choices of a whole country affect its standing among other nations.

christianity_proverbs_15_20.meaning: Being wise brings joy to family; being foolish hurts loved ones and shows disrespect.
christianity_proverbs_15_20.context: A smart son makes his dad happy, while a foolish man hurts his mom.

christianity_proverbs_15_22.meaning: Seek good advice and teamwork to make plans work and avoid failure.
christianity_proverbs_15_22.context: Without advice, plans break; with many helpers, plans succeed.

christianity_proverbs_15_24.meaning: Choosing wise actions keeps you safe and away from harmful or dark places.
christianity_proverbs_15_24.context: Wise people walk a safe path that keeps them from falling into danger.

christianity_proverbs_15_25.meaning: Pride leads to loss, but God cares for the vulnerable and keeps them safe.
christianity_proverbs_15_25.context: God removes the homes of the proud but protects the widow’s home.

christianity_proverbs_15_10.meaning: If you refuse to listen when others correct you, you will likely face severe negative consequences.
christianity_proverbs_15_10.context: This verse warns that ignoring wise advice leads to serious trouble and bad outcomes.

christianity_proverbs_15_12.meaning: People who laugh at advice will never seek out wise people to help them grow better.
christianity_proverbs_15_12.context: A person who mocks others refuses to accept any criticism or helpful feedback from anyone.

christianity_proverbs_15_14.meaning: A wise heart always wants to learn more, but a foolish mind only consumes bad ideas.
christianity_proverbs_15_14.context: Smart people actively look for new information, while foolish people only talk about nonsense.

christianity_proverbs_15_16.meaning: It is better to have less money but live peacefully than to be rich but full of worry.
christianity_proverbs_15_16.context: This compares having a small amount of money with having a lot of money and stress.

christianity_proverbs_15_1.meaning: The verse teaches us that choosing a gentle and understanding response can defuse conflicts and maintain peaceful relationships. On the other hand, being harsh and insensitive can escalate conflicts and harm connections.
christianity_proverbs_15_1.context:
This verse is from the Christian book of Proverbs, written by Solomon. It talks about the impact of our words on others and how they can either calm or inflame conflicts.
For example, imagine two people arguing over a disagreement. One person responds calmly and kindly, while the other person speaks harshly. The first person's gentle answer will likely make the other person feel understood and less angry, while the second person's harsh words will only make the situation worse.

christianity_proverbs_15_2.meaning: Us that being wise and knowledgeable in our conversations can lead to productive discussions, while being foolish and unthinking can result in pointless debates.
christianity_proverbs_15_2.context:
This verse is also from the Christian book of Proverbs, discussing the importance of wisdom and knowledge in communication.
Imagine two people discussing a topic. One person speaks knowledgeably and intelligently, while the other person talks recklessly and without thought.
The first person's wise words contribute to a meaningful conversation, while the second person's foolish statements only lead to a pointless discussion.

christianity_proverbs_15_3.meaning: God is all-knowing and always watching us. We should act with consideration for His presence and strive to do what is right.
christianity_proverbs_15_3.context:
This verse is from the Christian book of Proverbs, highlighting the omniscience of God and His watchful presence.
Imagine a person who is being watched by everyone around them. Yahweh, the God of the Bible, is mentioned as watching everyone's actions and thoughts.
This verse emphasizes that God is aware of everything we do and that we should behave accordingly.

christianity_proverbs_15_5.meaning: Us that seeking guidance from experienced people can lead to wiser decisions and that being stubborn prevents us from growing and learning.
christianity_proverbs_15_5.context:
This verse is also from the Christian book of Proverbs, discussing the importance of listening to wisdom and learning from others.
Imagine a person who disregards advice from their parents or elders and chooses to act foolishly.
This verse highlights the value of seeking wisdom from experienced individuals and not being stubborn.

christianity_proverbs_16_4.meaning: That God has a plan for everything, even for wicked people. Their actions may lead to punishment, but they are still part of God's bigger plan.
christianity_proverbs_16_4.context: This verse is from the Christian Bible, specifically Proverbs 16:4. It talks about how God has created everything with a purpose, even the wicked people for the day of trouble or evil.

christianity_proverbs_16_5.meaning: That being proud goes against God's will. Proud people will face punishment as God does not favor such attitudes.
christianity_proverbs_16_5.context: Proverbs 16:5 is a verse from the Christian Bible. It highlights that God disapproves of people with a proud heart and they will face consequences.

christianity_proverbs_16_9.meaning: That a person's thoughts and decisions originate from their heart. However, ultimately, God influences and controls their actions.
christianity_proverbs_16_9.context: Proverbs 16:9 is a verse from the Christian Bible. It states that a person's intentions are formed in their heart, but God ultimately guides their actions.

christianity_proverbs_16_10.meaning: This verse advises that a leader, such as a king, should make decisions based on justice and not let personal feelings influence their judgments.
christianity_proverbs_16_10.context: Proverbs 16:10 is a verse from the Christian Bible. It says that a king's decisions should be based on fair judgments and not personal bias.

christianity_proverbs_15_26.meaning: In simple words, this verse means that God disapproves of bad thoughts and actions. On the other hand, He values and is happy with good thoughts and actions of righteous people. Being pure-hearted is pleasing to God.
christianity_proverbs_15_26.context: This verse is from the Christian Bible, specifically Proverbs 15:26. It talks about Yahweh, the God of the Hebrews, disliking the thoughts and intentions of evil or wicked people, while appreciating and being pleased with those of the righteous and pure-hearted individuals.

christianity_proverbs_15_27.meaning: This verse means that seeking wealth at the expense of family leads to problems at home. On the other hand, avoiding bribes brings happiness and a good life.
christianity_proverbs_15_27.context: Proverbs 15:27 in the Christian Bible talks about the consequences of greed and accepting bribes. It highlights that those who seek gain at the cost of their family will face problems within their house, while those who refuse bribes will enjoy a peaceful life.

christianity_proverbs_15_29.meaning: This verse tells us that God is distant from people who do evil. However, He is close to those who lead a righteous life and pray to Him.
christianity_proverbs_15_29.context: Proverbs 15:29 in the Christian Bible discusses Yahweh's distance from wicked people and closeness to the righteous. It emphasizes that God is far from evil individuals, but hears and answers the prayers of the righteous.

christianity_proverbs_15_31.meaning: The value of listening to advice and learning from others. Those who accept guidance and grow from their experiences will have a fulfilling and successful life.
christianity_proverbs_15_31.context: Proverbs 15:32 in the Christian Bible talks about the importance of listening to advice and learning from others. It says that those who accept correction and learn from others will live a long and prosperous life.

christianity_proverbs_15_32.meaning: Learning from advice and criticism helps us grow and understand life better. Ignoring it harms our development and shows a lack of respect for ourselves.
christianity_proverbs_15_32.context: This verse from the Christian book of Proverbs talks about the importance of accepting advice and correction. It mentions that those who refuse guidance are showing disrespect for themselves, while those who listen and learn from reproof gain wisdom.

christianity_proverbs_16_1.meaning: Our thoughts and decisions stem from our hearts, but ultimately, God reveals our true motives and intentions.
christianity_proverbs_16_1.context: That human intentions and decisions come from within, but ultimately, God reveals their true intentions.

christianity_proverbs_16_2.meaning: We tend to think our actions are perfect, but God evaluates the true intentions behind them.
christianity_proverbs_16_2.context: That a person often overestimates the goodness of their actions in their own eyes. God, however, evaluates the true intentions behind our actions.

christianity_proverbs_16_3.meaning: By entrusting our plans to God, we can have confidence in His guidance, leading to successful outcomes.
christianity_proverbs_16_3.context: This verse from the Christian book of Proverbs encourages us to entrust our plans and actions to God, trusting that He will guide them to success.

christianity_proverbs_16_11.meaning: Being honest with measurements ensures fair trade and reflects God's values. Trust in His guidance for success.
christianity_proverbs_16_11.context: This verse is from the Christian book of Proverbs, written by Solomon. It talks about the importance of honest measurements and weights in trade and commerce, as they are created and controlled by God.

christianity_proverbs_16_15.meaning: Having the king's favor brings blessings and is like the life-giving rain of spring; be humble and seek to please others.
christianity_proverbs_16_15.context: This verse is also from the Christian book of Proverbs. It emphasizes the value of a king's favor, comparing it to the life-giving rain of spring.

christianity_proverbs_16_17.meaning: Staying away from evil and following one's path ensures personal well-being and protection.
christianity_proverbs_16_17.context: This verse is from the Christian book of Proverbs. It advises choosing the right path by avoiding evil and preserving one's soul.

christianity_proverbs_16_18.meaning: Pride leads to downfall; humility is essential for a good life.
christianity_proverbs_16_18.context: This verse is also from the Christian book of Proverbs. It highlights the danger of pride and the importance of humility before falling.

christianity_proverbs_16_20.meaning: Listening to God's Word and putting your trust in Him brings prosperity and happiness. Ignoring or distrusting Him leads to trouble.
christianity_proverbs_16_20.context: This verse is from the Christian book of Proverbs, written by King Solomon. It talks about the importance of listening to and trusting in God's Word for prosperity and blessings.

christianity_proverbs_16_22.meaning: Having wisdom and understanding is beneficial, while foolishness brings punishment and foolishness.
christianity_proverbs_16_22.context: Proverbs 16:22 is part of a collection of wisdom teachings from King Solomon. It emphasizes the value of wisdom and understanding in life.

christianity_proverbs_16_24.meaning: Speaking kindly and positively brings joy and healing to the soul, much like honeycomb brings nourishment to the body.
christianity_proverbs_16_24.context: The power of pleasant words and their positive impact on one's soul and overall well-being.

christianity_proverbs_16_25.meaning: Trusting in one's own path may seem right, but ultimately leads to destruction and disappointment.
christianity_proverbs_16_25.context: Proverbs 16:25 is part of a collection of wisdom teachings from King Solomon. It warns about following one's own way instead of seeking God's guidance.

christianity_proverbs_16_26.meaning: The verse emphasizes that a person's hard work contributes to their achievements. It encourages us to be persistent and diligent in our endeavors.
christianity_proverbs_16_26.context: The importance of perseverance and diligence.

christianity_proverbs_16_27.meaning: This verse from the Bible (Proverbs 16:27) cautions about the harmful intentions of a worthless person. It reminds us to be mindful of the words we use and the impact they can have.
christianity_proverbs_16_27.context: Proverbs 16:27 (Christianity) describes a worthless person who plans evil deeds through their words. It sets a warning about the destructive power of gossip and deceit.

christianity_proverbs_16_29.meaning: A person uses deceitful tactics to mislead others. It warns us about the risks of being easily influenced and the importance of making our own decisions.
christianity_proverbs_16_29.context: Proverbs 16:29 (Christianity) talks about a person who uses manipulation to lead others astray. It highlights the danger of being led astray by others.

christianity_proverbs_16_30.meaning: This verse from the Bible (Proverbs 16:30) warns about someone who deceives others subtly. It encourages us to be aware of the intentions behind people's actions and not be easily fooled.
christianity_proverbs_16_30.context: Proverbs 16:30 (Christianity) describes a person who deceives others through subtle actions. It advises us to be cautious of hidden intentions.

christianity_proverbs_16_33.meaning: Even when things seem random, God is in control. You can trust that He guides your life path.
christianity_proverbs_16_33.context: People used to toss lots to make choices, but the book says God truly decides the final outcome.

christianity_proverbs_17_2.meaning: Good character matters more than bloodline. A smart and kind person earns respect and a fair share.
christianity_proverbs_17_2.context: A wise servant is better than a foolish son who brings shame to the family name and honor.

christianity_proverbs_17_3.meaning: Hard times test your character. God uses trials to help you grow stronger and become a better person.
christianity_proverbs_17_3.context: Metal workers use heat to remove impurities from silver and gold, making the metal pure and strong.

christianity_proverbs_17_4.meaning: You become like the people you listen to. Choose good friends who will help you grow in the right way.
christianity_proverbs_17_4.context: Bad people naturally listen to other bad people because they share the same wrong and harmful views.

christianity_proverbs_17_6.meaning: The verse emphasizes the value of children in the lives of their parents, especially elderly ones. Children's success brings glory to their parents, reinforcing the importance of family and intergenerational bonds.
christianity_proverbs_17_6.context: This verse is from the Christian book of Proverbs, written by Solomon. It talks about the importance of children for elderly parents and how their achievements bring honor to their parents.

christianity_proverbs_17_7.meaning: The verse highlights that arrogance and dishonesty are inappropriate traits for someone, especially for someone in a position of authority like a prince. Being humble and truthful is essential for any individual, regardless of their status.
christianity_proverbs_17_7.context: This verse is also from the Christian book of Proverbs, discussing the unfitness of arrogance and lying for a fool or a prince.

christianity_proverbs_17_8.meaning: The verse explains that giving a bribe can be highly appealing, but it ultimately leads to detrimental outcomes for the person involved. Honesty and integrity should be prioritized over material gain.
christianity_proverbs_17_8.context: This verse is from the Christian book of Proverbs, describing the allure and consequences of bribery.

christianity_proverbs_17_10.meaning: The verse indicates that receiving advice or correction is more beneficial than receiving numerous physical punishments. Being open to learning and understanding is crucial for personal growth and development.
christianity_proverbs_17_10.context: This verse is also from the Christian book of Proverbs, emphasizing the importance of wisdom and learning from criticism.

christianity_proverbs_17_11.meaning: The verse teaches us to avoid dealing with or associating with evil people, as they will only cause trouble. Instead, we should focus on positive interactions and relationships.
christianity_proverbs_17_11.context: This verse is from the Christian book of Proverbs, written by Solomon. It talks about an evil person who constantly causes trouble and stirs up conflicts. In this context, a 'cruel messenger' refers to someone sent to deal with or punish that evil person.

christianity_proverbs_17_12.meaning: This verse advises us to avoid interacting with foolish individuals, as they can cause harm or danger. Instead, we should focus on positive relationships and surround ourselves with wise people.
christianity_proverbs_17_12.context: This verse is also from the Christian book of Proverbs. It suggests that it is better to encounter a bear that has lost her cubs than to meet a foolish person who keeps making mistakes. The imagery highlights the danger of dealing with foolish people.

christianity_proverbs_17_13.meaning: The verse teaches us to respond to negative actions with positive actions, not more negativity. Retaliation only fuels more conflict and does not resolve issues.
christianity_proverbs_17_13.context: This verse is from the Christian book of Proverbs. It talks about the consequences of retaliating with evil when good intentions are met with evil. The phrase 'evil for good' represents returning evil deeds with more evil deeds.

christianity_proverbs_17_14.meaning: The verse emphasizes the importance of avoiding conflicts and disputes, as they can lead to unnecessary suffering and harm. Instead, we should focus on peaceful resolutions and positive interactions.
christianity_proverbs_17_14.context: This verse is from the Christian book of Proverbs. It compares starting a conflict to breaking a dam, which can cause great damage. The verse advises against engaging in unnecessary disputes.

christianity_proverbs_17_19.meaning: Choosing to break rules causes endless conflict. People who ignore wisdom will face serious trouble and lose their peace.
christianity_proverbs_17_19.context: This verse warns that loving rebellion leads to constant fighting and ruin for those who seek it.

christianity_proverbs_17_20.meaning: Bad thoughts and lies stop you from succeeding. Being dishonest leads to trouble and keeps you from finding true happiness.
christianity_proverbs_17_20.context: This saying shows that having a twisted heart and lying tongue brings bad results for the person.

christianity_proverbs_17_21.meaning: Raising a foolish child brings great sorrow. Parents lose their joy when their offspring ignore good advice and wisdom.
christianity_proverbs_17_21.context: This verse describes the deep sadness a parent feels when their child refuses to learn right from wrong.

christianity_proverbs_17_23.meaning: Taking bribes ruins fairness for everyone. Secret payments destroy justice and hurt innocent people who need help and protection.
christianity_proverbs_17_23.context: This text explains how corrupt people take secret money to twist the law and hide the truth.

christianity_proverbs_17_25.meaning: Bad behavior from a child causes real pain and sorrow for the people who raised them.
christianity_proverbs_17_25.context: A parent feels deep sadness when their child acts badly and ignores good advice.

christianity_proverbs_17_26.meaning: It is wrong to punish good people or leaders just because they are honest and fair.
christianity_proverbs_17_26.context: This verse talks about how leaders should treat people who are doing the right thing.

christianity_proverbs_18_1.meaning: Staying isolated shows selfishness and means you ignore the wise advice of the community.
christianity_proverbs_18_1.context: Some people choose to stay alone and refuse to talk or work with others.

christianity_proverbs_18_2.meaning: Fools only want to share their own views and do not care about actually learning.
christianity_proverbs_18_2.context: A foolish person does not care about learning new things or understanding the truth.

christianity_proverbs_17_15.meaning: That God disapproves of judges who favor the wicked over the righteous and punish the innocent. It emphasizes the importance of fair judgment and upholding justice.
christianity_proverbs_17_15.context: This verse from Proverbs 17:15 in Christianity talks about two situations. In the first, a judge or judge's decision favors an unjust person (wicked), while in the second, a judge or judge's decision punishes an innocent person (righteous). Both of these actions are considered detestable or abhorrent to God.

christianity_proverbs_17_16.meaning: The foolishness of spending money on wisdom when one lacks understanding. It teaches that true wisdom comes from seeking knowledge and growing in understanding, rather than simply spending resources.
christianity_proverbs_17_16.context: Proverbs 17:16 is a verse from the Christian Bible, specifically in the book of Proverbs. It discusses a foolish person having money to buy wisdom, which seems contradictory because they lack understanding.

christianity_proverbs_17_17.meaning: The importance of true friendship, where friends stand by each other in both good times and bad times. It teaches the value of loyalty, trust, and unconditional love in relationships.
christianity_proverbs_17_17.context: Proverbs 17:17 is a verse from the Christian Bible, specifically in the book of Proverbs. It talks about the deep bond between friends who support each other through good and bad times.

christianity_proverbs_17_18.meaning: The dangers of blindly agreeing to participate in risky or harmful situations without considering the potential outcomes. It teaches the importance of making informed decisions and avoiding unnecessary risks.
christianity_proverbs_17_18.context: Proverbs 17:18 is a verse from the Christian Bible, specifically in the book of Proverbs. It discusses a person who agrees to be involved in a risky or harmful situation without fully understanding the consequences.

christianity_proverbs_18_13.meaning: Be cautious before responding to situations or answering questions. Take time to understand the matter before speaking or making decisions.
christianity_proverbs_18_13.context: This verse is from the Christian book of Proverbs, written by Solomon. It talks about making hasty decisions without considering all aspects first.

christianity_proverbs_18_16.meaning: Developing skills and talents can lead to opportunities and success in life.
christianity_proverbs_18_16.context: This verse is also from the Christian book of Proverbs. It highlights the importance of having talents or gifts that can open doors for a person and help him interact with influential people.

christianity_proverbs_18_17.meaning: Seeking fairness and allowing others to share their perspectives is essential in resolving conflicts.
christianity_proverbs_18_17.context: This verse is from the same Christian book of Proverbs. It emphasizes the importance of fairness in resolving conflicts and allows both parties to present their cases.

christianity_proverbs_18_18.meaning: Resolving conflicts can involve external factors or methods, but understanding and empathy are also crucial.
christianity_proverbs_18_18.context: This verse is from the Christian book of Proverbs. It mentions the role of fate or destiny in resolving disputes, using a lot or a method of deciding between parties.

christianity_proverbs_18_8.meaning: Be cautious about the words you share, especially those that involve spreading rumors or negative information, as they can deeply impact others' thoughts and behavior.
christianity_proverbs_18_8.context: This verse from the Christian book of Proverbs talks about the harmful effects of gossip. It compares the appealing nature of gossip to the taste of sweet food that goes straight to a person's innermost thoughts and actions.

christianity_proverbs_18_9.meaning: Effort and dedication in your work are essential for personal growth and success. Avoid being lazy as it may lead to negative associations with harmful individuals.
christianity_proverbs_18_9.context: The importance of diligence in one's work. It suggests that a person who is lazy in their tasks is similar to someone who is dangerous and causes harm.

christianity_proverbs_18_10.meaning: Trust in God and rely on His strength for protection and peace. God's name represents His power and guidance, providing safety and security for those who seek refuge in Him.
christianity_proverbs_18_10.context: The sanctity of God's name, Yahweh. It compares seeking refuge in God to finding safety within a strong tower.

christianity_proverbs_18_11.meaning: Understand that wealth and material possessions do not bring true security or happiness. Focus on building a strong relationship with God and living a virtuous life.
christianity_proverbs_18_11.context: The temporary and fragile nature of material possessions.

christianity_proverbs_18_3.meaning: The verse teaches us to avoid wicked actions and instead promote righteousness. By doing so, we can prevent negative reactions from others and maintain our own honor.
christianity_proverbs_18_3.context: This verse from the Christian book of Proverbs talks about the consequences of allowing wickedness to exist. It mentions that when wickedness occurs, both contempt and disgrace will also happen.

christianity_proverbs_18_5.meaning: The verse emphasizes the need for fairness and justice. By not showing partiality to the wicked and giving due rights to the innocent, we uphold moral values and build trust among people.
christianity_proverbs_18_5.context: The importance of fairness and treating everyone equally.

christianity_proverbs_18_6.meaning: The verse cautions against engaging in foolish talk and disputes. It teaches us to be mindful of our words and avoid causing harm to ourselves and others.
christianity_proverbs_18_6.context: This verse from Proverbs warns that a fool's words can lead to conflicts and trouble. It suggests that a fool's mouth can become a trap for their own soul.

christianity_proverbs_18_7.meaning: The verse advises against foolish decisions and behaviors. It reminds us to think before acting and choose wisely, as foolish choices can harm us and our lives.
christianity_proverbs_18_7.context: That a fool's actions can lead to their own downfall.

christianity_proverbs_18_19.meaning: Holding a grudge against a loved one hurts your soul much more than any outside enemy.
christianity_proverbs_18_19.context: Angry fights between close family members can cause deep and lasting emotional pain.

christianity_proverbs_18_20.meaning: Your words and thoughts feed your mind, so positive speech brings you true inner peace.
christianity_proverbs_18_20.context: What you say and think shapes your daily life and your inner feelings.

christianity_proverbs_18_22.meaning: A good marriage is a blessing that shows God is happy and pleased with your life.
christianity_proverbs_18_22.context: Finding a good partner is seen as a special gift from God in this verse.

christianity_proverbs_18_23.meaning: People with money often ignore the needy, while the poor must beg for basic kindness.
christianity_proverbs_18_23.context: The unfair gap between how the poor and rich are treated.

christianity_proverbs_18_24.meaning: One true friend who stays loyal is far more valuable than a large group of shallow acquaintances.
christianity_proverbs_18_24.context: This verse warns that having many casual friends can actually lead to your downfall and ruin.

christianity_proverbs_19_1.meaning: Living with honesty and good character is much better than being wealthy but full of lies and foolishness.
christianity_proverbs_19_1.context: The writer compares a poor person who is honest with a rich person who lies often.

christianity_proverbs_19_2.meaning: You need to think carefully before acting, or you will make mistakes and end up lost.
christianity_proverbs_19_2.context: This advice tells people not to rush into action just because they feel excited or eager.

christianity_proverbs_19_3.meaning: When people act stupidly, they hurt themselves and become angry at God for their own bad decisions.
christianity_proverbs_19_3.context: This line describes how a foolish person makes bad choices that ruin their own life path.

christianity_proverbs_19_4.meaning: Money can attract many people to you, but it does not guarantee true friendship or loyalty.
christianity_proverbs_19_4.context: Rich people often have many social connections, while poor people often feel alone and left out.

christianity_proverbs_19_6.meaning: Many people act friendly only because they want something, so their kindness is not real.
christianity_proverbs_19_6.context: People often try to please leaders or those with power to get what they want.

christianity_proverbs_19_7.meaning: True friends stay by your side even when you have nothing, but many leave when you need help.
christianity_proverbs_19_7.context: When someone becomes poor, even their own family and close friends often stop visiting them.

christianity_proverbs_19_10.meaning: Leaders need to be wise and careful, because foolish decisions can cause great harm to others.
christianity_proverbs_19_10.context: This verse warns that unwise people should not hold high positions of power or authority.

christianity_proverbs_19_16.meaning: Obeying good rules keeps you safe and healthy. Disrespecting them brings serious trouble and leads to a bad end.
christianity_proverbs_19_16.context: This verse warns that ignoring rules leads to harm while following them protects your life and well being.

christianity_proverbs_19_17.meaning: When you help poor people, God notices your kindness. He will bless you and give you good things in return.
christianity_proverbs_19_17.context: Helping those who have no money is like lending to God himself. He sees your kindness and will repay you.

christianity_proverbs_19_18.meaning: Teaching kids rules gives them a good future. Ignoring their mistakes can lead to serious harm or death.
christianity_proverbs_19_18.context: Parents must teach their children right from wrong. If you ignore bad behavior, you risk your child's future safety.

christianity_proverbs_19_19.meaning: Angry people face trouble for their actions. Helping them repeatedly does not fix their anger or stop the problems.
christianity_proverbs_19_19.context: Angry people cause trouble and must face consequences. Saving them once often means you will have to save them again.

christianity_proverbs_19_11.meaning: True honor comes from staying calm and forgiving others when they hurt you rather than getting angry.
christianity_proverbs_19_11.context: A wise person controls their temper and chooses to ignore insults instead of fighting back.

christianity_proverbs_19_13.meaning: Bad behavior in family members brings deep sorrow and endless stress to those who love them.
christianity_proverbs_19_13.context: A foolish child causes great trouble for his parents while a quarrelsome wife creates constant noise.

christianity_proverbs_19_14.meaning: Material wealth is inherited but finding a good partner is a special blessing from the divine source.
christianity_proverbs_19_14.context: Money and houses come from your parents but a wise and good wife is a gift from God.

christianity_proverbs_19_15.meaning: If you do not work hard you will face poverty and hunger because effort is required for success.
christianity_proverbs_19_15.context: Being lazy leads to excessive sleeping while an idle person will eventually go hungry and poor.

christianity_proverbs_19_20.meaning: Listening to good advice helps you make smart choices today so you can live wisely and happily in your later years.
christianity_proverbs_19_20.context: This verse advises young people to listen to wise elders and accept their guidance for a better future.

christianity_proverbs_19_22.meaning: Being kind makes people like you more than money does. It is better to be poor and honest than rich and dishonest.
christianity_proverbs_19_22.context: This saying compares the value of kindness against wealth and truthfulness against lying in social relationships.

christianity_proverbs_19_23.meaning: Respecting God brings peace and safety to your life. You will feel calm and protected from many troubles and worries.
christianity_proverbs_19_23.context: This verse describes the peaceful life that comes from respecting God and following his ways with trust.

christianity_proverbs_19_24.meaning: Extreme laziness makes people too weak to do even the simplest tasks. Hard work is needed to sustain life and health.
christianity_proverbs_19_24.context: This image shows a lazy person who is too tired to even lift food from the plate to eat.

christianity_proverbs_20_1.meaning: Staying sober helps you think clearly. Getting drunk leads to bad choices and foolish behavior.
christianity_proverbs_20_1.context: This verse warns that drinking too much alcohol makes people act silly and start fights.

christianity_proverbs_20_2.meaning: Do not anger powerful leaders. Their rage can destroy your life, so always show respect.
christianity_proverbs_20_2.context: A king is compared to a lion because his anger is powerful and dangerous to face.

christianity_proverbs_20_3.meaning: Avoiding conflict shows wisdom and honor. Only foolish people enjoy starting arguments and causing trouble.
christianity_proverbs_20_3.context: The text says it is good to stay away from arguments and not join in fights.

christianity_proverbs_20_4.meaning: Hard work now prevents hunger later. If you are lazy, you will have nothing when food is needed.
christianity_proverbs_20_4.context: A lazy person refuses to work the fields during the cold winter season.

christianity_proverbs_19_26.meaning: Harming your parents brings deep shame to your family and shows you have no basic respect for them.
christianity_proverbs_19_26.context: This verse talks about how a child should treat their parents with deep respect and care.

christianity_proverbs_19_27.meaning: If you ignore good advice, you will lose your way and miss out on true wisdom and understanding.
christianity_proverbs_19_27.context: A father is warning his son about the dangers of ignoring wise advice and good teaching.

christianity_proverbs_19_28.meaning: Lying in court makes a joke of fairness, and bad people happily accept and spread wrong actions.
christianity_proverbs_19_28.context: This describes how dishonest people act in courtrooms and how they treat the idea of fairness.

christianity_proverbs_19_29.meaning: People who laugh at rules and act foolishly will face punishment and physical trouble for their choices.
christianity_proverbs_19_29.context: This verse warns about the natural consequences that come from being rude and refusing to learn.

christianity_proverbs_20_7.meaning: When you live with honesty and kindness, your family will be happy and blessed because of your good example.
christianity_proverbs_20_7.context: This verse describes a good person who lives honestly and does right things every single day.

christianity_proverbs_20_8.meaning: Fair leaders use their power to spot trouble early and remove evil so that everyone can live in peace.
christianity_proverbs_20_8.context: A wise leader sits on his throne and watches closely to stop bad people from doing harm.

christianity_proverbs_20_9.meaning: No one is perfect. We all make mistakes, so we should stay humble and admit our faults to God.
christianity_proverbs_20_9.context: This question asks if anyone can truly claim they are perfect and have never done anything wrong.

christianity_proverbs_20_10.meaning: God hates dishonesty. You should always be fair in business and treat others with honesty and respect.
christianity_proverbs_20_10.context: This verse talks about merchants who use fake scales to cheat customers when buying or selling goods.

christianity_proverbs_20_16.meaning: Us to be careful when lending to strangers or helping others with valuable possessions. If you provide aid, ensure they have the means to repay to avoid unnecessary sacrifices or disappointments.
christianity_proverbs_20_16.context: This verse from the Bible, found in Proverbs 20:16, talks about a situation where someone lends money or an item to a stranger who cannot repay it. The lender then uses the item as collateral until the debt is paid.

christianity_proverbs_20_19.meaning: Be cautious of friends who gossip or share others' secrets. Avoiding such people helps protect your own privacy and maintain strong, trustworthy relationships.
christianity_proverbs_20_19.context: In Christianity, Proverbs 20:19 advises against associating with someone who gossips or spreads rumors, as they may reveal your secrets too.

christianity_proverbs_20_20.meaning: Respect and honor your parents. Cursing them goes against God's commandments and can lead to negative consequences in your life.
christianity_proverbs_20_20.context: Proverbs 20:20 in the Bible warns that cursing one's parents is a grave sin, as it brings darkness to their child's life.

christianity_proverbs_20_21.meaning: Patience and wise investments are essential for long-term prosperity. Quick wealth may seem beneficial initially, but it often leads to disappointment later.
christianity_proverbs_20_21.context: This verse from Proverbs 20:21 advises against acquiring wealth too quickly, as it may not bring blessings in the end.

christianity_proverbs_20_11.meaning: Us that a person's actions speak louder than words. Children, even, can show whether they are good or bad by their behavior. It highlights the significance of a person's actions in reflecting their character.
christianity_proverbs_20_11.context: This verse from the Bible, found in Proverbs 20:11, talks about how a child's actions reveal their character and whether they are good or evil. It emphasizes the importance of a person's deeds in determining their character.

christianity_proverbs_20_12.meaning: God created our senses to help us understand and enjoy life. By listening, seeing, and experiencing, we can gain knowledge and appreciate the world.
christianity_proverbs_20_12.context: Proverbs 20:12 is another verse from the Bible, which says that God created both the ear to hear and the eye to see. It emphasizes the importance of using our senses to understand and appreciate the world around us.

christianity_proverbs_20_14.meaning: Us the importance of being honest and consistent in our words and actions. When we praise something, we should do so truthfully, and not change our opinions once we have made a purchase or decision.
christianity_proverbs_20_14.context: Proverbs 20:14 is a verse from the Bible that talks about how a buyer may praise a product but later regret their purchase. It highlights the importance of being honest and true in our words and actions.

christianity_proverbs_20_15.meaning: The value of wisdom and knowledge over material possessions. Just like gold and rubies are valuable, wisdom and knowledge are also precious and should be pursued.
christianity_proverbs_20_15.context: Proverbs 20:15 is a verse from the Bible that compares the value of gold and rubies to the value of knowledge. It emphasizes the importance of wisdom and learning.

christianity_proverbs_20_22.meaning: The verse advises us not to take revenge when faced with evil. Instead, we should trust in God and wait for His help. This teaches us to rely on divine guidance and not engage in harmful actions.
christianity_proverbs_20_22.context: This verse is from the Christian book of Proverbs, written by Solomon. It talks about the importance of trusting in God's plan and not seeking revenge when someone harms us. The verse is set in a society where people often resort to retaliation instead of relying on God for protection.

christianity_proverbs_20_23.meaning: The verse emphasizes the importance of honesty and fair dealing in business. God disapproves of dishonest practices, so we should strive to be truthful and just in our dealings with others.
christianity_proverbs_20_23.context: This verse is also from the Christian book of Proverbs, discussing the importance of honesty and fairness in business transactions. The verse highlights the displeasure of God towards dishonest practices.

christianity_proverbs_20_24.meaning: The verse highlights that our actions are influenced by God's plan and we cannot fully comprehend our life's journey. It teaches us to trust in God's guidance and accept that we may not fully understand our life's purpose.
christianity_proverbs_20_24.context: This verse is from the Christian book of Proverbs, written by Solomon. It talks about the idea that human actions are guided by God's plan and we cannot fully understand our own paths.

christianity_proverbs_20_25.meaning: The verse warns against making quick decisions and promises without careful thought. It emphasizes the importance of considering the consequences before making commitments and fulfilling them responsibly.
christianity_proverbs_20_25.context: This verse is also from the Christian book of Proverbs, written by Solomon. It discusses the danger of making hasty promises and the consequences of not fulfilling them.

christianity_proverbs_20_26.meaning: Good leaders must remove harmful people to protect the group, just like cleaning grain from dirt.
christianity_proverbs_20_26.context: A smart ruler removes bad people from his land to keep the community safe and fair.

christianity_proverbs_20_29.meaning: Each age has its own special beauty. Young people shine with energy, and elders shine with experience.
christianity_proverbs_20_29.context: Young people show their power through physical strength, while older people show wisdom through their age.

christianity_proverbs_21_3.meaning: Doing what is right and fair matters more to God than just giving him gifts or offerings.
christianity_proverbs_21_3.context: God values how you treat others more than the religious rituals you perform in his house.

christianity_proverbs_21_5.meaning: Taking your time and working steadily leads to success, while rushing around usually causes you to fail.
christianity_proverbs_21_5.context: People who work hard and plan well usually succeed, but those who rush often fail and lose money.

christianity_proverbs_21_6.meaning: Be cautious of dishonest ways to gain wealth, as they are temporary and can lead to dangerous outcomes.
christianity_proverbs_21_6.context: This verse is from the Christian book of Proverbs, written by Solomon. It talks about the futility of seeking wealth through deceitful means, especially when it leads to seeking death.

christianity_proverbs_21_9.meaning: It is preferable to live separately from a contentious person, as living with them causes trouble.
christianity_proverbs_21_9.context: Proverbs 21:9 is a verse from the Christian book of Proverbs. It advises against living with a contentious woman, suggesting it is better to live alone on the roof.

christianity_proverbs_21_10.meaning: A wicked person who desires evil and lacks compassion for others will experience a similar lack of mercy.
christianity_proverbs_21_10.context: In Proverbs 21:10, Solomon warns about the wicked person who desires evil and shows no mercy to his neighbor.

christianity_proverbs_21_13.meaning: Failing to help the needy will result in one's own plights going unaddressed.
christianity_proverbs_21_13.context: Proverbs 21:13 speaks about ignoring the cries of the poor, which leads to one's own unheard cries as well.

christianity_proverbs_21_16.meaning: Ignoring wisdom leads to serious trouble and eventual ruin because you lose your way in life.
christianity_proverbs_21_16.context: This verse warns people who ignore good advice and choose to live foolishly instead of wisely.

christianity_proverbs_21_19.meaning: Peace is more valuable than comfort so being alone is better than constant fighting at home.
christianity_proverbs_21_19.context: This saying compares living alone in a harsh place to living with a constantly angry person.

christianity_proverbs_21_20.meaning: Smart planning brings lasting wealth but reckless spending destroys your savings and leaves you with nothing.
christianity_proverbs_21_20.context: Wise people save valuable resources for the future while foolish people waste everything they have quickly.

christianity_proverbs_21_22.meaning: Using your brain is stronger than muscle because wisdom can defeat even the most powerful opponents.
christianity_proverbs_21_22.context: A clever person can overcome strong defenses by using strategy rather than just brute force or power.

christianity_proverbs_21_28.meaning: Honesty builds a strong legacy while lying destroys your reputation and leads to a shameful end.
christianity_proverbs_21_28.context: Liars face ruin while those who listen to truth speak with lasting power and wisdom.

christianity_proverbs_21_29.meaning: Stay steady in doing what is right even when others refuse to change their bad ways.
christianity_proverbs_21_29.context: Bad people act stubbornly but good people stay firm in their right path and choices.

christianity_proverbs_21_30.meaning: Trust in God because human plans cannot override His will or change His final decision.
christianity_proverbs_21_30.context: No human plan or smart advice can stop or change what God has decided to do.

christianity_proverbs_21_31.meaning: Do your best work but remember that success depends on God and not just your efforts.
