John the Baptist was a prophet who had been preparing the way for Jesus' arrival. Jesus is telling the people to share with John the amazing things that have happened since he started his ministry.

christianity_luke_7_23.meaning: This verse means that it is important to focus on the teachings and actions of Jesus, rather than being judgmental or finding faults. We should trust in Jesus and follow his teachings without criticizing others.
christianity_luke_7_23.context: This verse is also from the Christian Gospel of Luke, chapter 7, verse 23. It is part of a conversation between Jesus and people who were questioning him.

christianity_luke_7_24.meaning: This verse is a response to the people's question about Jesus' humble appearance compared to John the Baptist. Jesus is reminding them that true worth isn't determined by outward appearances, but by the message and actions one represents.
christianity_luke_7_24.context: This verse is from the Christian Gospel of Luke, chapter 7, verse 24. It is part of a conversation between Jesus and people who were questioning him. John the Baptist was a prophet who had been preparing the way for Jesus' arrival.

christianity_luke_7_25.meaning: This verse is a response to the people's question about Jesus' humble lifestyle compared to the rich and powerful. Jesus is teaching that true greatness comes from serving others and following God's teachings, not from material wealth or power.
christianity_luke_7_25.context: This verse is from the Christian Gospel of Luke, chapter 7, verse 25. It is part of a conversation between Jesus and people who were questioning him.

christianity_luke_7_26.meaning: John was not just a prophet. He was far more important because he prepared the way for the Messiah to arrive.
christianity_luke_7_26.context: Jesus asks the crowd what they expected to see when they went out to the desert to meet John.

christianity_luke_7_27.meaning: John had a special job. He was sent to clear the path so that people could be ready to meet God.
christianity_luke_7_27.context: Jesus quotes an old scripture to show that John was the messenger promised to come before the Lord.

christianity_luke_7_28.meaning: John was the greatest prophet, but even the smallest person in God's kingdom has a higher standing than he did.
christianity_luke_7_28.context: Jesus compares John to all other prophets, saying he is the greatest one born from a woman.

christianity_luke_7_29.meaning: These people accepted God's justice. They showed this by getting baptized, which meant they wanted to turn their lives around.
christianity_luke_7_29.context: The crowd and tax collectors heard Jesus speak and agreed that God was right about John's teachings.

christianity_luke_7_30.meaning: Pride stops people from accepting truth. We must be humble and willing to change our ways.
christianity_luke_7_30.context: Religious leaders refused to accept God's plan because they would not follow John's baptism example.

christianity_luke_7_31.meaning: Some people are so stubborn they find fault with everyone. They never seem satisfied with anything.
christianity_luke_7_31.context: Jesus asks a question to show how hard it is to please this stubborn crowd.

christianity_luke_7_32.meaning: People often complain no matter what you do. You cannot please those who want to criticize.
christianity_luke_7_32.context: Children complain that others will not play their games or join their serious mourning rituals.

christianity_luke_7_33.meaning: Critics will find reasons to attack you. Do not let their unfair words stop your good work.
christianity_luke_7_33.context: John lived a strict life without food or wine, yet critics called him possessed by evil.

christianity_luke_7_34.meaning: This verse criticizes the religious leaders for judging Jesus based on his lifestyle, rather than focusing on his teachings and miracles. It highlights the importance of understanding a person's character through their actions rather than superficial appearances.
christianity_luke_7_34.context: This verse is from the Christian Bible, specifically in the Gospel of Luke by Luke the Evangelist. It is part of a larger narrative about Jesus Christ and his interactions with various people, including a religious leader named Simon who questions Jesus's actions.

christianity_luke_7_35.meaning: That wisdom is proven by the actions and beliefs of those who follow it. In this case, Jesus' actions of healing and teaching demonstrate the truth of his wisdom.
christianity_luke_7_35.context: This verse is from the same Gospel of Luke, chapter 7, verse 35. It is part of a conversation between Jesus and a woman named Syrophoenician woman who seeks healing for her daughter.

christianity_luke_7_36.meaning: This verse shows Jesus' humility and acceptance of people from all walks of life. It teaches us to be open-minded and accepting of others, regardless of their social status or beliefs.
christianity_luke_7_36.context: This verse is from the same Gospel of Luke, chapter 7, verse 36. It describes an event where Jesus is invited to a meal at the house of a Pharisee named Simon.

christianity_luke_7_37.meaning: The importance of forgiveness, love, and self-sacrifice. Jesus accepts Mary's act of love and forgives her, showing us the value of showing love and compassion towards others, even those considered sinners.
christianity_luke_7_37.context: This verse is also from the Gospel of Luke, chapter 7, verse 37. It narrates an incident where a sinner named Mary anoints Jesus with costly ointment.

christianity_luke_7_42.meaning: That forgiveness leads to gratitude and love. When both debtors were forgiven, the one who was forgiven more should love the creditor more. It shows the importance of forgiveness and its impact on relationships.
christianity_luke_7_42.context: This verse is from the Christian Bible, specifically in the Gospel of Luke by Luke the Evangelist. It tells a story about a man who borrows money from two debtors but can't repay. The creditor chooses to forgive both debts.

christianity_luke_7_43.meaning: The role of forgiveness in evaluating love. Simon believed that the debtor forgiven more would love the creditor more. Jesus confirms this perspective, showing the connection between forgiveness and love.
christianity_luke_7_43.context: In the same story, Simon, a man who was present, tries to justify his answer about which debtor loved the creditor more. Jesus approves Simon's response.

christianity_luke_7_44.meaning: The importance of showing kindness and compassion. Simon failed to show hospitality to Jesus, while the woman demonstrated great love and respect. Jesus points this out to Simon, emphasizing the value of compassion and humility.
christianity_luke_7_44.context: The woman washes Jesus' feet with her tears and wipes them with her hair, while Simon didn't show such hospitality. Jesus addresses this to Simon.

christianity_luke_7_45.meaning: Humility and respect. Simon, being a Pharisee, failed to show Jesus the respect he deserved as a guest. Jesus, being humble and loving, honored Jesus' presence.
christianity_luke_7_45.context: Simon the Pharisee invited Jesus to his home, but didn't show proper respect. Jesus, on the other hand, showed great love and respect.

christianity_luke_7_46.meaning: The importance of showing gratitude and love towards those who help or bless us. The person who showed more love (anointing Jesus' feet) received more in return, while the one who showed less love (not anointing Jesus' head) received less.
christianity_luke_7_46.context: This verse is from the Bible, specifically in the Gospel of Luke (7:46) in Christianity. It tells a story about a woman who anoints Jesus' feet with ointment during a dinner. Another person, who did not do the same, complains about it.

christianity_luke_7_47.meaning: Us that when we are forgiven much, we should love and serve more. On the other hand, those who receive less forgiveness tend to love less and be less forgiving towards others.
christianity_luke_7_47.context: In the same Bible passage (Luke 7:47), Jesus continues to teach a lesson about forgiveness. He talks about a woman who was forgiven much for her great love, while someone else, who was forgiven less, loved less.

christianity_luke_7_48.meaning: Jesus' power to forgive sins and the astonishment it caused among his followers. It emphasizes the belief that Jesus has the authority to forgive sins and change people's lives.
christianity_luke_7_48.context: In the same chapter (Luke 7:48), Jesus heals a woman's sins and she is amazed. Those who were present at the table began to question Jesus' authority to forgive sins.

christianity_luke_7_49.meaning: This verse shows Jesus' disciples' astonishment at his forgiveness towards the woman. It emphasizes the importance of understanding and showing compassion towards those who seek forgiveness, as Jesus did.
christianity_luke_7_49.context: In the same passage (Luke 7:49), Jesus' disciples express their surprise at his forgiveness towards the woman.

christianity_luke_7_38.meaning: True love and repentance are shown through humble actions and deep gratitude for forgiveness received.
christianity_luke_7_38.context: A woman known for sinning shows deep love by washing Jesus feet with tears and oil.

christianity_luke_7_39.meaning: Judging others based on their past mistakes prevents us from seeing their genuine faith.
christianity_luke_7_39.context: The host judges the woman silently, thinking Jesus would know she is a bad person.

christianity_luke_7_40.meaning: Being open to learning from others helps us understand deeper spiritual truths about grace.
christianity_luke_7_40.context: Jesus speaks to Simon the Pharisee, inviting him to listen to a story about forgiveness.

christianity_luke_7_41.meaning: Understanding debt helps us see how much forgiveness we have received from God.
christianity_luke_7_41.context: Jesus tells a parable about two people who owed money to the same lender.

christianity_luke_8_8.meaning: Good hearts accept God's word and let it grow into a life full of good deeds.
christianity_luke_8_8.context: Jesus finishes his story about seeds growing in different soil types for the crowd.

christianity_luke_8_9.meaning: Sometimes we need help to understand deep spiritual truths that are not obvious at first.
christianity_luke_8_9.context: The followers ask Jesus what his story about seeds and soil really means to them.

christianity_luke_8_10.meaning: Only those who truly care and listen will understand the deep secrets of God's kingdom.
christianity_luke_8_10.context: Jesus tells his close friends that they get special insight into God's hidden plans.

christianity_luke_8_11.meaning: The seed in the story stands for the message of God that we share with others.
christianity_luke_8_11.context: Jesus begins to explain the meaning of the seed story to his inner circle of friends.

christianity_luke_7_50.meaning: Us the importance of faith and trust in God. When we have faith, He can forgive our sins and provide us with peace. Jesus is an example of compassion and forgiveness.
christianity_luke_7_50.context: This verse is from the Christian Gospel of Luke (7:50), where Jesus speaks to a woman who had great faith. She had been touched by Jesus, and her faith in him led to her being declared sinless. Jesus then tells her to go in peace.

christianity_luke_8_1.meaning: Jesus' mission to share the message of God's Kingdom and the importance of spreading good news. He was accompanied by the twelve apostles, showing the significance of teamwork and support in achieving a common goal.
christianity_luke_8_1.context: This verse is from the same Gospel of Luke (8:1), describing Jesus' journey through cities and villages. He was spreading the message of God's Kingdom and was accompanied by the twelve apostles.

christianity_luke_8_2.meaning: This verse tells us about the support Jesus received from women, who believed in him and used their resources to help him. It emphasizes the importance of supporting those who share our beliefs and values.
christianity_luke_8_2.context: Mary Magdalene, Joanna, the wife of Churbas, Herod's steward, Susanna, and many others are mentioned. These women were supporting Jesus financially by using their possessions.

christianity_luke_8_3.meaning: The importance of spreading the message of God's Kingdom and the role of women in supporting Jesus' mission. It shows the unity among believers and the significance of teamwork in spreading faith.
christianity_luke_8_3.context: This verse is from the same Gospel of Luke (8:3)

christianity_luke_8_4.meaning: He used a story to help people understand deep spiritual truths about how we receive and keep his words.
christianity_luke_8_4.context: Jesus stood before a huge crowd from many cities to teach them a lesson using a simple story.

christianity_luke_8_5.meaning: Some people hear the message but do not understand it, so they let it go without keeping it in mind.
christianity_luke_8_5.context: A farmer scattered seeds on the ground, but some fell on hard paths where birds quickly ate them.

christianity_luke_8_6.meaning: Some accept the message with joy but give up quickly when they face trouble or lack deep roots.
christianity_luke_8_6.context: Other seeds landed on rocky soil and sprouted fast, but they died because there was no deep water.

christianity_luke_8_7.meaning: Life worries and greed can crowd out faith, preventing it from growing strong and producing good results.
christianity_luke_8_7.context: More seeds fell among thorny bushes, which grew up and choked the young plants so they could not thrive.

christianity_luke_8_17.meaning: Do not hide your true self because truth always comes out in the end.
christianity_luke_8_17.context: Jesus teaches that all secrets will eventually be uncovered and made known to everyone.

christianity_luke_8_18.meaning: If you listen well you gain wisdom but if you ignore it you lose what you had.
christianity_luke_8_18.context: Jesus warns listeners to pay close attention to his words and teachings carefully.

christianity_luke_8_19.meaning: Sometimes busy schedules or crowds prevent us from connecting with our loved ones.
christianity_luke_8_19.context: Jesus family arrives to visit him but the large crowd blocks their path.

christianity_luke_8_20.meaning: Family often waits patiently for us to make time for them despite our busy lives.
christianity_luke_8_20.context: A messenger informs Jesus that his mother and brothers are waiting outside to see him.

christianity_luke_8_12.meaning: If you do not hold onto good advice, bad influences will steal it away and stop you from finding peace.
christianity_luke_8_12.context: Jesus explains why some people hear his message but do not truly understand or keep it in their minds.

christianity_luke_8_13.meaning: Excitement fades quickly when hard times come, so you must build a strong foundation to stay faithful during trouble.
christianity_luke_8_13.context: Some people are happy to hear the truth at first, but they do not dig deep roots in their lives.

christianity_luke_8_14.meaning: Do not let busy schedules or material things crowd out your spiritual growth, or you will never reach your full potential.
christianity_luke_8_14.context: Others hear the message but let daily worries, money, and fun block the truth from growing inside them.

christianity_luke_8_16.meaning: Share your good deeds and wisdom openly with others, so everyone around you can see the light and follow you.
christianity_luke_8_16.context: Jesus says you should not hide a lit lamp under a bowl or bed, but place it high up.

christianity_luke_8_21.meaning: Us that true family and connections are based on understanding and following divine teachings, not on blood relations. We should prioritize listening and acting upon God's word in our lives.
christianity_luke_8_21.context: This verse is from the Christian Gospel of Luke, chapter 8, verse 21. It tells about Jesus Christ addressing a crowd who considered him related to his family based on blood relations. Instead, he says his 'mother and brothers' are those who listen to God's word and act upon it.

christianity_luke_8_22.meaning: This verse describes a journey in which Jesus and his followers board a boat to cross a lake. It symbolizes our spiritual journey to reach our destination (God) by following Jesus.
christianity_luke_8_22.context: In Christianity, Luke chapter 8, verse 22, Jesus and his disciples board a boat to cross the lake. They plan to go to the other side of the lake.

christianity_luke_8_23.meaning: This verse tells the story of Jesus and his disciples on a boat facing a dangerous storm at sea. It teaches us to trust in God during tough times and not to fear, as He is with us and can calm the storms of life.
christianity_luke_8_23.context: In Luke 8:23, during the journey, Jesus falls asleep while a severe storm and danger arise due to a strong wind and waves.

christianity_luke_8_24.meaning: This verse tells the story of Jesus calming the storm and saving his disciples. It teaches us to put our faith in God above all else and trust in His protection during difficult times.
christianity_luke_8_24.context: In Luke 8:24, Jesus wakes up, rebukes the storm, and all is calm. The disciples learn to fear God above all else.

christianity_luke_8_29.meaning: Sin can trap us deeply. Jesus has the power to free us from our darkest struggles and pain.
christianity_luke_8_29.context: A man possessed by demons lived in tombs. He broke chains and lived alone in the desert.

christianity_luke_8_30.meaning: Evil forces can be many. Jesus knows our true condition and calls out the darkness hiding within us.
christianity_luke_8_30.context: Jesus asked the demon for its name. It replied Legion because many spirits lived inside that one man.

christianity_luke_8_31.meaning: Evil fears judgment. We should also fear the consequences of sin and choose the path of light.
christianity_luke_8_31.context: The demons begged Jesus not to send them into the deep abyss where they would be trapped forever.

christianity_luke_8_32.meaning: Jesus allows consequences to show truth. We must trust his wisdom even when outcomes seem strange or costly.
christianity_luke_8_32.context: A large herd of pigs was nearby. The demons begged to enter them, and Jesus gave them permission.

christianity_luke_8_33.meaning: Bad forces can cause great harm when they are released, showing the serious power of evil.
christianity_luke_8_33.context: Evil spirits left a sick man and went into pigs that drowned in the water.

christianity_luke_8_34.meaning: People often spread news of amazing events quickly, even if they are scared by what they saw.
christianity_luke_8_34.context: The men watching the pigs ran away quickly to tell everyone in town about the strange event.

christianity_luke_8_35.meaning: True healing brings peace and order, but people may fear change or power they do not understand.
christianity_luke_8_35.context: Crowds came to see the healed man sitting calmly with Jesus, looking clean and sane, which scared them.

christianity_luke_8_36.meaning: Sharing true stories of healing helps others understand the power of faith and the goodness of God.
christianity_luke_8_36.context: Witnesses explained to the crowd how the man who was possessed by demons was completely healed by Jesus.

christianity_luke_8_25.meaning: We must trust God fully even when life feels dangerous or out of control because he has power over all things.
christianity_luke_8_25.context: Jesus calmed a storm on the sea and asked his scared disciples why they lacked trust in him.

christianity_luke_8_26.meaning: God often leads us to new places and situations where we can see his power work in unexpected ways.
christianity_luke_8_26.context: The boat crossed the lake and landed in a foreign region called Gadarenes which was on the other side.

christianity_luke_8_27.meaning: No matter how broken or lost you feel, Jesus is ready to meet you and bring healing to your life.
christianity_luke_8_27.context: A very sick man who lived among dead bodies and wore no clothes ran out to meet Jesus.

christianity_luke_8_28.meaning: Even evil spirits know Jesus is powerful and holy, so we should also respect his authority and seek his help.
christianity_luke_8_28.context: The possessed man recognized Jesus as God and begged him not to hurt him because he knew who he was.

christianity_luke_8_46.meaning: Jesus knew someone needed help and wanted them to step forward so they could receive full healing and peace.
christianity_luke_8_46.context: Jesus stopped walking because he felt power leave his body when a sick woman touched his clothes in the crowd.

christianity_luke_8_47.meaning: Honesty and faith bring healing. Jesus wants us to share our needs openly so he can restore our health completely.
christianity_luke_8_47.context: The woman was scared but came forward to tell Jesus why she touched him and how she felt better right away.

christianity_luke_8_49.meaning: Bad news can make us feel hopeless, but we should not give up on seeking help even when things look dark.
christianity_luke_8_49.context: A messenger arrived to tell the synagogue leader that his daughter had died and Jesus should not bother helping.

christianity_luke_8_50.meaning: Faith means trusting God even when death seems final. Belief opens the door for miracles and brings hope to despair.
christianity_luke_8_50.context: Jesus heard the sad news about the girl and told her father not to fear but to trust in him.

christianity_luke_8_37.meaning: Fear can sometimes make people reject good news even when they see powerful proof of divine help.
christianity_luke_8_37.context: The locals were terrified by the miracle and asked Jesus to leave their region immediately.

christianity_luke_8_38.meaning: Your first mission is often to share your story with those closest to you.
christianity_luke_8_38.context: The healed man wanted to follow Jesus closely but Jesus told him to go home instead.

christianity_luke_8_39.meaning: Share your personal testimony openly so others can see the power and love of God.
christianity_luke_8_39.context: Jesus told the man to go home and tell everyone about the great things God did.

christianity_luke_8_40.meaning: People who seek truth will eagerly welcome the one who brings healing and hope.
christianity_luke_8_40.context: Jesus came back to the other side and a large crowd was waiting to welcome him.

christianity_luke_8_41.meaning: We should humbly ask for help when we are in deep trouble and need divine guidance and support.
christianity_luke_8_41.context: A synagogue leader named Jairus fell down before Jesus and begged him to come to his home for help.

christianity_luke_8_42.meaning: Life is fragile and urgent. We must act quickly with faith when facing serious personal crises and fears.
christianity_luke_8_42.context: Jairus had a dying twelve year old daughter. Crowds pressed against Jesus as he walked toward the house.

christianity_luke_8_43.meaning: When human efforts fail, we should turn to spiritual hope. Faith can heal what medicine cannot fix.
christianity_luke_8_43.context: A woman suffered from bleeding for twelve years. She spent all her money on doctors but found no cure.

christianity_luke_8_45.meaning: Jesus seeks personal connection, not just physical contact. True faith requires intentional and deliberate action from us.
christianity_luke_8_45.context: Jesus asked who touched him. The crowd denied it. Peter pointed out the crowds were pressing against him constantly.

christianity_luke_8_51.meaning: Sometimes you need a quiet, private space to focus on what truly matters in life.
christianity_luke_8_51.context: Jesus arrived at the house and let only a few close friends and the parents inside.

christianity_luke_8_52.meaning: True faith sees hope and life where others only see final loss and deep sadness.
christianity_luke_8_52.context: Everyone was crying sadly, but Jesus calmly told them the girl was just sleeping peacefully.

christianity_luke_8_53.meaning: People often mock what they do not understand or what seems impossible to their eyes.
christianity_luke_8_53.context: The people laughed at Jesus because they clearly saw the girl had already passed away.

christianity_luke_8_54.meaning: Real power comes from quiet focus and direct action, not from the noise of a crowd.
christianity_luke_8_54.context: Jesus sent the crowd out, held the girl's hand, and commanded her to stand up.

christianity_luke_8_55.meaning: The power of Jesus to bring life and restore hope. It also shows His care for human needs, as He provided food for the woman after raising her from the dead.
christianity_luke_8_55.context: This verse is from the Christian Bible, specifically the Gospel of Luke (8:55). It tells the story of a woman who was raised from the dead by Jesus. Her spirit was restored, and she got up right away. Jesus instructed that food be given to her.

christianity_luke_8_56.meaning: Jesus' ability to perform miracles and His desire to maintain a balance between public recognition and personal faith. It teaches us to respect His ways and not to share everything with everyone.
christianity_luke_8_56.context: (Luke 8:56), Jesus' parents and the people present were amazed by the woman's resurrection. Jesus instructed them not to share the story publicly.

christianity_luke_9_1.meaning: This verse tells the story of Jesus gathering His closest followers (the apostles) to give them authority to drive out demons and heal the sick. It teaches us the importance of faith and divine guidance in overcoming challenges and helping others.
christianity_luke_9_1.context: In Luke 9:1 (Christianity), Jesus gathered His disciples (the twelve apostles) to empower them with divine authority over evil forces (demons) and heal the sick.

christianity_luke_9_2.meaning: This verse describes Jesus instructing His disciples to share the message of God's love and compassion (the Gospel) while helping others through healing. It teaches us the importance of spreading kindness, love, and compassion to improve the world.
christianity_luke_9_2.context: In Luke 9:2 (Christianity), Jesus instructed His disciples to spread the Gospel and heal the sick.

christianity_luke_9_3.meaning: Simplicity and detachment from worldly possessions. It teaches us to focus on our spiritual journey rather than being burdened by material possessions.
christianity_luke_9_3.context: This verse is from the Christian Bible, specifically the Gospel of Luke (9:3). It narrates a teaching of Jesus Christ to His disciples before they embark on a missionary journey. Jesus instructs them to carry no belongings, such as staffs, wallets, food, or money.

christianity_luke_9_4.meaning: Patience and obedience. It teaches us to respect the hospitality we receive and not rush through our experiences.
christianity_luke_9_4.context: This verse is also from the Gospel of Luke (9:4). It is part of Jesus' instructions to His disciples during their missionary journey. Jesus instructs them to stay in the house they enter and not move on immediately.

christianity_luke_9_5.meaning: Us to prioritize our faith and values over personal relationships. It reminds us to stand firm in our beliefs and not compromise them for others.
christianity_luke_9_5.context: This verse is from the same source, the Gospel of Luke (9:5). It is a part of Jesus' instructions to His disciples while they were on their missionary journey. Jesus advises them to avoid unbelievers and show no mercy towards them.

christianity_luke_9_6.meaning: The importance of dedicating ourselves to our purpose and not being distracted by worldly matters. It reminds us to prioritize our spiritual journey over material concerns.
christianity_luke_9_6.context: This verse is from the same source, the Gospel of Luke (9:6). It is part of Jesus' instructions to His disciples during their missionary journey. Jesus encourages them to focus on their mission and not be hindered by personal concerns.

christianity_luke_9_11.meaning: Jesus welcomes everyone, shares hope, and shows God's power by healing those in need.
christianity_luke_9_11.context: Jesus sees many people, invites them, talks about God's Kingdom, heals the sick.

christianity_luke_9_12.meaning: The disciples worry about practical needs, but Jesus will provide for everyone.
christianity_luke_9_12.context: The crowd grows, the disciples ask Jesus to send them away to find food and rest.

christianity_luke_9_13.meaning: Even small offerings can be enough when shared with faith and trust in Jesus.
christianity_luke_9_13.context: Jesus tells the disciples to give food, but they only have five loaves and two fish.

christianity_luke_9_14.meaning: Jesus organizes the crowd to make feeding easier, showing thoughtful planning.
christianity_luke_9_14.context: About five thousand people are present; Jesus instructs disciples to seat them in groups of fifty.

christianity_luke_9_15.meaning: Us to be resourceful and to share what we have with others, even when it seems insufficient. It demonstrates Jesus' compassion and ability to provide for many with minimal resources.
christianity_luke_9_15.context: This verse is from the Bible, specifically in the Gospel of Luke chapter 9, verse 15. It talks about Jesus and his disciples performing a miracle and feeding a large crowd with a few small resources.

christianity_luke_9_16.meaning: Us to trust in God and believe in His power to provide for us. It shows Jesus' humility by taking the time to bless, break, and distribute the food to the people.
christianity_luke_9_16.context: This verse is also from the Gospel of Luke in the Bible, chapter 9, verse 16. It describes Jesus performing a miracle by multiplying a small amount of food to feed a large crowd.

christianity_luke_9_17.meaning: The importance of gratitude and being satisfied with what we have. It demonstrates Jesus' generosity and the abundance He provides even with minimal resources.
christianity_luke_9_17.context: This verse is from the same Bible passage, Luke 9:17. It tells the story of Jesus feeding a large crowd with only a few small resources leftover.

christianity_luke_9_18.meaning: Us the value of prayer and seeking guidance from God. It shows Jesus' humility and reliance on His Father's will before taking action.
christianity_luke_9_18.context: This verse is from the same Bible passage, Luke 9:18. It describes Jesus praying with His disciples before performing the miracle of feeding the crowd.

christianity_luke_9_7.meaning: Herod struggled to understand Jesus' impact. People had different opinions about him, ranging from a resurrected prophet to a returned old prophet or Elijah. Jesus' actions caused confusion.
christianity_luke_9_7.context: Herod the tetrarch, a ruler, heard about Jesus' actions and became confused because some believed John the Baptist had come back from the dead and others thought Elijah or an old prophet had returned.

christianity_luke_9_8.meaning: Herod was perplexed by Jesus' fame. People had diverse opinions about him, ranging from John the Baptist's resurrection to an old prophet's reappearance.
christianity_luke_9_8.context: Herod wondered about Jesus, as he heard various reports: some said John the Baptist had risen, while others believed an old prophet had been resurrected.

christianity_luke_9_9.meaning: Herod wanted to meet Jesus after hearing about his actions. Despite believing John the Baptist was dead, he was curious to confirm the rumors and understand Jesus better.
christianity_luke_9_9.context: Herod sought to meet Jesus after hearing about his deeds. He believed John the Baptist had been beheaded, but still wanted to see Jesus to clarify the rumors.

christianity_luke_9_10.meaning: The apostles came back and shared their stories with Jesus. In response, Jesus retreated to a peaceful spot near Bethsaida.
christianity_luke_9_10.context: The apostles returned and told Jesus about their experiences. Jesus then withdrew to a quiet area near a town called Bethsaida.

christianity_luke_9_19.meaning: People often guess about spiritual leaders based on rumors. We should look deeper than just public opinion to find truth.
christianity_luke_9_19.context: Jesus asks his disciples what people think about him. They list various popular opinions and guesses.

christianity_luke_9_20.meaning: True faith requires personal conviction. You must decide for yourself who Jesus is and what he means to you.
christianity_luke_9_20.context: Jesus turns the question back to his followers. Peter boldly declares that Jesus is the promised Messiah of God.

christianity_luke_9_21.meaning: Some truths are revealed in time. Patience and obedience are important when following divine instructions and plans.
christianity_luke_9_21.context: Jesus tells his disciples to keep this secret. He does not want people to know his identity yet.

christianity_luke_9_22.meaning: Great purpose often involves hardship. Hope remains even in suffering because new life follows death and sacrifice.
christianity_luke_9_22.context: Jesus explains that his mission involves great suffering. He predicts his death and resurrection after three days.

christianity_luke_9_23.meaning: To follow Jesus, one must be willing to forsake their own desires and priorities, and instead align themselves with Jesus' teachings and mission.
christianity_luke_9_23.context: This verse is from the Christian Bible, specifically in the Gospel of Luke chapter 9, verse 23. It is part of a teaching by Jesus Christ where He calls for discipleship and commitment.

christianity_luke_9_24.meaning: Saving one's life by prioritizing self over Jesus' message leads to loss, while losing one's life for Jesus results in salvation.
christianity_luke_9_24.context: This verse is also from the Gospel of Luke in the Christian Bible, chapter 9, verse 24. It is connected to verse 23 and emphasizes the importance of self-sacrifice for the sake of Jesus and His teachings.

christianity_luke_9_25.meaning: Valuing worldly possessions over oneself leads to emptiness; understanding one's true worth and following Jesus brings fulfillment.
christianity_luke_9_25.context: This verse is from the same chapter and book as verses 23 and 24, Luke 9:25. It discusses the value of a person's life when compared to material possessions and worldly success.

christianity_luke_9_26.meaning: Shunning Jesus and His teachings may result in exclusion; being devoted to Jesus brings closeness and honor.
christianity_luke_9_26.context: This verse is from the same book and chapter as verses 23 and 24, Luke 9:26. It highlights the importance of being ashamed of Jesus and His teachings, which could lead to exclusion from His glory and the company of holy angels.

christianity_luke_9_27.meaning: The concept of Jesus' prophecy about the nearness of God's Kingdom and reassures his followers that they will experience its arrival before they die.
christianity_luke_9_27.context: This verse is from the Gospel of Luke in Christianity, written by the disciple Luke. It is spoken by Jesus Christ to his disciples, emphasizing the idea of the coming of God's Kingdom and the experiences of those present who will not die before witnessing it.

christianity_luke_9_28.meaning: This verse introduces a crucial moment in the life of Jesus, where he took three key disciples with him for a spiritual journey.
christianity_luke_9_28.context: This verse describes an event eight days after Jesus spoke the words in verse 1 (v1). Jesus chose Peter, John, and James to accompany him on this significant journey.

christianity_luke_9_29.meaning: This verse depicts a miraculous event where Jesus undergoes a spiritual transfiguration before his disciples, symbolizing his divine nature.
christianity_luke_9_29.context: While on the mountain, Jesus was transfigured before his disciples, with his appearance and clothing changing dramatically.

christianity_luke_9_30.meaning: This verse reveals a divine encounter where Jesus is accompanied by Old Testament figures, Moses and Elijah, emphasizing the continuity of God's message and his connection with the past.
christianity_luke_9_30.context: During the transfiguration event, Moses and Elijah appeared alongside Jesus, representing the Old Testament and its teachings.

christianity_luke_9_39.meaning: Some problems in life are too strong for us to handle alone and need divine help to find peace.
christianity_luke_9_39.context: A father describes his son suffering from a severe seizure caused by an evil spirit that hurts him badly.

christianity_luke_9_40.meaning: Even good people can fail when they lack true faith, showing that human effort alone is often not enough.
christianity_luke_9_40.context: The father tells Jesus that his followers tried to help the boy but failed to remove the spirit.

christianity_luke_9_41.meaning: We must trust in God fully during hard times, because doubt blocks the power of healing and hope.
christianity_luke_9_41.context: Jesus expresses sadness over the people's lack of faith and asks the father to bring his son closer.

christianity_luke_9_42.meaning: Jesus has ultimate power over evil and suffering, bringing peace and restoration to those who seek his help.
christianity_luke_9_42.context: The spirit attacks the boy again, but Jesus commands it to leave, heals the child, and returns him safely.

christianity_luke_9_31.meaning: Jesus, being divine, appeared in glory to communicate His plan of sacrifice for our salvation. Following this, His disciples learned the importance of understanding and accepting His teachings.
christianity_luke_9_31.context: This verse talks about Jesus appearing in glory and discussing His upcoming sacrifice in Jerusalem. Jesus informed His disciples about His impending crucifixion.

christianity_luke_9_32.meaning: Even when tired, we should stay awake spiritually to witness divine wonders. Peter's words show our desire for sacred spaces even for mortal figures like Moses and Elijah, symbolizing seeking guidance and wisdom.
christianity_luke_9_32.context: Peter and his companions were tired from sleep but woke up to witness Jesus' glory and two mysterious men. They were amazed and didn't fully understand the significance.

christianity_luke_9_33.meaning: It demonstrates the disciples' admiration for holy figures and their longing for spiritual guidance. Peter's words reveal our innate desire to connect with divine beings.
christianity_luke_9_33.context: Peter proposed building shelters for Jesus, Moses, and Elijah, not knowing what he was saying. This shows their awe and desire for divine presence.

christianity_luke_9_34.meaning: When we encounter the divine, we may feel overwhelmed or fearful due to the unknown. The cloud represents the unexplainable nature of these experiences.
christianity_luke_9_34.context: As Jesus spoke, a cloud covered Him, causing fear in His followers. This signifies the mysterious nature of divine encounters.

christianity_luke_9_35.meaning: We should pay close attention to Jesus teachings because he carries the direct message and will of God.
christianity_luke_9_35.context: God speaks from heaven to confirm Jesus is his special son during a holy moment on the mountain.

christianity_luke_9_36.meaning: Some spiritual experiences are personal and deep, so we should respect silence and not rush to share everything.
christianity_luke_9_36.context: After the voice stops, Jesus stands alone with his friends who keep the amazing event a secret.

christianity_luke_9_37.meaning: Life moves from quiet moments back to busy daily routines where we must serve many people.
christianity_luke_9_37.context: The group leaves the high mountain and walks down to find a large crowd waiting for Jesus.

christianity_luke_9_38.meaning: When we face hard problems, we should ask for help with honest and urgent faith in others.
christianity_luke_9_38.context: A desperate father shouts to Jesus, asking him to help his only sick child who needs healing.

christianity_luke_9_43.meaning: When people are amazed by great things, we should listen closely to the deeper truths behind them.
christianity_luke_9_43.context: The crowd was amazed by Jesus power, and he turned to speak privately to his close followers.

christianity_luke_9_44.meaning: We must be ready for hard times, even when we do not fully understand why they happen.
christianity_luke_9_44.context: Jesus told his followers that he would soon be handed over to people who would harm him.

christianity_luke_9_45.meaning: Fear can stop us from seeking clarity, so we should always ask questions when we are confused.
christianity_luke_9_45.context: The disciples did not grasp what Jesus said and were too scared to ask him for more help.

christianity_luke_9_46.meaning: We should focus on serving others rather than competing for status or trying to be the best.
christianity_luke_9_46.context: The disciples started arguing with each other about who among them was the most important person.

christianity_luke_9_51.meaning: When you know your goal is hard, you must stay focused and move forward with purpose.
christianity_luke_9_51.context: Jesus knew his time on earth was ending, so he decided to head to Jerusalem.

christianity_luke_9_52.meaning: Preparing the way for others shows care and helps make important journeys smoother and easier.
christianity_luke_9_52.context: Jesus sent his followers ahead to a town to arrange a place for him to stay.

christianity_luke_9_53.meaning: People often reject truth or change when they are afraid of what it might bring to them.
christianity_luke_9_53.context: The villagers refused to welcome Jesus because he was heading to Jerusalem for his final days.

christianity_luke_9_54.meaning: Anger can make us want to hurt others, but true strength comes from choosing peace over revenge.
christianity_luke_9_54.context: James and John were angry at the rejection and asked if they should call down fire to punish them.

christianity_luke_9_47.meaning: True greatness comes from humble service and caring for the small and weak people.
christianity_luke_9_47.context: Jesus saw his disciples arguing about who was the greatest among them all.

christianity_luke_9_48.meaning: Welcoming the humble is like welcoming God. The least among you will be great.
christianity_luke_9_48.context: Jesus placed a child beside him to teach his followers about humility and service.

christianity_luke_9_49.meaning: We often judge others harshly when they do good things but are not our friends.
christianity_luke_9_49.context: John told Jesus they stopped a man using his name to cast out demons.

christianity_luke_9_50.meaning: Do not block those who do good. Anyone not against us is actually for us.
christianity_luke_9_50.context: Jesus corrected John and told him not to stop the man from doing good.

christianity_luke_9_55.meaning: Jesus warned the people that he is not a common person but possesses divine power. His purpose is not to destroy lives but to save and guide them.
christianity_luke_9_55.context: This verse is from the Christian Bible, specifically in the Gospel of Luke (9:55). Jesus and his disciples were traveling when they encountered some people who didn't understand the nature of Jesus' mission.

christianity_luke_9_56.meaning: Jesus came to bring love, compassion, and redemption, not to cause suffering. His purpose is to save and bring about a better life for all.
christianity_luke_9_56.context: In Luke 9:56 (Christianity), Jesus and his disciples were on a journey. The verse talks about Jesus' mission to save lives, not harm them.

christianity_luke_9_57.meaning: This verse illustrates the importance of trusting in Jesus and following his teachings. Jesus welcomes those who desire to learn from him and serve others.
christianity_luke_9_57.context: In Luke 9:57 (Christianity), Jesus and his disciples were traveling when a man approached him and expressed his desire to follow Jesus wherever he goes.

christianity_luke_9_58.meaning: The humility and selflessness of Jesus. He doesn't seek material comforts but focuses on fulfilling his divine mission.
christianity_luke_9_58.context: Luke 9:58 (Christianity) tells the story of Jesus and his disciples on a journey. A man asked Jesus about his lack of a place to rest.

christianity_luke_9_59.meaning: Jesus teaches that following Him must come before family duties or personal plans.
christianity_luke_9_59.context: A man wants to follow Jesus but says he must first bury his father.

christianity_luke_9_60.meaning: He urges people to focus on spreading faith, not on worldly concerns.
christianity_luke_9_60.context: Jesus tells a man to leave the dead to bury their dead and announce God's Kingdom.

christianity_luke_9_61.meaning: Jesus shows that devotion to Him must not be delayed by personal attachments.
christianity_luke_9_61.context: Another man says he wants to follow Jesus but must say goodbye to his household first.

christianity_luke_9_62.meaning: He stresses that once you choose Him, you must stay focused and not return to old ways.
christianity_luke_9_62.context: Jesus says no one can work and look back to be fit for God's Kingdom.

christianity_luke_10_1.meaning: Jesus' commitment to spreading his message and emphasizes the importance of following his teachings. It encourages us to be obedient and ready to serve others, just as Jesus sent out his disciples.
christianity_luke_10_1.context: This verse talks about Jesus Christ choosing and sending out seventy disciples ahead of him to different towns and places where he was going to visit. This event is mentioned in the Christian Gospel of Luke, chapter 10, verse 1.

christianity_luke_10_2.meaning: The vastness of the task at hand and the importance of prayer and intercession for spiritual growth and the expansion of the kingdom of God.
christianity_luke_10_2.context: Chapter 10, verse 2, Jesus addresses his disciples and mentions that the world is filled with people in need of salvation, but there are few dedicated followers to help them. He urges his disciples to pray for more workers to serve in spreading the gospel.

christianity_luke_10_3.meaning: Following a higher purpose may put us in difficult situations. We should remain steadfast, trusting in God's protection and guidance.
christianity_luke_10_3.context: This verse from the Christian Gospel of Luke, chapter 10, verse 3, is spoken by Jesus to his disciples before sending them out on their mission. It warns them that they will face opposition and challenges, comparing them to lambs among wolves.

christianity_luke_10_4.meaning: The importance of simplicity, trust in God, and focusing on our mission rather than worldly possessions.
christianity_luke_10_4.context: In Luke 10:4 of the Christian Gospel, Jesus instructs his disciples on how they should behave while serving others. He instructs them not to carry money, supplies, or greet people on their mission.

christianity_luke_10_9.meaning: Jesus' mission to bring healing and salvation to people, as well as the importance of sharing the message of God's love and mercy.
christianity_luke_10_9.context: Jesus instructs His disciples to heal the sick people in the towns they visit and announce that the Kingdom of God is near. This shows Jesus' compassion and concern for the well-being of others.

christianity_luke_10_10.meaning: Us to persevere in sharing the message of faith, even when faced with rejection or opposition, as God's Kingdom is always near.
christianity_luke_10_10.context: When entering a town and receiving no welcome, Jesus' followers are told to leave the town and publicly announce that God's Kingdom is near, even if it brings shame upon the town.

christianity_luke_10_11.meaning: The importance of sharing the Gospel and the consequences of rejecting God's love and truth.
christianity_luke_10_11.context: Jesus' followers are instructed to tell the people of the town they are visiting that they will receive less punishment from God than the town if they do not accept Jesus and His message.

christianity_luke_10_12.meaning: This verse warns about the seriousness of turning away from God and encourages accepting and spreading the Gospel.
christianity_luke_10_12.context: Jesus compares the unrepentant town to the ancient city of Sodom, emphasizing the severity of rejecting God's message and ignoring His love.

christianity_luke_10_5.meaning: Us to show kindness and positivity to the places and people we interact with. It emphasizes the importance of starting relationships on a peaceful note.
christianity_luke_10_5.context: This verse is from the Christian Bible, specifically in the book of Luke (10:5). It is part of a story about Jesus sending out his disciples to preach and heal. When they enter a town or house, they are instructed to first wish for peace and blessings upon that place.

christianity_luke_10_6.meaning: Us to discern the character of the people we interact with and adapt our interactions accordingly. It highlights the importance of harmony and understanding in relationships.
christianity_luke_10_6.context: Luke 10:6 is another verse from the Christian Bible. It continues the story of Jesus' disciples. This verse explains that if the people in a house are peaceful and welcoming, your blessings will be bestowed upon them; otherwise, they will return to you.

christianity_luke_10_7.meaning: The importance of accepting the generosity of others and being grateful for their kindness. It teaches us to be content with what we receive and not seek more.
christianity_luke_10_7.context: Luke 10:7 is another verse from the Christian Bible. This verse is also part of the story of Jesus' disciples. It instructs them to stay in the house they are welcomed into and enjoy the food and hospitality offered.

christianity_luke_10_8.meaning: Us the importance of being grateful for the kindness of others and not expecting anything in return. It reminds us to be content with what we have and not seek material gains.
christianity_luke_10_8.context: Luke 10:8 is another verse from the Christian Bible. This verse continues the story of Jesus' disciples. It instructs them to accept the food and hospitality offered by the people they visit.

christianity_luke_10_13.meaning: Seeing great signs is not enough. People must truly change their hearts and turn away from sin to find peace.
christianity_luke_10_13.context: Jesus warns two cities that saw many miracles but still refused to change their hearts and turn back to God.

christianity_luke_10_14.meaning: Having more knowledge brings greater responsibility. Ignoring clear truth leads to harsher consequences than simply not knowing the truth at all.
christianity_luke_10_14.context: Jesus says those who never saw miracles will face a lighter judgment than those who saw them and still refused to believe.

christianity_luke_10_15.meaning: Pride leads to a fall. Being close to God does not save you if you do not humble yourself and follow his ways.
christianity_luke_10_15.context: Capernaum was proud because Jesus lived there, but its pride led to a fall from grace and deep spiritual darkness.

christianity_luke_10_16.meaning: How you treat others shows your heart. Rejecting a messenger is like rejecting the sender. Love and respect those who share the truth.
christianity_luke_10_16.context: Jesus tells his followers that accepting or rejecting them is the same as accepting or rejecting him and God.

christianity_luke_10_22.meaning: That only the Father knows the Son completely, and only the Son knows who the Father is. Jesus reveals the Father's mysteries to those He chooses.
christianity_luke_10_22.context: This verse is from the Gospel of Luke in the Christian New Testament, specifically in the story where Jesus teaches His disciples. Jesus is talking about His authority and relationship with the Father.

christianity_luke_10_23.meaning: The importance of being grateful for the eyes that see divine revelations and the ears that understand spiritual truths.
christianity_luke_10_23.context: In the same scene, Jesus speaks privately to His disciples, highlighting the blessedness of those who see and understand divine revelations.

christianity_luke_10_24.meaning: The value of the disciples' experiences and teaches that seeking and understanding spiritual truths is a desire shared by many throughout history.
christianity_luke_10_24.context: Jesus continues His teaching by comparing the disciples' privilege to see and hear divine revelations to the longing of many prophets and kings in the past.

christianity_luke_10_25.meaning: This verse shows Jesus' ability to guide people in their quest for eternal life and emphasizes the importance of seeking wisdom and understanding from a wise teacher.
christianity_luke_10_25.context: A lawyer asks Jesus about eternal life, demonstrating Jesus' authority to teach on moral and spiritual matters.

christianity_luke_10_17.meaning: The power and authority Jesus bestowed upon his disciples, enabling them to drive out demons and spread His message with confidence.
christianity_luke_10_17.context: Specifically in the Gospel of Luke (10:17), seventy disciples return from their mission with great happiness. They share their experience that even evil spirits, also known as demons, obey them when they use Jesus' name.

christianity_luke_10_18.meaning: The fall of Satan and highlights Jesus' authority over him. It shows that even powerful beings can be defeated by God's grace and truth.
christianity_luke_10_18.context: In the same passage from Luke 10:18, Jesus speaks about the fall of Satan, who was once an angel in heaven. He reveals this to his disciples.

christianity_luke_10_19.meaning: This verse bestows upon Jesus' followers the ability to overcome evil forces and protect themselves. It highlights the strength found in trusting in God's protection and guidance.
christianity_luke_10_19.context: In Luke 10:19, Jesus gives his disciples authority to overcome evil forces, such as snakes, scorpions, and the power of the enemy. He assures them of their protection.

christianity_luke_10_21.meaning: This verse demonstrates Jesus' appreciation for humility and simplicity. It teaches us that true wisdom comes from God and is not dependent on human intelligence or knowledge.
christianity_luke_10_21.context: In Luke 10:21, Jesus expresses gratitude to His Father for hiding divine truths from the wise and intelligent, and revealing them to humble and innocent individuals.

christianity_luke_10_26.meaning: True faith starts with knowing the rules. We must read and understand the word to live right.
christianity_luke_10_26.context: Jesus asks a lawyer about the law to test his knowledge and understanding of God's commands.

christianity_luke_10_28.meaning: Knowing the truth is good. But you must actually do it to find true life and peace.
christianity_luke_10_28.context: Jesus confirms the lawyer gave the right answer about loving God and loving your neighbor fully.

christianity_luke_10_29.meaning: Do not make excuses to avoid helping others. Love everyone, not just the people you like.
christianity_luke_10_29.context: The lawyer tries to excuse himself by asking who exactly counts as a neighbor to him.

christianity_luke_10_30.meaning: Bad things happen to good people. We need to be ready to help those in deep trouble.
christianity_luke_10_30.context: Jesus tells a story about a man attacked by thieves on a dangerous road between cities.

christianity_luke_10_31.meaning: Kindness and compassion should not be conditional on relationships or beliefs; helping others in need is essential.
christianity_luke_10_31.context: A priest and a Levite encounter a wounded man by the roadside. They choose to ignore him instead of helping.

christianity_luke_10_32.meaning: Avoiding responsibility or standing idly by when someone is suffering is not virtuous.
christianity_luke_10_32.context: Similarly, a Levite also avoids helping the wounded man.

christianity_luke_10_34.meaning: Kindness, empathy, and taking action to help others are virtuous actions.
christianity_luke_10_34.context: A kind Samaritan stops, cares for the man, and takes him to an inn.

christianity_luke_10_35.meaning: Returning favors, generosity, and taking responsibility for our actions are important values.
christianity_luke_10_35.context: The Samaritan returns to pay for the man's further care, showing generosity and responsibility.

christianity_luke_10_36.meaning: Us to show compassion and help those in need, regardless of who they are or what they do. We should not judge others but act kindly and generously.
christianity_luke_10_36.context: This verse is from the Bible, specifically in the Gospel of Luke chapter 10, verse 36. It tells the story of a man who was robbed and left for dead. Three people were passing by, and one of them was asked to help the man.

christianity_luke_10_38.meaning: The importance of hospitality and welcoming guests into our homes with kindness and generosity. It also shows the contrast between Martha, who was busy serving, and her sister Mary, who listened to Jesus' teachings.
christianity_luke_10_38.context: This verse is from the Bible, specifically in the Gospel of Luke chapter 10, verse 38. It describes a scene where Jesus entered a village and was hosted by a woman named Martha.

christianity_luke_10_39.meaning: Us the value of prioritizing spiritual growth and learning over worldly tasks. It shows the contrast between Martha, who was busy with practical matters, and Mary, who focused on spiritual matters.
christianity_luke_10_39.context: This verse is from the Bible, specifically in the Gospel of Luke chapter 10, verse 39. It describes a scene where Mary chose to listen to Jesus while Martha was occupied with serving.

christianity_luke_10_40.meaning: This verse encourages us to prioritize relationships and spiritual growth over worldly tasks. Martha's concern for practical matters overshadowed her relationship with Jesus, while Mary chose to prioritize listening to Jesus and growing spiritually.
christianity_luke_10_40.context: This verse is from the Bible, specifically in the Gospel of Luke chapter 10, verse 40. It describes a conversation between Jesus and Martha.

christianity_luke_10_41.meaning: Martha is worried about many tasks and responsibilities, while Mary focuses on listening to Jesus' teachings. Jesus reminds us to prioritize spiritual things over worldly concerns.
christianity_luke_10_41.context: This verse is from the Bible, specifically in the book of Luke chapter 10, where Jesus is interacting with Martha, a woman from the town of Bethany. Martha is worried about many things, while her sister Mary is sitting at Jesus' feet listening to him.

christianity_luke_10_42.meaning: Mary chose to focus on listening to Jesus, while Martha is preoccupied with worldly tasks. Jesus teaches us to prioritize spiritual things over worldly matters.
christianity_luke_10_42.context: Specifically in the book of Luke chapter 10, Jesus is talking to Martha, a woman from Bethany. Martha is worried about many things, while her sister Mary is sitting at Jesus' feet listening to him.

christianity_luke_11_1.meaning: The disciple is seeking wisdom on how to pray. Jesus teaches us the importance of focusing on God, His name, His kingdom, and His will.
christianity_luke_11_1.context: This verse is from the Bible, specifically in the book of Luke chapter 11, where Jesus is teaching his disciples. One of his disciples, asking for prayer guidance, wants to know how to pray.

christianity_luke_11_2.meaning: The disciple is seeking wisdom on how to pray. Jesus teaches us the importance of focusing on God, His name, His kingdom, and His will.
christianity_luke_11_2.context: This verse is from the Bible, specifically in the book of Luke chapter 11, where Jesus is teaching his disciples. The disciple asks for prayer guidance, wanting to know how to pray.

christianity_luke_11_3.meaning: Learn to trust God for your daily provisions. Don't worry about tomorrow's problems; focus on today's tasks and faithfully serve Him.
christianity_luke_11_3.context: This verse is part of a prayer Jesus taught his disciples to ask God for their daily needs. The disciples faced challenges in providing for themselves and others, so they learned to rely on God for their basic necessities.

christianity_luke_11_5.meaning: Be understanding and compassionate when helping others, even in unexpected situations. Offer support without judgment or delay.
christianity_luke_11_5.context: This verse describes a hypothetical situation where a friend asks for help late at night. The speaker represents a person seeking assistance.

christianity_luke_11_6.meaning: Be prepared to help those in need, even if it disrupts your personal life. Don't dismiss others' requests based on inconvenience.
christianity_luke_11_6.context: The speaker is explaining a genuine situation where a friend has arrived unexpectedly and needs food. The speaker is caught off guard and unprepared.

christianity_luke_11_7.meaning: Understand that we cannot meet every need instantly, but we should still try our best and not reject others' requests out of comfort or busyness.
christianity_luke_11_7.context: The speaker represents a person who is already occupied and cannot immediately attend to the friend's request. The friend is left waiting.

christianity_luke_11_12.meaning: That God is good and will not give us evil things when we ask for good things. It emphasizes the idea of trusting in God's wisdom and care.
christianity_luke_11_12.context: This verse is from the Christian Gospel of Luke, chapter 11, verse 12. It is a parable told by Jesus to illustrate that a generous father would not give his child something harmful in response to a reasonable request.

christianity_luke_11_14.meaning: Jesus' power over demons and his ability to heal. It demonstrates his divine nature and the astonishment of the people who witnessed the miracle.
christianity_luke_11_14.context: This verse is from the Christian Gospel of Luke, chapter 11, verse 14. It describes an event where Jesus casts out a demon from a mute man and the man speaks after the demon leaves.

christianity_luke_11_15.meaning: This verse shows the opposition Jesus faced from some people who did not believe in his divine authority. It emphasizes the importance of faith and understanding the true nature of Jesus as the Son of God.
christianity_luke_11_15.context: This verse is from the Christian Gospel of Luke, chapter 11, verse 15. It mentions that some people accused Jesus of casting out demons using Satan's power, Beelzebul, the prince of demons.

christianity_luke_11_16.meaning: The importance of faith and trust in Jesus rather than seeking miracles. It teaches that true faith comes from understanding and following Jesus' teachings, not just demanding miracles.
christianity_luke_11_16.context: This verse is from the Christian Gospel of Luke, chapter 11, verse 16. It describes people who questioned Jesus for signs instead of believing in his teachings.

christianity_luke_11_8.meaning: Us that persistence pays off. Even if someone initially refuses to help or give something, if we keep asking, seeking, or knocking, we will eventually receive what we need.
christianity_luke_11_8.context: This verse is from the Christian Bible, specifically in the Gospel of Luke by Luke the Evangelist. It tells a story about a man who goes to his friend for help but the friend doesn't want to give him what he needs. However, because of the man's persistence, the friend eventually gives him what he requires.

christianity_luke_11_9.meaning: The importance of perseverance in seeking what we need. Just like in verse 11, if we keep asking, searching, and knocking, we will obtain what we desire.
christianity_luke_11_9.context: This verse is also from the Gospel of Luke in the Christian Bible. It is a continuation of the previous verse and emphasizes the importance of asking, seeking, and knocking for what we need.

christianity_luke_11_10.meaning: This verse reinforces the idea of persistence. Just like in verses 11 and 12, if we keep asking, searching, and knocking, we will receive what we need.
christianity_luke_11_10.context: This verse is also from the Gospel of Luke in the Christian Bible. It is another version of the same message as verses 11 and 12, emphasizing the idea of persistence.

christianity_luke_11_11.meaning: Us that parents and others should fulfill our reasonable requests, just as the man in the story didn't give the persistent man a harmful stone instead of bread.
christianity_luke_11_11.context: This verse is from the Gospel of Luke in the Christian Bible. It compares a person's persistence to a father who would not give his child a harmful object instead of what is needed.

christianity_luke_11_21.meaning: When a person is fully protected by good spirit, their life stays safe and stable.
christianity_luke_11_21.context: Jesus uses a picture of a strong guard protecting his home to explain spiritual power.

christianity_luke_11_22.meaning: A greater evil force can defeat a lesser one and take away its power completely.
christianity_luke_11_22.context: A stronger attacker beats the guard and steals all the valuable items from the house.

christianity_luke_11_23.meaning: You must fully support good. If you do not help, you are actually helping the enemy.
christianity_luke_11_23.context: Jesus states a clear rule about choosing sides in the spiritual battle between good and evil.

christianity_luke_11_24.meaning: If you do not fill your life with good things, bad habits will come back to you.
christianity_luke_11_24.context: A bad spirit leaves a person but wanders around looking for a new place to live.

christianity_luke_11_25.meaning: Just cleaning up outside is not enough. You must fill your heart with good things to stay safe.
christianity_luke_11_25.context: Jesus tells a story about a clean house that looks ready for a bad spirit to return.

christianity_luke_11_26.meaning: If you leave your heart empty, worse problems will come back. You need to stay full of good.
christianity_luke_11_26.context: The bad spirit brings back seven worse friends to live in the empty and clean house again.

christianity_luke_11_27.meaning: People often think being close to great people makes you special. She praised his mother for that.
christianity_luke_11_27.context: A woman in the crowd shouts that Jesus mother is lucky because she gave birth to him.

christianity_luke_11_28.meaning: Real blessing comes from listening to God and doing what he says, not just from family ties.
christianity_luke_11_28.context: Jesus gently corrects the woman and points to a different way to be truly blessed and happy.

christianity_luke_11_17.meaning: When people fight each other inside a group, that group will fail and fall apart. Unity is essential for any community to survive and succeed.
christianity_luke_11_17.context: Jesus knew the teachers were thinking bad thoughts about him. He used a simple analogy about divided kingdoms to show their error.

christianity_luke_11_18.meaning: An enemy cannot destroy itself from within. If the forces of evil were fighting each other, their power would collapse quickly and completely.
christianity_luke_11_18.context: The critics claimed Jesus used evil power to heal. Jesus pointed out that if evil fights itself, it cannot possibly stay strong or last.

christianity_luke_11_19.meaning: If your own people do similar things, you cannot judge me unfairly. You must be consistent and honest in your judgments of others.
christianity_luke_11_19.context: Jesus challenged the critics by asking who gives power to their own followers. He showed that their logic was completely flawed and unfair.

christianity_luke_11_20.meaning: True power comes from God, not evil. When you see good works, recognize that God is actively working in the world around you today.
christianity_luke_11_20.context: Jesus declared that his power comes from God alone. He explained that his miracles prove the divine kingdom is present among them now.

christianity_luke_11_29.meaning: Jesus calls this generation unbelieving and disbelieving in miracles. He compares it to the people of Nineveh who repented through Jonah's preaching.
christianity_luke_11_29.context: Jesus was speaking to a large crowd when He said this generation is unbelieving and seeks for miraculous signs. He cited the example of Jonah and the prophet as a sign.

christianity_luke_11_30.meaning: Jesus compares the Son of Man's resurrection to Jonah's, emphasizing the importance of faith and repentance.
christianity_luke_11_30.context: Jesus compares the resurrection of the Son of Man to Jonah's resurrection after being in the belly of the whale.

christianity_luke_11_31.meaning: Jesus compares this generation to the Queen of Sheba, who traveled far to learn from Solomon. He urges them to learn from the repentance of Nineveh and Jonah's message.
christianity_luke_11_31.context: The Queen of Sheba heard about Solomon's wisdom and traveled long distances to learn from him. Jesus compares this generation to her, stating they should learn from the repentance of Nineveh and Jonah's message.

christianity_luke_11_32.meaning: Jesus compares the Nineveh's repentance to the present generation's need to repent like them, emphasizing the importance of repentance.
christianity_luke_11_32.context: The people of Nineveh repented when Jonah preached to them, and Jesus compares this to the present generation's need for repentance.

christianity_luke_11_33.meaning: The verse teaches us to share our good qualities, knowledge, and blessings openly, as putting them in hiding prevents others from benefiting. It encourages us to let our positive traits shine brightly for the good of all.
christianity_luke_11_33.context: This verse is from the Christian Bible, specifically in the Gospel of Luke by Luke the Evangelist. It talks about a lamp being placed in a visible place so that those around can see the light it gives.

christianity_luke_11_34.meaning: The importance of our senses and how they influence our lives. A healthy mind and good senses lead to a well-guided life, while poor senses can lead to confusion and darkness.
christianity_luke_11_34.context: This verse is from the same Gospel of Luke, discussing the connection between the health of our eyes and the overall well-being of our body. It refers to the eye as the source of understanding and guidance.

christianity_luke_11_35.meaning: The verse urges us to examine our inner selves and ensure that we are not hiding any darkness or evil within. It encourages self-reflection and introspection.
christianity_luke_11_35.context: This verse is also from the Gospel of Luke, where Jesus is teaching about the inner light within a person.

christianity_luke_11_36.meaning: The verse emphasizes the significance of being open, honest, and having no secrets or negative aspects within us. It encourages us to be whole and transparent in our lives.
christianity_luke_11_36.context: This verse is from the same Gospel of Luke, discussing the importance of being whole and having no hidden darkness in our lives.

christianity_luke_11_37.meaning: Be open to socializing with people of different backgrounds, as Jesus accepted the Pharisee's invitation despite their differing beliefs. It shows humility and unity.
christianity_luke_11_37.context: This verse describes a situation where Jesus is invited to a Pharisee's house for dinner. Jesus accepts the invitation and sits down to eat.

christianity_luke_11_38.meaning: Pay attention to both spiritual and physical cleanliness, as the Pharisee recognized the importance of ritual washing. It teaches us to consider both inner and outer cleanliness.
christianity_luke_11_38.context: The Pharisee is surprised that Jesus didn't first wash his hands and feet before dining, following Jewish rituals.

christianity_luke_11_39.meaning: Focus on inner purity and addressing moral flaws, rather than just observing external customs. It emphasizes the importance of inner character.
christianity_luke_11_39.context: Jesus addresses the Pharisee, criticizing their hypocrisy for focusing on external rituals while ignoring internal moral issues.

christianity_luke_11_40.meaning: Understand that a person's inner and outer qualities are equally important. It highlights the balance between spiritual and physical aspects of life.
christianity_luke_11_40.context: Jesus rebukes the Pharisee for not understanding that God created both the outer and inner aspects of a person.

christianity_luke_11_49.meaning: God sends helpers to guide us, but we must listen and accept their message instead of hurting those who try to help.
christianity_luke_11_49.context: Jesus speaks about God sending messengers to people who often reject them and cause them great harm and suffering.

christianity_luke_11_50.meaning: We are accountable for how we treat truth and those who share it, so we must choose kindness and acceptance.
christianity_luke_11_50.context: Jesus explains that the current leaders are responsible for the harm done to holy messengers throughout all of history.

christianity_luke_11_51.meaning: Ignoring spiritual truth leads to serious trouble, so we should pay attention to God's message and live with respect.
christianity_luke_11_51.context: Jesus lists the first and last martyrs to show that rejecting God's word has serious consequences for everyone.

christianity_luke_11_52.meaning: Do not block others from finding truth or learning, because sharing knowledge helps everyone grow and understand life better.
christianity_luke_11_52.context: Jesus criticizes religious experts for hiding the truth and stopping others from learning about God's love and ways.

christianity_luke_11_41.meaning: The verse teaches us to help those in need with the resources we possess. By doing so, our hearts become pure and clean.
christianity_luke_11_41.context: This verse is from the Christian Gospel of Luke (11:41), where Jesus Christ addresses the importance of giving to the poor and needy with what we have. It is said in the context of discussing spiritual purity.

christianity_luke_11_42.meaning: The verse highlights the importance of prioritizing essential values like justice and love over trivial matters like religious practices.
christianity_luke_11_42.context: This verse is also from the Gospel of Luke (11:42), where Jesus criticizes the Pharisees for focusing on small matters like tithing while neglecting the bigger ones like showing love and justice.

christianity_luke_11_43.meaning: The verse warns against seeking praise and recognition from others instead of focusing on inner goodness and compassion.
christianity_luke_11_43.context: This verse is from the Gospel of Luke (11:43), where Jesus denounces the Pharisees for seeking recognition and prestige in public places.

christianity_luke_11_44.meaning: The verse cautions against pretending to be righteous while having hidden evil within, as it leads to spiritual death.
christianity_luke_11_44.context: This verse is from the Gospel of Luke (11:44), where Jesus compares Pharisees to hidden graves, emphasizing the danger of hypocrisy.

christianity_luke_11_45.meaning: The importance of considering others' feelings when speaking. The lawyer felt insulted because Jesus' words seemed to criticize him and his fellow lawyers. It emphasizes the need to be mindful of how our words impact others.
christianity_luke_11_45.context: This verse is from the Christian Bible, specifically in the book of Luke (11:45). It narrates a conversation between Jesus and a lawyer. Jesus is teaching, and a lawyer questions Him about His statement. The lawyer feels insulted by Jesus' words.

christianity_luke_11_46.meaning: The hypocrisy and selfishness of religious leaders. Jesus accuses the lawyers of creating difficult rules for others to follow while not helping them. It teaches us the importance of practicing what we preach and being compassionate towards others.
christianity_luke_11_46.context: In Luke 11:46 (Christianity), Jesus continues His conversation with the lawyer. He addresses the religious leaders, known as lawyers, and accuses them of making burdensome laws for others to follow, while not being willing to help carry those burdens themselves.

christianity_luke_11_47.meaning: The responsibility of past generations on present ones. Jesus accuses the leaders of not only continuing the traditions of their ancestors but also taking part in their actions. It teaches us the importance of acknowledging and learning from the mistakes of our ancestors.
christianity_luke_11_47.context: Luke 11:47 (Christianity) describes a situation where Jesus addresses the religious leaders. He criticizes them for not only building tombs for the prophets who were killed but also for continuing their fathers' actions.

christianity_luke_11_48.meaning: This verse criticizes the religious leaders for not standing up for the oppressed and practicing what they preach. It teaches us the importance of living according to our beliefs and being compassionate towards those in need.
christianity_luke_11_48.context: In Luke 11:49 (Christianity), Jesus continues His conversation with the religious leaders. He addresses their hypocrisy and lack of action towards the oppressed.

christianity_luke_12_3.meaning: The importance of considering the consequences of our actions and words, as everything we say or do will eventually be known. It encourages honesty, integrity, and humility.
christianity_luke_12_3.context: This verse is from the Bible, specifically in the Gospel of Luke chapter 12, verse 3. It is part of Jesus Christ's teachings and addresses His followers about how their words spoken in secret or private will be revealed in public.

christianity_luke_12_6.meaning: Us that God values every living being, no matter how small or insignificant they may seem. It reminds us to have faith in God's care for all creatures and to respect all life.
christianity_luke_12_6.context: This verse is also from the Gospel of Luke in the Bible, chapter 12, verse 6. It is part of Jesus Christ's teachings and talks about the value of even insignificant things like sparrows.

christianity_luke_12_7.meaning: This verse encourages trust in God's knowledge and care for us, no matter how insignificant our worries may seem. It teaches us to have peace and confidence in God's guidance.
christianity_luke_12_7.context: This verse is from the same source as v2, Luke 12:7 in the Bible. It is part of Jesus Christ's teachings and talks about the importance of not being afraid because even the tiniest details of our lives are known by God.

christianity_luke_12_8.meaning: The importance of openly acknowledging Jesus and sharing our faith with others. It encourages us to be bold in our beliefs and not hide them.
christianity_luke_12_8.context: This verse is from the Gospel of Luke in the Bible, chapter 12, verse 8. It is part of Jesus Christ's teachings and talks about the consequences of confessing Jesus before others.

christianity_luke_12_9.meaning: This verse means that those who reject or deny Jesus Christ in front of others will face rejection from God's angels when they stand before Him. It emphasizes the importance of acknowledging and accepting Jesus as a crucial aspect of one's faith.
christianity_luke_12_9.context: This verse is from the Christian Bible, specifically in the Gospel of Luke (12:9). It is part of a larger teaching by Jesus Christ addressing His followers about the consequences of denying Him in front of others.
